Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 1:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Kaf, Ha, Ya, 'Ayn, Sad﴾ (1)

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the interpretation of His saying, dhikruhu ta'ala (exalted is His mention): the kaf in ﴿Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad﴾. Some of them said: its interpretation is that it is a letter of His name, which is Kabir (the Great), by which He is indicated, and by mentioning it He dispenses with mentioning the rest of the name.

Mention of those who said this:

• Abu Husayn Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to me, saying: Abthar narrated to us, saying: Husayn narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Rashid, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding this verse ﴿Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad﴾, he said: "Kabir" — meaning by Kabir: the kaf in ﴿Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad﴾.

• Hannad ibn al-Sarri narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Husayn, from Isma'il ibn Rashid, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, the like of it.

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: Husayn informed us, from Isma'il ibn Rashid, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he used to say regarding ﴿Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad﴾: "Kaf: kabir."

• Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Ibn Idris informed us, from Husayn, from Isma'il ibn Rashid, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad﴾, he said: "Kaf: kabir."

• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Husayn, from Isma'il, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it.

And others said: rather, the kaf in it is a letter of His name which is Kafin (the Sufficient).

Mention of those who said this:

• Yahya ibn Talha al-Yarbu'i narrated to me, saying: Shurayk informed us, from Salim, from Sa'id, regarding His saying ﴿Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad﴾, he said: "Kaf: kafin."

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, saying: Abu Rawq informed us, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, regarding His saying ﴿Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad﴾, he said: "Kaf: kafin."

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Anbasa, from al-Kalbi, the like of it.

And others said: rather, it is a letter of His name which is Karim (the Generous).

Mention of those who said this:

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Amr, from Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, ﴿Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad﴾, he said: "Kaf of Karim."

Those who interpreted it in this manner said regarding the Ha in ﴿Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad﴾: it is a letter of His name which is Hadi (the Guide).

Mention of those who said this:

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: Abu Husayn informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: he used to say regarding the Ha in ﴿Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad﴾: Hadi.

• Abu Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abthar narrated to us, saying: Husayn narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Rashid, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it.

• Hannad narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Husayn, from Isma'il, from Sa'id, the like of it.

• Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Husayn, from Isma'il ibn Rashid, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, the like of it.

• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Husayn, from Isma'il, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it.

• Yahya ibn Talha narrated to me, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, saying: Abu Rawq informed us, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, regarding His saying ﴿Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad﴾, he said: "Ha: Hadi."

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, saying: Anbasa narrated to us, from al-Kalbi, the like of it.

They differed regarding the interpretation of the Ya in it. Some of them said: it is a letter of His name which is Yamin (the Right Hand).

Mention of those who said this:

• Abu Husayn narrated to me, saying: Abthar narrated to us, saying: Husayn narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Rashid, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Ya" in ﴿Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad﴾ is Ya of Yamin.

• Abu Husayn narrated to me, saying: Abthar narrated to us, saying: Husayn narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Rashid, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Ya" in ﴿Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad﴾ is Ya of Yamin.

Mention of those who said this:

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: Husayn informed us, from Isma'il ibn Rashid, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it.

• Hannad narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Husayn, from Isma'il ibn Rashid, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, the like of it.

• Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Husayn, from Isma'il ibn Rashid, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: Ya: Yamin.

And others said: rather, it is a letter of His name which is Hakim (the Wise).

Mention of those who said this:

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Amr, from Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, ﴿Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad﴾, he said: "Ya: of Hakim."

And others said: rather, they are letters from the saying of the speaker: "Ya man yujir" (O You who grants protection).

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Anbasa, from al-Kalbi, the like of it.

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: Husayn informed us, from Isma'il ibn Rashid, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it.

• Amr narrated to us, saying: Marwan ibn Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-'Ala' ibn al-Musayyib ibn Rafi', from his father, regarding His saying ﴿Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad﴾, he said: "'Ayn: of 'Alim."

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Amr, from Ata', from Sa'id, ﴿Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad﴾, he said: "Sad: Sadiq."

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, saying: Anbasa narrated to us, from al-Kalbi, he said: "Sadiq."

Mention of those who said this:

• Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Khidash narrated to me, saying: Salim ibn Qutayba narrated to me, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, from 'Atika, from Fatima bint 'Ali, who said: 'Ali used to say: "Ya Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad, forgive me."

• 'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad﴾, he said: "It is an oath which Allah swore by, and it is one of the names of Allah."

And others said: each letter of it is a name of the names of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.

Mention of those who said this:

• Matar ibn Muhammad al-Dabbi narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muslim al-Qasmali, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliya, who said: "There is no letter in ﴿Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad﴾ except that it is a name."

And others said: this word is one of the names of the Qur'an.

Mention of those who said this:

• al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad﴾, he said: "It is one of the names of the Qur'an."

Abu Ja'far said: The view we hold regarding this is parallel to the view regarding ﴿Alif Lam Mim﴾ and the rest of the disjointed letters (fawatih) at the openings of the surahs of the Qur'an, which begin with letters of the alphabet (huruf al-mu'jam). We have already mentioned that earlier, so it suffices us from repeating it in this place.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verses 2–4:

Discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿This is a mention of the mercy of your Lord to His servant Zakariyya﴾ [2] ﴿when he called upon his Lord in a secret call﴾ [3] ﴿He said, "My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened and my head has glistened with grey hair, and I have never been unblessed in my supplication to You, my Lord"﴾ [4]

The scholars of Arabic grammar (ahl al-'arabiyya) differed over what raises the word "dhikr" (mention) and what puts the word "'abd" (servant) in the accusative. Some grammarians of Basra said that the meaning is as if He said: "Among what We relate to you is the mention of the mercy of your Lord to His servant," and "'abd" is in the accusative by "al-rahma" (mercy), just as you say: "dhikr darb Zayd 'Amran" (the mention of Zayd's striking 'Amr). Some grammarians of Kufa said: I put "dhikr" in the nominative by "Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad" (the disjoined letters), and if you wish, you may supply "this is the mention of the mercy of your Lord," and he said: the meaning is "your Lord mentioned His servant with His mercy," with an inversion of order.

Abu Ja'far said: The view that is correct in my opinion regarding this is that it is said: "dhikr" is in the nominative by an omitted hidden subject, which is "this," as was done in other surahs, like the saying of God: ﴿A declaration of immunity from God and His Messenger﴾ and His saying: ﴿A surah which We have sent down﴾ and similar to that. "'Abd" is in the accusative by "al-rahma," and "Zakariyya" is in the accusative position, because it is an explanation of "'abd." So the meaning of the speech is: "This is the mention of the mercy of your Lord to His servant Zakariyya."

* *

As for His words: ﴿when he called upon his Lord in a secret call﴾

It says: when he called upon his Lord and asked Him with a hidden call, meaning: while he was concealing his supplication and his request of what he asked, out of his aversion to showing off.

As related:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿when he called upon his Lord in a secret call﴾, i.e., secretly, and indeed God knows the pure heart and hears the faint voice.

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His words ﴿when he called upon his Lord in a secret call﴾, he said: He did not intend showing off.

⁕ Musa ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Zakariyya desired offspring, so he stood and prayed, then called upon his Lord secretly, saying: ﴿My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened...﴾ to ﴿and make him, my Lord, pleasing﴾. And His words: ﴿He said, "My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened"﴾ — He, exalted is His remembrance, says: his hidden call with which he called upon his Lord was that he said: ﴿My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened﴾, meaning by His words ﴿weakened﴾: became feeble and soft from old age.

As related:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿He said, "My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened"﴾, i.e., the bone within me became feeble.

⁕ al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿and my bones have weakened﴾, he said: the bone became emaciated. 'Abd al-Razzaq said, al-Thawri said: It reached me that Zakariyya was seventy years old.

The scholars of Arabic grammar differed over the reason for the accusative in "shayb" (grey hair). Some grammarians of Basra said: it is in the accusative as a verbal noun (masdar) from the meaning of the speech, as if when he said "ishta'ala" (has glistened), he said "shaab" (has grown grey), and then said "shaybā" as a verbal noun. He said: and it is not in the sense of "tafaqa'tu shahman" (I burst with fat) and "imtala'tu ma'an" (I was filled with water), because that is not a verbal noun. Another said: "shayb" is in the accusative as an explanation (tafsir), because it is said: "ishta'ala shayb ra'si" (the grey hair of my head glistened), and "ishta'ala ra'si shaybā" (my head glistened with grey hair), just as it is said: "tafaqa'tu shahman" and "tafaqa'a shahmi" (my fat burst).

* *

As for His words: ﴿and I have never been unblessed in my supplication to You, my Lord﴾

It says: I have not been made wretched, O my Lord, by Your supplication, because You did not disappoint my supplication before, when I was calling upon You in my need of You; rather, You would answer and fulfil my need before I asked.

As related:

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His words: ﴿and I have never been unblessed in my supplication to You, my Lord﴾, he says: You had already made me know answering in the past.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿He said, "My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened"﴾, i.e., the bone within me became feeble.

⁕ al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿and my bones have weakened﴾, he said: the bone became emaciated. 'Abd al-Razzaq said, al-Thawri said: It reached me that Zakariyya was seventy years old.

The scholars of Arabic grammar differed over the reason for the accusative in "shayb" (grey hair). Some grammarians of Basra said: it is in the accusative as a verbal noun (masdar) from the meaning of the speech, as if when he said "ishta'ala" (has glistened), he said "shaab" (has grown grey), and then said "shaybā" as a verbal noun. He said: and it is not in the sense of "tafaqa'tu shahman" (I burst with fat) and "imtala'tu ma'an" (I was filled with water), because that is not a verbal noun. Another said: "shayb" is in the accusative as an explanation (tafsir), because it is said: "ishta'ala shayb ra'si" (the grey hair of my head glistened), and "ishta'ala ra'si shaybā" (my head glistened with grey hair), just as it is said: "tafaqa'tu shahman" and "tafaqa'a shahmi" (my fat burst).

* *

As for His words: ﴿and I have never been unblessed in my supplication to You, my Lord﴾

It says: I have not been made wretched, O my Lord, by Your supplication, because You did not disappoint my supplication before, when I was calling upon You in my need of You; rather, You would answer and fulfil my need before I asked.

As related:

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His words: ﴿and I have never been unblessed in my supplication to You, my Lord﴾, he says: You had already made me know answering in the past.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 5–6:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And indeed I fear the mawali (heirs/kinsmen) after me, and my wife is barren, so grant me from Yourself an heir, who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Ya'qub; and make him, my Lord, pleasing﴾.

He says: "And indeed I fear my paternal cousins and my agnates (ʿaṣabah) after me," i.e., after my death, that they will inherit me. It has also been said that by His saying ﴿min warā'ī﴾ ("after me") is meant "in front of me and before me"; and I have already explained the permissibility of that earlier.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation) said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

• Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, who said: my father narrated to me, who said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, who said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿And indeed I fear the mawali after me﴾: he means by the mawali: the kalalah, the heirs, that they would inherit him; so God granted him Yahya.

• Yahya ibn Dawud al-Wasiti narrated to us, who said: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying ﴿And indeed I fear the mawali after me﴾, he said: the ʿaṣabah.

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, who said: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying ﴿And indeed I fear the mawali after me﴾, he said: he feared the mawali of the kalalah.

• Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid informed us, from Abu Salih, with the like of it.

• Ya'qub narrated to me, who said: Hushaym narrated to us, who said: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid informed us, from Abu Salih, ﴿And indeed I fear the mawali after me﴾, he said: he means the kalalah.

• Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, who said: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, who said: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, who said: al-Hasan narrated to us, who said: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God ﴿I fear the mawali after me﴾, he said: the ʿaṣabah.

• al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

• al-Hasan narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And indeed I fear the mawali after me﴾, he said: the ʿaṣabah.

• Musa narrated to me, who said: ʿAmr narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, ﴿And indeed I fear the mawali after me﴾, and the mawali: they are the ʿaṣabah. The mawali is the plural of mawla, and the mawla and the wali are one in the speech of the Arabs. The readers of the major cities recited ﴿And indeed I fear the mawali﴾ with the meaning of fear which is the fear of [losing] security. It is narrated from ʿUthman ibn ʿAffan that he recited it: ﴿wa-innī khaffat al-mawālī﴾ with the fa' doubled and the kha' vowelled with fatha, from lightness (khiffah), as if he understood the meaning of the speech to be: "my agnates have gone, and those who would inherit me from my paternal cousins have departed." When it is recited thus, the ya' of al-mawali is a sukun (unvowelled), not moving, because it is in the position of raf' (nominative) after khaffat.

* *

His saying ﴿And my wife is barren﴾

He says: my wife does not bear children. It is said from this: a man ʿaqir and a woman ʿaqir with one form, as the poet said:

"Wretched is the youth if I am one-eyed, barren, / cowardly, so what is my excuse before every gathering?" [[The verse is in the Diwan of ʿAmir ibn al-Tufayl, Leiden edition 1913. The reading there is "fa-biʾsa" in place of "la-biʾsa". In Lisan: the ʿaqir is she who does not bear; a man ʿaqir: one to whom no child is born; women ʿiqr, with the ʿayn vowelled and the qaf doubled and fatha. The author cited it for the meaning of ʿaqir in Surah Al ʿImran (3:257) and repeated it here, and the place of citation in both is one.]]

* *

His saying ﴿So grant me from Yourself a wali﴾

He says: so provide me from Your presence with a son who is an heir and a helper.

* *

His saying: ﴿who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Ya'qub﴾

He says: he will inherit my wealth after my death, and he will inherit from the family of Ya'qub prophethood, because Zakariyya was a descendant of Ya'qub.

Ahl al-ta'wil said things similar to what we have said.

• Mujahid narrated to us, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Isma'il informed us, from Abu Salih regarding His saying ﴿who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Ya'qub﴾, he said: he will inherit my wealth and inherit from the family of Ya'qub prophethood.

Qatadah said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God ﷺ, whenever he recited this verse and reached ﴿who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Ya'qub﴾, said: "May God have mercy on Zakariyya, what did he have to do with his heirs."

• al-Hasan narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "May God have mercy on Zakariyya, what did he have to do with his heirs, and may God have mercy on Lut, when he would take refuge in a mighty pillar."

• Musa narrated to me, who said: ʿAmr narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, (So grant me from Yourself a wali, who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Ya'qub), he said: he will inherit my prophethood and the prophethood of the family of Ya'qub.

The readers differed in the recitation of His saying: ﴿yarithunī wa-yarithu min āli Ya'qūb﴾. The majority of the readers of Madinah and Makkah and a group of the people of Kufa recited that:

﴿yarithunī wa-yarithu﴾ with both verbs in the raf' (nominative), meaning: grant me the one who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Ya'qub, taking "who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Ya'qub" as a relative clause (ṣilah) of the wali. The exposition of His words, exalted is He: ﴿O Zechariah, indeed We give you good news of a boy whose name is Yahya; We have not before made for him any namesake﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: So his Lord answered him, and said to him: O Zechariah, indeed We give you good news of Our gift to you of a boy whose name is Yahya.

Qatada used to say: God named him Yahya (Yahya) only because He gave him life (yuhyi) through faith.

Ḥaddathana Bishr, who said: Thana Yazid, who said: Thana Sa'id, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿O Zechariah, indeed We give you good news of a boy whose name is Yahya﴾: a servant whom God brought to life through faith.

* *

As for His words ﴿We have not before made for him any namesake﴾:

The interpreters differed in the interpretation of this. Some of them said its meaning is: no barren woman has ever borne one like him.

Those who said this:

Haddathani Ali, who said: Thana Abdullah, who said: Thani Mu'awiya, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words concerning Yahya ﴿We have not before made for him any namesake﴾: he says, barren women have never borne a child like him.

Others said: rather, its meaning is: We have not made for him before him any like.

Those who said this:

Haddathana Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, who said: Thana Abu al-Rabi', the two of them said: Thana Salim ibn Qutayba, who said: Akhbarana Shu'ba, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿We have not before made for him any namesake﴾, he said: a likeness.

Haddathani Muhammad ibn Amr, who said: Thana Abu Asim, who said: Thana Isa; and Haddathani al-Harith, who said: Thana al-Hasan, who said: Thana Warqa', all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿We have not before made for him any namesake﴾, he said: an equal.

Haddathana al-Qasim, who said: Thana al-Husayn, who said: Thani Hajjaj, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Others said: the meaning of that is that no one before him had been named with his name.

Those who said this:

Haddathana Bishr, who said: Thana Yazid, who said: Thana Sa'id, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿We have not before made for him any namesake﴾: no one before him was named with it.

Haddathana al-Hasan, who said: Akhbarana Abd al-Razzaq, who said: Akhbarana Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿We have not before made for him any namesake﴾, he said: no one before him was named Yahya.

Haddathana al-Qasim, who said: Thana al-Husayn, who said: Thani Hajjaj, from Ibn Jurayj, the like of it.

Haddathani Yunus, who said: Akhbarana Ibn Wahb, who said: Thana Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, regarding the saying of God ﴿We have not before made for him any namesake﴾, he said: no one before him was named with this name.

Haddathana Musa, who said: Thana Amr, who said: Thana Asbat, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿O Zechariah, indeed We give you good news of a boy whose name is Yahya; We have not before made for him any namesake﴾: no one before him was named Yahya.

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This view, namely the view of those who said that there was no one before Yahya who was named with his name, is closer to the correct interpretation of this verse. The meaning of the speech is: We have not made for the boy whom We grant you, whose name is Yahya, any previously named with his name; and "samiyy" is an adjective of the pattern fa'il, transferred from the sense of maf'ul (named).

The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted: ﴿He said, "My Lord, how can I have a boy when my wife is barren and I have reached extreme old age?"﴾

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: Zechariah said, when God gave him the good news of Yahya: ﴿My Lord, how can I have a boy?﴾ In what manner would that be for me, when my wife is barren and cannot conceive, and I have grown too weak from old age for intercourse with women—so that You would strengthen me for what I have become too weak to do, and make my wife fertile, for You are capable of that and of whatever You will? Or (does he ask) by my marrying a wife other than my barren wife? He sought to confirm from his Lord the matter of the manner in which the child would come to him, which God had given him good news of. It was not a denial on his part (ﷺ) of the reality of what God had promised him of a child, nor how that could be a denial that He would grant him the child He had given him good news of—he had himself begun by asking his Lord for that, saying ﴿So grant me from Yourself an heir who will inherit from me and inherit from the family of Ya'qub﴾, after saying ﴿Indeed my bones have weakened within me and my head has blazed with white hair﴾.

As-Suddi said concerning this:

Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr told us, saying: Asbat told us, from as-Suddi, who said: Gabriel called out to Zechariah, ﴿Indeed We give you good news of a boy whose name is Yahya; We have not made for him before this any namesake﴾. When he heard the call, Satan came to him and said: "O Zechariah, the voice you heard is not from God; it is from Satan, mocking you. If it were from God, He would have revealed it to you as He reveals other matters to you." So he doubted and said, ﴿How can I have a boy?﴾, meaning: from where would it come, ﴿when old age has overtaken me and my wife is barren﴾.

As for His words, ﴿and I have reached extreme old age﴾:

He means: I have become exceedingly old from age, so that I have become like the dried-out bones of a palm stalk. It is said of a dry stick: ʿawda ʿātin wa ʿāsin (ʿawd ʿātin wa ʿās), and ʿatā yaʿtū ʿatiyyan wa ʿutuwwan, and ʿasā yaʿsū ʿisiyyan wa ʿusuwwan. Anyone who has reached his limit in old age, corruption or disbelief is called ʿāt and ʿās.

The people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said. Those who said so:

Yaqub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: Husayn informed us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: I have known the entire Sunnah, except that I do not know whether the Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to recite aloud in the noon and afternoon prayers, nor do I know how he would recite this word: ﴿and I have reached extreme old age, ʿitiyyan﴾ or ﴿ʿisiyyan﴾.

Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿and I have reached extreme old age, ʿitiyyan﴾, he said: By ʿitiyy he means old age.

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim told us, saying: ʿIsa told us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿ʿitiyyan﴾, he said: the wasting away of the bone.

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Mamar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿from old age, ʿitiyyan﴾, he said: in years; and he was about seventy-some years old.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿and I have reached extreme old age, ʿitiyyan﴾: al-ʿItiyy is one who has grown old in a way that he cannot beget children, as he sees himself, and no child is born to him.

I was told by al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd ibn Sulayman told us, saying: I heard ad-Dahhak say, regarding His words ﴿and I have reached extreme old age, ʿitiyyan﴾: it is old age.

**The commentary on His words, the Exalted: ﴿He said, "So it is. Your Lord says, 'It is easy for Me, and I created you before, when you were nothing.'"﴾ (9) ﴿He said, "My Lord, appoint for me a sign." He said, "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three nights, while sound."﴾ (10)**

The Exalted says: God said to Zakariyya, answering him, ﴿He said, "So it is"﴾, meaning: the matter is just as you say, that your wife is barren and that you have reached the extreme of old age (al-'itiyy). But your Lord says: creating the boy I gave you good news of, the one you mentioned to Me, whose name is Yahya, is easy for Me. So this is from His words ﴿Your Lord says, "It is easy for Me"﴾, a metonymy (kinaya) for creation.

* *

As for His words ﴿and I created you before, when you were nothing﴾:

The Exalted says: the creation of what I promised to grant you, the boy you mentioned to Me despite your old age and your wife's barrenness, is not more wondrous than My creating you. I created you and brought you into being as a complete human before My creating what I gave you good news of, that I would grant you a child. You were nothing. So likewise I will create for you the child I gave you good news of from your barren wife, despite your decrepitude, the weakness of your bones, and the whiteness that has spread over your head.

* *

As for His words: ﴿He said, "My Lord, appoint for me a sign."﴾

The Exalted says: Zakariyya said: My Lord, appoint for me a knowledge and a proof of what Your angels gave me good news of, concerning this boy, by Your command and Your message, so that my heart may be reassured by it.

As transmitted:

• Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿He said, "My Lord, appoint for me a sign"﴾: He said, "My Lord, appoint for me a sign that this is from You."

• Musa related to us, saying: 'Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "My Lord, if this voice is from You, then appoint for me a sign." ﴿He said﴾ God said, ﴿"Your sign"﴾ for that, ﴿"is that you will not speak to the people for three nights, while sound"﴾. He means, the Exalted: your sign for that, and your proof of it, is that you will not speak to the people for three nights while you are sound and healthy, with no illness of yours, such as muteness or sickness, preventing you from speaking.

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

• Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, from 'Amr, from 'Ata', from Sa'id, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning ﴿three nights, while sound﴾: He said: his tongue was bound without illness.

• 'Ali related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, His words ﴿three nights, while sound﴾: He said, without muteness.

• Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿three nights, while sound﴾: He said: no illness prevents you from speaking.

• al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, ﴿Not to speak to the people for three nights, while sound﴾: He said: healthy, with no illness preventing you from speaking.

• Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, ﴿He said, "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three nights, while sound"﴾: without affliction or muteness. He was only punished in this way because he asked for a sign after the angels had spoken to him directly; his tongue was seized so that speech did not flow from him except as gestures.

• al-Hasan related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, from 'Ikrima, concerning His words ﴿three nights, while sound﴾: sound, without muteness.

• Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿He said, "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three nights"﴾ "while you are healthy": he said: his tongue was held back, so he could not speak to anyone, yet he would glorify God, and read the Torah and read the Gospel. When he wanted to speak to people, he could not speak to them.

• Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salama related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from one whom he did not suspect, from Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani, who said: God seized his tongue without any harm, so he could not bear speech; his speech to his people was only by signs, until the three days God had made a sign had passed, as confirmation of what He had promised him of the gift of a son.

• Musa related to us, saying: 'Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, ﴿He said, "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three nights, while sound"﴾: without muteness, except by gesture; so his tongue was bound for three days and three nights.

Others said: "sound" (sawiyyan) describes the nights, and the meaning of the speech is: He said, "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three consecutive nights."

Those who said this:

• Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿He said, "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three nights, while sound"﴾: He said: three consecutive nights.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 11:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So he came out to his people from the prayer niche, and he signalled to them to glorify God morning and evening.﴾

He, may He be remembered, says: Zechariah came out to his people from his place of prayer, at the time his tongue was restrained from speaking to people, as a sign from God to him of the truth of His promise that He had made to him. Ibn Jurayj used to say, concerning the meaning of his coming out from his niche (mihrab):

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿he came out to his people from the niche﴾: He looked out over his people from the niche.

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: We have already explained the meaning of the mihrab earlier, in a way that makes repeating it in this place unnecessary.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿he came out to his people from the niche﴾: The mihrab is his place of prayer. And he recited: ﴿Then the angels called to him while he was standing in prayer in the niche﴾.

And His saying: ﴿Then he signalled to them﴾

He says: he gestured to them. That gesture may be by hand, by writing, or by other means by which what he intends is understood from him. The Arabs have two forms for this: waha and awha. Whoever says waha, in the imperfect says yahi; whoever says awha, says yuhi. Likewise awma and wama: whoever says wama, in the imperfect says yami; whoever says awma, says yumi.

The exegetes differed concerning the manner in which he signalled to his people. Some of them said: he signalled to them by a gesture of the hand.

Those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿he signalled﴾: Zechariah gestured.

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from one who is not accused of falsehood, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, ﴿then he signalled to them﴾: The wahy is the gesture.

⁕ Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, ﴿then he signalled to them﴾: He gestured to them.

Others said: the meaning of awha is: he wrote.

Those who said this:

⁕ Mahmud ibn Khidash narrated to us, saying: Abbad ibn al-Awwam narrated to us, from Sufyan ibn Husayn, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God, the Exalted, ﴿then he signalled to them to glorify [God] morning and evening﴾: He wrote for them on the ground.

⁕ Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from al-Thawri, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Hakam, ﴿then he signalled to them﴾: He wrote to them.

⁕ Musa narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, ﴿So he came out to his people from the niche﴾, then he wrote for them in a document ﴿to glorify [God] morning and evening﴾, and that is His saying ﴿then he signalled to them﴾.

Others said: the meaning of that is: he commanded them.

Those who said this:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿then he signalled to them to glorify [God] morning and evening﴾: I do not know whether it was a document he wrote for them or a gesture he made, and God knows best. He commanded them to glorify [God] morning and evening, while he did not speak to them.

* *

As for His saying ﴿to glorify [God] morning and evening﴾:

I have already explained earlier the ways in which tasbih (glorification of God, i.e. declaring Him free of imperfection) is used. In this place it is permissible that by it is meant the tasbih which is the remembrance of God, so that He commanded them to devote themselves to remembering God at the two ends of the day by glorifying Him; and it is permissible that by it is meant the prayer (salah), so that He commanded them to pray at these two times.

Qatada used to say, regarding His saying ﴿then he signalled to them to glorify [God] morning and evening﴾: He gestured to them to pray morning and evening.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 19, verses 12–13:

The explanation of the words of the Exalted: ﴿O Yahya, take the Book with determination. And We gave him judgment while yet a boy﴾ (12) ﴿and tenderness from Us and purity. And he was fearing of Allah﴾ (13)

The Exalted says: So a son was born to Zakariyya, Yahya. When he was born, Allah said to him: "O Yahya, take this Book with determination," meaning the Book of Allah which He sent down to Musa, which is the Torah, "with determination" — that is, with earnestness.

As related:

- Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿take the Book with determination﴾, he said: "with earnestness."

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿take the Book with determination﴾, he said: "with earnestness."

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Ibn Zayd said regarding this:

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿O Yahya, take the Book with determination﴾: "The determination (quwwah) is that he acts upon what Allah commanded him, and keeps away from what Allah forbade him."

Abu Ja'far said: I have already explained the meaning of this with its evidences earlier in this our book, in Surah Al 'Imran, so that suffices and there is no need to repeat it in this place.

* *

And His words ﴿and We gave him judgment while yet a boy﴾

The Exalted says: And We gave him understanding of the Book of Allah in his childhood, before he reached the age of men.

- Ahmad ibn Mani' narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar informed me, and did not mention it from anyone, regarding this verse ﴿and We gave him judgment while yet a boy﴾, he said: "It reached me that the boys said to Yahya: 'Come, let us play.' He said: 'I was not created for play.' So Allah sent down ﴿and We gave him judgment while yet a boy﴾."

* *

And His words ﴿and tenderness from Us﴾

The Exalted says: And mercy from Us and love for him, We gave him judgment while yet a boy.

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of al-Hanan (tenderness). Some of them said: its meaning is mercy, and they directed the statement toward the sense we have indicated.

Those who said that:

- 'Ali narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and tenderness from Us﴾, he said: "and mercy from Us."

- Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, regarding this verse ﴿and tenderness from Us﴾, he said: "mercy."

- al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿and tenderness from Us﴾, he said: "mercy from Us."

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, regarding His words ﴿and tenderness from Us﴾, he said: "mercy from Us, which none other than Us can bestow."

- I was told on the authority of al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿and tenderness from Us﴾: "mercy from Us, which none can bestow except Us."

Others said: rather, the meaning is: mercy from Us toward Zakariyya; We gave him judgment while yet a boy, and did with him what We did.

Those who said that:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿and tenderness from Us﴾, he said: "mercy from Us."

Others said: the meaning is: compassion from Us toward him, which is why We did that.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿and tenderness from Us﴾, he said: "compassion from his Lord toward him."

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Others said: rather, the meaning of al-hanan is love. They directed the meaning of the statement to: love from Us, and so We did that.

Those who said that:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from 'Anbasah, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from 'Ikrimah, regarding ﴿and tenderness from Us﴾, he said: "love for him."

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿and tenderness﴾, he said: "As for al-hanan, it is love."

Others said its meaning is exaltation from Us toward him.

Those who said that:

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Tumaylah narrated to us, from Abu Hamzah, from Jabir, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, regarding ﴿and tenderness from Us﴾, he said: "exaltation from Us." It is also reported from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: "I do not know what al-hanan is."

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Amr ibn Dinar informed me that he heard 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, say: "By Allah, I do not know what hanana is."

Among the Arabs, for hananaka there are two usages: "hananaka, O our Lord" and "hananayka"; as Tarafah ibn al-'Abd said regarding hananayk:

* *

His saying ﴿ʿasiyyan﴾ (disobedient)

It is on the pattern of faʿīl, meaning that he possesses disobedience, from the speaker's saying: "So-and-so disobeyed (ʿasā) his Lord, so he disobeys Him, ʿasiyyan."

* *

His saying ﴿And peace is upon him the day he was born, and the day he dies, and the day he is raised alive﴾

He says: a security from Allah on the day he was born, from Satan touching him with harm in the way he touches the children of Adam. This is because it has been narrated from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Every child of Adam comes on the Day of Resurrection carrying a sin, except Yahya ibn Zakariyya."

⁕ Ibn Humayd related this to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: Ibn al-'As told me that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say that.

⁕ al-Hasan related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿arrogant or disobedient﴾, he said: Ibn al-Musayyab used to mention, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no one who meets Allah on the Day of Resurrection except that he has a sin, except Yahya ibn Zakariyya."

He said: Qatadah said: He did not commit a sin, nor did he intend (to commit one) with a woman.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And mention in the Book Mary, when she withdrew from her family to a place facing east (16). And she took a screen apart from them; then We sent to her Our Spirit, and it appeared before her as a well-proportioned man (17).﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And mention, O Muhammad, in the Book of Allah which He sent down to you with truth, Mary, daughter of Imran, when she withdrew from her family and secluded herself from them. Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Salt narrated to us, saying: Abu Kudayna narrated to us, from Qabus, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿when she withdrew from her family to a place facing east﴾, he said: she went out to a place facing east.

Musa narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Mary went out to the side of the niche (al-mihrab) because of a menstruation that had befallen her, and this is His saying [[So here, and in two places after: fa-intabadhat; the recitation is: idh intabadhat.]] So she withdrew from her family to a place facing east: to the east of the niche.

* *

As for His saying ﴿to a place facing east﴾:

It means: she withdrew and separated herself from her family in a place toward the direction of the sunrise, not its sunset.

As related:

Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿to a place facing east﴾, he said: from the direction of the east.

Ishaq ibn Shahin narrated to me, saying: Khalid ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Dawud, from Amir, from Ibn Abbas, who said: I know better than any of Allah's creation why the Christians took the east as a qibla, because of Allah's saying: So she withdrew from her family to a place facing east; so they took the birth of Jesus as a qibla.

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Amir, from Ibn Abbas, the same.

Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Salt informed us, saying: Abu Kudayna narrated to us, from Qabus, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The People of the Book were commanded to pray toward the House and the Hajj was for Allah, and they were turned away from these only by the interpretation of your Lord ﴿when she withdrew from her family to a place facing east﴾; so they prayed before the rising of the sun.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah ﴿when she withdrew from her family to a place facing east﴾, he said: distant and remote.

It has been said: she was in a place adjacent to the rising of the sun, because what is adjacent to the east was regarded by them as better than what is adjacent to the west, and this is likewise mentioned among the Arabs.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and she took a screen apart from them﴾:

It means: she took a veil between herself and her family and people, something to conceal her from them and from people. It is mentioned from Ibn Abbas that she was in a place adjacent to the east because Allah shaded her with the sun and made for her from it a screen.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿withdrew from her family to a place facing east﴾, he said: a place the sun shaded so that none of them could see her.

Others said other than this:

Musa narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi ﴿and she took a screen apart from them﴾: from the walls.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Then We sent to her Our Spirit﴾:

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We sent to her, when she withdrew from her family to a place facing east and took a screen apart from them, Gabriel.

In agreement with what we have said on this, the people of interpretation have spoken.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 19, verses 18–19:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿She said: "I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing"﴾ (19:18) ﴿He said: "I am only a messenger of your Lord, to give you a pure boy"﴾ (19:19).

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: Mary feared Our messenger when he appeared to her in the form of a well-proportioned man, and she thought he was a man who wanted to have her against her will.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying, ﴿Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing﴾, he said: She feared that he wanted her for himself.

Musa narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿So He appeared to her as a well-proportioned man﴾: when she saw him she was frightened of him and said: ﴿Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing﴾. She said: "Indeed, I seek refuge, O man, in the Most Merciful from you," meaning: I seek protection with the Most Merciful from you, that you should obtain from me what He has forbidden to you, if you are one who has piety toward Him and avoids what He has prohibited and shuns His disobedience; for whoever is God-fearing toward Allah avoids that. And it would be a valid reading if it is understood that she meant: "I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you fear God in my seeking protection and refuge in Him from you."

As related:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from one whom he does not accuse of falsehood, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, regarding ﴿She said: "Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing"﴾, and she did not see him as anything other than a man among the children of Adam.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr narrated to us, from Asim, who said: Ibn Zayd said, mentioning the story of Mary: "She knew that the God-fearing person possesses restraint, when she said: ﴿Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing. He said: Indeed I am only a messenger of your Lord﴾." His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: Our spirit said to her: "Indeed I am only a messenger of your Lord, O Mary, sent by Him to you," ﴿to give you a pure boy﴾.

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of the Hijaz and Iraq, other than Abu Amr, recited ﴿li-ahaba laki﴾ (with alif, "that I may give you"), meaning: "I am only a messenger of your Lord": he says, "He sent me to you that I may give you a pure boy," read as a continuation of the speech (ḥikāyah). Abu Amr ibn al-Ala recited ﴿liyahaba laki ghulaman zakiyyan﴾ (with yā', "that He may give you"), meaning: "I am only a messenger of your Lord, who sent me to you so that God may give you a pure boy."

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The correct reading in this matter is what the regional reciters of the cities have agreed upon, namely ﴿li-ahaba laki﴾ with alif and not yā', because it is so in the codices of the Muslims, and the reading of their earlier and later generations is upon it, except Abu Amr; and it is not permissible to oppose them in what they have unanimously agreed upon, nor is it lawful for anyone to oppose their codices. And "a pure boy" (al-ghulam al-zakiyy) is one free from sins; and thus the Arabs say: "ghulam zakin" and "zakiyy," and "ʿal" and "ʿaliyy."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 20–23 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿She said, "How can I have a boy when no man has touched me and I have not been unchaste?" (20) He said, "Thus [it will be]. Your Lord says, 'It is easy for Me, and [We will do it] so that We may make him a sign for the people and a mercy from Us. And it is a matter [already] decreed.'"﴾ (21)

Exalted is His mention says: Maryam said to Jibril, ﴿"How can I have a boy?"﴾ In what manner will I have a boy? Will it be through a husband I marry, from whom I conceive, or will God originate His creation in me as a new beginning? ﴿"When no man has touched me"﴾ of the descendants of Adam through lawful marriage. ﴿"And I have not been unchaste"﴾ since no one among them has touched me in a lawful manner, ﴿"unchaste"﴾ meaning, "I have not committed unchastity and done that in an unlawful way, so that I would have conceived through fornication."

As related:
⁕ Musa narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿"And I have not been unchaste"﴾: he says, "a fornicator."

﴿"He said, 'Thus [it will be]. Your Lord says, "It is easy for Me."'"﴾ Exalted is His mention says: Jibril said to her, "The matter is just as you describe it, that no man has touched you and you were not unchaste. But your Lord said, 'It is easy for Me': that is, the creation of the boy that I said I would bestow upon you is easy for Me; its creation is not beyond Me, and I will bestow him upon you without a stallion who would mount you."

﴿"And so that We may make him a sign for the people"﴾ says: And so that We may make the boy whom We bestow upon you a sign and a proof regarding My creation, I bestow him upon you. ﴿"And a mercy from Us"﴾ says: and a mercy from Us to you and to whoever believes in him and affirms him; I will create him from you. ﴿"And it is a matter [already] decreed"﴾ says: and his creation from you was a matter decreed by God, which has passed in His judgment and in His foreknowledge that it would come to be from you.

As related:
⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Someone I do not suspect told me, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, regarding ﴿"And it is a matter [already] decreed"﴾: that is, God has resolved upon that, and there is no escape from it.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So she conceived him, and withdrew with him to a remote place. (22) Then the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree. She said, "Would that I had died before this and had become a thing forgotten and out of mind!"﴾ (23)

In this speech there is an omitted element whose mention has been dropped, being sufficiently indicated by what was mentioned of it: ﴿"Then We breathed into her of Our spirit"﴾ [and she conceived a boy], ﴿"So she conceived him and withdrew with him to a remote place"﴾. This is also the interpretation of the people of interpretation.

Those who said this:
⁕ Muhammad ibn Sahl narrated to me, saying: Ismaʿil ibn ʿAbd al-Karim narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Samad ibn Maʿqil, the nephew of Wahb ibn Munabbih, narrated to me, saying: I heard Wahb say: When God sent Jibril to Maryam, he appeared to her in the form of a well-proportioned man, and she said to him: ﴿"I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing."﴾ Then he breathed into the opening of her shift until the breath reached the womb, and she conceived.
⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from one I do not suspect, from Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani, who said: When he said that, that is, when Jibril said ﴿"Thus [it will be]. Your Lord says, 'It is easy for Me'"﴾ ... the verse, she submitted to the command of God, and he breathed into her opening, then departed from her.
⁕ Musa narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When Jibril said that to her, she cast her outer garment over herself, and Jibril took hold of its sleeves and breathed into the opening of her shift, which was split at the front, and the breath entered her chest, and she conceived. Then her sister, the wife of Zakariyya, visited her one night; when she opened the door for her, she embraced her, and the wife of Zakariyya said: "O Maryam, do you know that I am pregnant?" Maryam said: "Do you know that I too am pregnant?" The wife of Zakariyya said: "I found that what is in my womb prostrates to what is in your womb." That is His saying ﴿"confirming a word from God"﴾.
⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: They say that he breathed only into the opening of her shift and her sleeve.

* *

As for His saying ﴿"So she withdrew with him to a remote place"﴾:
It means: she secluded herself with the one she had conceived, who is ʿIsa, and withdrew with him from the people to a remote place, ﴿"a remote place"﴾ meaning a far-off place distant from the people. It is said: "He is in a qasiy place" and "qassiy" with the same meaning, as the rajaz poet said:
"You will surely sit in the seat of the distant one... from me, the foul-smelling, the hated one."[[The two verses are by Ru'ba ibn al-'Ajjaj, the rajaz poet (see Fawa'id al-Qala'id of al-'Ayni, pp. 115–116), and two further verses follow them...]]

It is said of it: qasa al-makan yaqsu qusuwwan, meaning: it became distant. And I made something distant (aqsaytu al-shay') when I removed it far away and delayed it.

The people of interpretation said likewise to what we have said.

Those who said this:
⁕ Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿"So she withdrew with him to a remote place"﴾: he said, "a far-off place."
⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿"a remote place"﴾: he said, "far-off."
⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.
⁕ Musa narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When the time of Maryam's delivery came, she went out to the side of the eastern prayer niche of the sanctuary and went to its farthest end.

* *

As for His saying ﴿"Then the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree"﴾:
Exalted is His mention says: the pains of childbirth brought her to the trunk of the palm tree. Then it was said: when the hamza was removed from it, [it became] ajaʾaha, as one says: "I brought you Zayd" (ataytuka bi-Zayd), and when the bi is dropped it is said "ataytuka Zayda," as His exalted saying: ﴿"Bring me blocks of iron"﴾ [ātūnī zubar al-ḥadīd], meaning: bring me with blocks of iron; but the alif was lengthened when the bi was dropped. Likewise they say: "I went out with him" and "I took him out," and "I went with him" and "I made him go." It is actually the causative form of "to come," as one says: "he came," and "I brought him" (ajaʾtuhu): that is, I brought him. And an Arab proverb: "Worst of what brought you to the marrow of Ur'ub" (shurra mā ajāʾanī ilā mukhkhat ʿurqūb), and "ashaʾa" is also said; it is said: "Worst of what brings you and drives you to that." From it is the saying of Zuhayr:

"And a neighbor who traveled, intending toward you, / fear and hope brought him (ajāʾathu al-makhāfatu wa'l-rajāʾ)."[[The verse is by Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma (Lisan: jay'a)...]]

That is: "he brought it," and "ajaʾahu ilaynā" and "ashaʾaka" is the dialect of Tamim, while "ajaʾaka" is the dialect of the people of al-ʿĀliya. Whoever interpreted it as "compelled her" (alja'aha) did so because when the labor pains came to her at the trunk of the palm, they had compelled her to it.

The people of interpretation said likewise to what we have said.

Those who said this:
⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿"the pains of childbirth"﴾: he said, "The pains compelled her."
⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: The pains compelled her. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn ʿAbbas said: The pains compelled her to the trunk of the palm tree.
⁕ Musa narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿"Then the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree"﴾: he says, "The pains compelled her to the trunk of the palm tree."
⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿"Then the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree"﴾: he said, "They forced her to the trunk of the palm tree."

They differed about the place where Maryam, with ʿIsa, withdrew and where the pains drove her to give birth. Some said: That was in the lowest land of Egypt and the farthest land of Syria, because she fled from her people when she became pregnant, heading toward Egypt, fleeing from them.

Those who said this:
⁕ Muhammad ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: Ismaʿil ibn ʿAbd al-Karim narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Samad ibn Maʿqil narrated to me, that he heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say: When Maryam was pregnant, she had with her a relative called Yusuf the Carpenter, and they were going to the mosque beside Mount Zion, which at that time was one of their greatest mosques. Maryam and Yusuf served in that mosque in that era, and service to it had great merit, so they were eager for it, and they would personally tend to its affairs: its whitewashing, sweeping, cleaning, and every task done in it. No one of their time was more diligent in worship than they. The first to notice Maryam's pregnancy was her companion Yusuf; when he saw what was upon her, he was appalled, it weighed heavily on him, and he was horrified by it, not knowing how to resolve her matter. When Yusuf wished to accuse her, he recalled her righteousness and innocence, and that she had never been absent from him for a single hour; and when he wished to exonerate her, he saw what had appeared on her. When this grew severe for him, he spoke to her. The first thing he said to her was: "A matter has arisen in my soul concerning you, which I feared; I was eager to suppress it and keep it hidden within myself, but it overcame me, and I saw that speaking of it would ease my heart." She said: "Then say a good word." He said: "I would say nothing but that. Tell me: does seed sprout without a sowing? " She said: "Yes." He said: "Does a tree grow without rain falling on it?" She said: "Yes." He said: "Can a child be born without a male?" She said: "Yes. Do you not know that God, blessed and exalted, caused the crop to grow on the day He created it without seed, and the seed on that day came into being from the crop that God had made grow without seed? Or do you not know that by His power God caused the tree to grow without rain, and that by that same power He made rain a life for the tree after each of them had been created separately? Or do you say that God cannot cause the tree to grow until He is assisted by water, and that without that He could not make it grow?" Yusuf said to her: "I do not say this; rather, I know that God, blessed and exalted, by His power over what He wills, says to it 'Be,' and it is." Maryam said: "Do you not know that God, blessed and exalted, created Adam and his wife without female or male?" He said: "Yes." When she said that to him, it came into his mind that what was in her was something from God, blessed and exalted, and that he could not ask her about it, because he saw how she kept it secret. Then Yusuf took over the service of the mosque and relieved her of every task she had been doing, because he saw the delicacy of her body, the yellowing of her complexion, the darkening of her face, the swelling of her belly, the weakness of her strength, and the fixed gaze of her eyes; and Maryam had not been like this before. When her time of childbirth drew near, God revealed to her: "Leave the land of your people, for if they overpower you they will reproach you and kill your child." That matter reached her sister, and her sister was then pregnant, and had been given good news of Yahya. When they met, the mother of Yahya found that what was in her womb had fallen prostrate to ʿIsa in submission. Yusuf carried her to the land of Egypt on a donkey of his, with nothing between her and the saddle when she mounted. Yusuf set out with her until, when they were near the borders of Egypt, at the edge of her people's lands, the pains of childbirth seized Maryam. He brought her to the stall of a donkey (ariyy himar, meaning the manger of the donkey) and the root of a palm tree, at a time I think was either cold or hot ("the doubt is from Abu Ja'far"). The pains grew severe for Maryam; when she felt their intensity, she clung to the palm tree and embraced it, and the angels surrounded her, standing in rows encircling her.

A different account has also been transmitted from Wahb ibn Munabbih, namely:
⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated it to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from one I do not suspect, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: When her delivery drew near, that is Maryam, and she experienced what a woman experiences of labor, she went out of the city westward from Iliya, until childbirth overtook her at a village of Iliya six miles away called Bethlehem; the pains of childbirth drove her to the root of a palm tree beneath which was a cattle manger and a stream of water, and she gave birth to him there.

Others said: Rather, when the time of her delivery of what was in her womb came, she went out to the side of the eastern prayer niche of the sanctuary and went to its farthest end, and the pains drove her to the trunk of a palm tree; this is the statement of al-Suddi, whose narration has been mentioned before.
⁕ Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'ida narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Al-Mughira ibn ʿUthman informed me, saying: I heard Ibn ʿAbbas say: It was nothing more than that she conceived and gave birth.
⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Al-Mughira ibn ʿUthman ibn ʿAbd Allah informed me that he heard Ibn ʿAbbas say: It was nothing more than that she conceived and bore.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿"Would that I had died before this"﴾:
It is mentioned that she said this in the state of labor, out of shame before the people.

As related:
⁕ Musa narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: She said, while in the pangs of labor, out of shame before the people: ﴿"Would that I had died before this and had become a thing forgotten and out of mind!"﴾ She means: "Would that I had died before this distress I am in, and before the grief of bearing a child without a husband. And would that I had been a 'nasy mansiyya': a thing that was forgotten and then left unsought, like menstrual rags which, once cast away, are neither sought nor remembered. Everything that is forgotten and abandoned and not sought is 'nasy'." The forms "nasy" and "nisy" (with fatha and kasra on the nun) are two well-known dialects of the Arabs with the same meaning, like "watr" and "witr," and "jasr" and "jisr." Whichever of them a reciter reads, it is correct in our view. Reading with kasra was the practice of most readers of the Hijaz, Medina, and Basra and some people of Kufa; reading with fatha was the practice of the people of Kufa. From it is the saying of the poet:

"As if for her in the earth there were a nasy she traces, / when she goes forth; and if she speaks to you, she is firm (tablat)."[[The verse is by al-Shanfara (Lisan: nasiya). It is said: al-nasy is the forgotten thing that is not remembered... Al-Farra said: al-nasy and al-nisy are two dialects, referring to rags a woman casts off from her menstrual blood, like watr and witr. He said: if he meant by nasy (with fatha) the verbal noun of forgetting, it would be correct.]]

By His saying "tuqussuhu" he means: she seeks it, because she had forgotten it until it was lost, then remembered it and sought it. By "tablat" he means: she is good and truthful.

If "nasy" is taken as a verbal noun of forgetting, it would be correct as well, since the Arabs, as is reported of them, say: "nasiytuhu nisyanan wa nasyan," just as some say "from obedience to the Lord and disobedience to Satan," meaning "and disobedience" (ʿisyan); and as you say "atayhu ityanan wa atyan," as the poet said:

"Its wickedness is well known among them, / and they see the doing of noble deeds as forbidden."[[In Lisan (atā): al-itiyan is coming... The author cites the verse to show that the Arabs say "nasiytuhu nisyanan wa nasyan" as they say "ataytuhu ityanan wa atyan." His word "ma'ruofa" is feminine because the subject, al-atī, is masculine, but it was made feminine by its annexation to al-fawahish, the plural of fahisha.]]

* *

As for His saying ﴿"mansiyyan"﴾:
It is the passive participle of "nasiytu al-shay'," as if she said: "Would that I had been the thing that is cast away, forgotten and abandoned."

Those who said likewise to what we have said among the people of interpretation:

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verses 20–23 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: ʿAtaʾ al-Khurasani informed me, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Would that I had died before this and had been a thing forgotten, utterly forgotten!﴾ "I had not been created, and I had not been anything."

⁕ Musa narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿and had been a thing forgotten, utterly forgotten﴾, he said: "Nisyan (a thing forgotten): my remembrance was forgotten. Mansiyyan (utterly forgotten): it is said, my trace was forgotten, so no trace or substance of mine is seen."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding ﴿and had been a thing forgotten, utterly forgotten﴾: "That is, a thing that is neither known nor mentioned."

⁕ al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding his saying ﴿and had been a thing forgotten, utterly forgotten﴾, he said: "I am not known, and it is not known who I am."

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Abu Jaʿfar, from al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas regarding ﴿nisyan mansiyyan﴾, he said: "It is the miscarriage (al-saqt)."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Would that I had died before this and had been a thing forgotten, utterly forgotten!﴾: "I had never been anything on the earth at all."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 20–23 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿She said, "How can I have a boy when no man has touched me and I have not been unchaste?" (20) He said, "Thus [it will be]. Your Lord says, 'It is easy for Me, and [We will do it] so that We may make him a sign for the people and a mercy from Us. And it is a matter [already] decreed.'"﴾ (21)

Exalted is His mention says: Maryam said to Jibril, ﴿"How can I have a boy?"﴾ In what manner will I have a boy? Will it be through a husband I marry, from whom I conceive, or will God originate His creation in me as a new beginning? ﴿"When no man has touched me"﴾ of the descendants of Adam through lawful marriage. ﴿"And I have not been unchaste"﴾ since no one among them has touched me in a lawful manner, ﴿"unchaste"﴾ meaning, "I have not committed unchastity and done that in an unlawful way, so that I would have conceived through fornication."

As related:
⁕ Musa narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿"And I have not been unchaste"﴾: he says, "a fornicator."

﴿"He said, 'Thus [it will be]. Your Lord says, "It is easy for Me."'"﴾ Exalted is His mention says: Jibril said to her, "The matter is just as you describe it, that no man has touched you and you were not unchaste. But your Lord said, 'It is easy for Me': that is, the creation of the boy that I said I would bestow upon you is easy for Me; its creation is not beyond Me, and I will bestow him upon you without a stallion who would mount you."

﴿"And so that We may make him a sign for the people"﴾ says: And so that We may make the boy whom We bestow upon you a sign and a proof regarding My creation, I bestow him upon you. ﴿"And a mercy from Us"﴾ says: and a mercy from Us to you and to whoever believes in him and affirms him; I will create him from you. ﴿"And it is a matter [already] decreed"﴾ says: and his creation from you was a matter decreed by God, which has passed in His judgment and in His foreknowledge that it would come to be from you.

As related:
⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Someone I do not suspect told me, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, regarding ﴿"And it is a matter [already] decreed"﴾: that is, God has resolved upon that, and there is no escape from it.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So she conceived him, and withdrew with him to a remote place. (22) Then the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree. She said, "Would that I had died before this and had become a thing forgotten and out of mind!"﴾ (23)

In this speech there is an omitted element whose mention has been dropped, being sufficiently indicated by what was mentioned of it: ﴿"Then We breathed into her of Our spirit"﴾ [and she conceived a boy], ﴿"So she conceived him and withdrew with him to a remote place"﴾. This is also the interpretation of the people of interpretation.

Those who said this:
⁕ Muhammad ibn Sahl narrated to me, saying: Ismaʿil ibn ʿAbd al-Karim narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Samad ibn Maʿqil, the nephew of Wahb ibn Munabbih, narrated to me, saying: I heard Wahb say: When God sent Jibril to Maryam, he appeared to her in the form of a well-proportioned man, and she said to him: ﴿"I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing."﴾ Then he breathed into the opening of her shift until the breath reached the womb, and she conceived.
⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from one I do not suspect, from Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani, who said: When he said that, that is, when Jibril said ﴿"Thus [it will be]. Your Lord says, 'It is easy for Me'"﴾ ... the verse, she submitted to the command of God, and he breathed into her opening, then departed from her.
⁕ Musa narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When Jibril said that to her, she cast her outer garment over herself, and Jibril took hold of its sleeves and breathed into the opening of her shift, which was split at the front, and the breath entered her chest, and she conceived. Then her sister, the wife of Zakariyya, visited her one night; when she opened the door for her, she embraced her, and the wife of Zakariyya said: "O Maryam, do you know that I am pregnant?" Maryam said: "Do you know that I too am pregnant?" The wife of Zakariyya said: "I found that what is in my womb prostrates to what is in your womb." That is His saying ﴿"confirming a word from God"﴾.
⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: They say that he breathed only into the opening of her shift and her sleeve.

* *

As for His saying ﴿"So she withdrew with him to a remote place"﴾:
It means: she secluded herself with the one she had conceived, who is ʿIsa, and withdrew with him from the people to a remote place, ﴿"a remote place"﴾ meaning a far-off place distant from the people. It is said: "He is in a qasiy place" and "qassiy" with the same meaning, as the rajaz poet said:
"You will surely sit in the seat of the distant one... from me, the foul-smelling, the hated one."[[The two verses are by Ru'ba ibn al-'Ajjaj, the rajaz poet (see Fawa'id al-Qala'id of al-'Ayni, pp. 115–116), and two further verses follow them...]]

It is said of it: qasa al-makan yaqsu qusuwwan, meaning: it became distant. And I made something distant (aqsaytu al-shay') when I removed it far away and delayed it.

The people of interpretation said likewise to what we have said.

Those who said this:
