⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿"a remote place"﴾: he said, "far-off."
⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.
⁕ Musa narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When the time of Maryam's delivery came, she went out to the side of the eastern prayer niche of the sanctuary and went to its farthest end.

* *

As for His saying ﴿"Then the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree"﴾:
Exalted is His mention says: the pains of childbirth brought her to the trunk of the palm tree. Then it was said: when the hamza was removed from it, [it became] ajaʾaha, as one says: "I brought you Zayd" (ataytuka bi-Zayd), and when the bi is dropped it is said "ataytuka Zayda," as His exalted saying: ﴿"Bring me blocks of iron"﴾ [ātūnī zubar al-ḥadīd], meaning: bring me with blocks of iron; but the alif was lengthened when the bi was dropped. Likewise they say: "I went out with him" and "I took him out," and "I went with him" and "I made him go." It is actually the causative form of "to come," as one says: "he came," and "I brought him" (ajaʾtuhu): that is, I brought him. And an Arab proverb: "Worst of what brought you to the marrow of Ur'ub" (shurra mā ajāʾanī ilā mukhkhat ʿurqūb), and "ashaʾa" is also said; it is said: "Worst of what brings you and drives you to that." From it is the saying of Zuhayr:

"And a neighbor who traveled, intending toward you, / fear and hope brought him (ajāʾathu al-makhāfatu wa'l-rajāʾ)."[[The verse is by Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma (Lisan: jay'a)...]]

That is: "he brought it," and "ajaʾahu ilaynā" and "ashaʾaka" is the dialect of Tamim, while "ajaʾaka" is the dialect of the people of al-ʿĀliya. Whoever interpreted it as "compelled her" (alja'aha) did so because when the labor pains came to her at the trunk of the palm, they had compelled her to it.

As for His saying ﴿"mansiyyan"﴾:
It is the passive participle of "nasiytu al-shay'," as if she said: "Would that I had been the thing that is cast away, forgotten and abandoned."

Those who said likewise to what we have said among the people of interpretation:

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: ʿAtaʾ al-Khurasani informed me, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Would that I had died before this and had been a thing forgotten, utterly forgotten!﴾ "I had not been created, and I had not been anything."

⁕ Musa narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿and had been a thing forgotten, utterly forgotten﴾, he said: "Nisyan (a thing forgotten): my remembrance was forgotten. Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 20–23 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿She said, "How can I have a boy when no man has touched me and I have not been unchaste?" (20) He said, "Thus [it will be]. Your Lord says, 'It is easy for Me, and [We will do it] so that We may make him a sign for the people and a mercy from Us. And it is a matter [already] decreed.'"﴾ (21)

Exalted is His mention says: Maryam said to Jibril, ﴿"How can I have a boy?"﴾ In what manner will I have a boy? Will it be through a husband I marry, from whom I conceive, or will God originate His creation in me as a new beginning? ﴿"When no man has touched me"﴾ of the descendants of Adam through lawful marriage. ﴿"And I have not been unchaste"﴾ since no one among them has touched me in a lawful manner, ﴿"unchaste"﴾ meaning, "I have not committed unchastity and done that in an unlawful way, so that I would have conceived through fornication."

As related:
⁕ Musa narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿"And I have not been unchaste"﴾: he says, "a fornicator."

﴿"He said, 'Thus [it will be]. Your Lord says, "It is easy for Me."'"﴾ Exalted is His mention says: Jibril said to her, "The matter is just as you describe it, that no man has touched you and you were not unchaste. But your Lord said, 'It is easy for Me': that is, the creation of the boy that I said I would bestow upon you is easy for Me; its creation is not beyond Me, and I will bestow him upon you without a stallion who would mount you."

﴿"And so that We may make him a sign for the people"﴾ says: And so that We may make the boy whom We bestow upon you a sign and a proof regarding My creation, I bestow him upon you. ﴿"And a mercy from Us"﴾ says: and a mercy from Us to you and to whoever believes in him and affirms him; I will create him from you. ﴿"And it is a matter [already] decreed"﴾ says: and his creation from you was a matter decreed by God, which has passed in His judgment and in His foreknowledge that it would come to be from you.

As related:
⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Someone I do not suspect told me, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, regarding ﴿"And it is a matter [already] decreed"﴾: that is, God has resolved upon that, and there is no escape from it.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So she conceived him, and withdrew with him to a remote place. (22) Then the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree. She said, "Would that I had died before this and had become a thing forgotten and out of mind!"﴾ (23)

In this speech there is an omitted element whose mention has been dropped, being sufficiently indicated by what was mentioned of it: ﴿"Then We breathed into her of Our spirit"﴾ [and she conceived a boy], ﴿"So she conceived him and withdrew with him to a remote place"﴾. This is also the interpretation of the people of interpretation.

Those who said this:
⁕ Muhammad ibn Sahl narrated to me, saying: Ismaʿil ibn ʿAbd al-Karim narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Samad ibn Maʿqil, the nephew of Wahb ibn Munabbih, narrated to me, saying: I heard Wahb say: When God sent Jibril to Maryam, he appeared to her in the form of a well-proportioned man, and she said to him: ﴿"I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing."﴾ Then he breathed into the opening of her shift until the breath reached the womb, and she conceived.
⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from one I do not suspect, from Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani, who said: When he said that, that is, when Jibril said ﴿"Thus [it will be]. Your Lord says, 'It is easy for Me'"﴾ ... the verse, she submitted to the command of God, and he breathed into her opening, then departed from her.
⁕ Musa narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When Jibril said that to her, she cast her outer garment over herself, and Jibril took hold of its sleeves and breathed into the opening of her shift, which was split at the front, and the breath entered her chest, and she conceived. Then her sister, the wife of Zakariyya, visited her one night; when she opened the door for her, she embraced her, and the wife of Zakariyya said: "O Maryam, do you know that I am pregnant?" Maryam said: "Do you know that I too am pregnant?" The wife of Zakariyya said: "I found that what is in my womb prostrates to what is in your womb." That is His saying ﴿"confirming a word from God"﴾.
⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: They say that he breathed only into the opening of her shift and her sleeve.

* *

As for His saying ﴿"So she withdrew with him to a remote place"﴾:
It means: she secluded herself with the one she had conceived, who is ʿIsa, and withdrew with him from the people to a remote place, ﴿"a remote place"﴾ meaning a far-off place distant from the people. It is said: "He is in a qasiy place" and "qassiy" with the same meaning, as the rajaz poet said:
"You will surely sit in the seat of the distant one... from me, the foul-smelling, the hated one."[[The two verses are by Ru'ba ibn al-'Ajjaj, the rajaz poet (see Fawa'id al-Qala'id of al-'Ayni, pp. 115–116), and two further verses follow them...]]

It is said of it: qasa al-makan yaqsu qusuwwan, meaning: it became distant. And I made something distant (aqsaytu al-shay') when I removed it far away and delayed it.

The people of interpretation said likewise to what we have said.

Those who said this:
⁕ Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿"So she withdrew with him to a remote place"﴾: he said, "a far-off place."
⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿"a remote place"﴾: he said, "far-off."
⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.
⁕ Musa narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When the time of Maryam's delivery came, she went out to the side of the eastern prayer niche of the sanctuary and went to its farthest end.

* *

As for His saying ﴿"Then the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree"﴾:
Exalted is His mention says: the pains of childbirth brought her to the trunk of the palm tree. Then it was said: when the hamza was removed from it, [it became] ajaʾaha, as one says: "I brought you Zayd" (ataytuka bi-Zayd), and when the bi is dropped it is said "ataytuka Zayda," as His exalted saying: ﴿"Bring me blocks of iron"﴾ [ātūnī zubar al-ḥadīd], meaning: bring me with blocks of iron; but the alif was lengthened when the bi was dropped. Likewise they say: "I went out with him" and "I took him out," and "I went with him" and "I made him go." It is actually the causative form of "to come," as one says: "he came," and "I brought him" (ajaʾtuhu): that is, I brought him. And an Arab proverb: "Worst of what brought you to the marrow of Ur'ub" (shurra mā ajāʾanī ilā mukhkhat ʿurqūb), and "ashaʾa" is also said; it is said: "Worst of what brings you and drives you to that." From it is the saying of Zuhayr:

"And a neighbor who traveled, intending toward you, / fear and hope brought him (ajāʾathu al-makhāfatu wa'l-rajāʾ)."[[The verse is by Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma (Lisan: jay'a)...]]

That is: "he brought it," and "ajaʾahu ilaynā" and "ashaʾaka" is the dialect of Tamim, while "ajaʾaka" is the dialect of the people of al-ʿĀliya. Whoever interpreted it as "compelled her" (alja'aha) did so because when the labor pains came to her at the trunk of the palm, they had compelled her to it.

The people of interpretation said likewise to what we have said.

Those who said this:
⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿"the pains of childbirth"﴾: he said, "The pains compelled her."
⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: The pains compelled her. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn ʿAbbas said: The pains compelled her to the trunk of the palm tree.
⁕ Musa narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿"Then the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree"﴾: he says, "The pains compelled her to the trunk of the palm tree."
⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿"Then the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree"﴾: he said, "They forced her to the trunk of the palm tree."

They differed about the place where Maryam, with ʿIsa, withdrew and where the pains drove her to give birth. Some said: That was in the lowest land of Egypt and the farthest land of Syria, because she fled from her people when she became pregnant, heading toward Egypt, fleeing from them.

Those who said this:
⁕ Muhammad ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: Ismaʿil ibn ʿAbd al-Karim narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Samad ibn Maʿqil narrated to me, that he heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say: When Maryam was pregnant, she had with her a relative called Yusuf the Carpenter, and they were going to the mosque beside Mount Zion, which at that time was one of their greatest mosques. Maryam and Yusuf served in that mosque in that era, and service to it had great merit, so they were eager for it, and they would personally tend to its affairs: its whitewashing, sweeping, cleaning, and every task done in it. No one of their time was more diligent in worship than they. The first to notice Maryam's pregnancy was her companion Yusuf; when he saw what was upon her, he was appalled, it weighed heavily on him, and he was horrified by it, not knowing how to resolve her matter. When Yusuf wished to accuse her, he recalled her righteousness and innocence, and that she had never been absent from him for a single hour; and when he wished to exonerate her, he saw what had appeared on her. When this grew severe for him, he spoke to her. The first thing he said to her was: "A matter has arisen in my soul concerning you, which I feared; I was eager to suppress it and keep it hidden within myself, but it overcame me, and I saw that speaking of it would ease my heart." She said: "Then say a good word." He said: "I would say nothing but that. Tell me: does seed sprout without a sowing? " She said: "Yes." He said: "Does a tree grow without rain falling on it?" She said: "Yes." He said: "Can a child be born without a male?" She said: "Yes. Do you not know that God, blessed and exalted, caused the crop to grow on the day He created it without seed, and the seed on that day came into being from the crop that God had made grow without seed? Or do you not know that by His power God caused the tree to grow without rain, and that by that same power He made rain a life for the tree after each of them had been created separately? Or do you say that God cannot cause the tree to grow until He is assisted by water, and that without that He could not make it grow?" Yusuf said to her: "I do not say this; rather, I know that God, blessed and exalted, by His power over what He wills, says to it 'Be,' and it is." Maryam said: "Do you not know that God, blessed and exalted, created Adam and his wife without female or male?" He said: "Yes." When she said that to him, it came into his mind that what was in her was something from God, blessed and exalted, and that he could not ask her about it, because he saw how she kept it secret. Then Yusuf took over the service of the mosque and relieved her of every task she had been doing, because he saw the delicacy of her body, the yellowing of her complexion, the darkening of her face, the swelling of her belly, the weakness of her strength, and the fixed gaze of her eyes; and Maryam had not been like this before. When her time of childbirth drew near, God revealed to her: "Leave the land of your people, for if they overpower you they will reproach you and kill your child." That matter reached her sister, and her sister was then pregnant, and had been given good news of Yahya. When they met, the mother of Yahya found that what was in her womb had fallen prostrate to ʿIsa in submission. Yusuf carried her to the land of Egypt on a donkey of his, with nothing between her and the saddle when she mounted. Yusuf set out with her until, when they were near the borders of Egypt, at the edge of her people's lands, the pains of childbirth seized Maryam. He brought her to the stall of a donkey (ariyy himar, meaning the manger of the donkey) and the root of a palm tree, at a time I think was either cold or hot ("the doubt is from Abu Ja'far"). The pains grew severe for Maryam; when she felt their intensity, she clung to the palm tree and embraced it, and the angels surrounded her, standing in rows encircling her.

A different account has also been transmitted from Wahb ibn Munabbih, namely:
⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated it to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from one I do not suspect, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: When her delivery drew near, that is Maryam, and she experienced what a woman experiences of labor, she went out of the city westward from Iliya, until childbirth overtook her at a village of Iliya six miles away called Bethlehem; the pains of childbirth drove her to the root of a palm tree beneath which was a cattle manger and a stream of water, and she gave birth to him there.

Others said: Rather, when the time of her delivery of what was in her womb came, she went out to the side of the eastern prayer niche of the sanctuary and went to its farthest end, and the pains drove her to the trunk of a palm tree; this is the statement of al-Suddi, whose narration has been mentioned before.
⁕ Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'ida narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Al-Mughira ibn ʿUthman informed me, saying: I heard Ibn ʿAbbas say: It was nothing more than that she conceived and gave birth.
⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Al-Mughira ibn ʿUthman ibn ʿAbd Allah informed me that he heard Ibn ʿAbbas say: It was nothing more than that she conceived and bore.

It is mentioned that she said this in the state of labor, out of shame before the people.

Those who said this:
⁕ Muhammad ibn Sahl narrated to me, saying: Ismaʿil ibn ʿAbd al-Karim narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Samad ibn Maʿqil, the nephew of Wahb ibn Munabbih, narrated to me, saying: I heard Wahb say: When God sent Jibril to Maryam, he appeared to her in the form of a well-proportioned man, and she said to him: ﴿"I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing."﴾ Then he breathed into the opening of her shift until the breath reached the womb, and she conceived.
⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from one I do not suspect, from Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani, who said: When he said that, that is, when Jibril said ﴿"Thus [it will be]. Your Lord says, 'It is easy for Me'"﴾ ... the verse, she submitted to the command of God, and he breathed into her opening, then departed from her.
⁕ Musa narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When Jibril said that to her, she cast her outer garment over herself, and Jibril took hold of its sleeves and breathed into the opening of her shift, which was split at the front, and the breath entered her chest, and she conceived. Then her sister, the wife of Zakariyya, visited her one night; when she opened the door for her, she embraced her, and the wife of Zakariyya said: "O Maryam, do you know that I am pregnant?" Maryam said: "Do you know that I too am pregnant?" The wife of Zakariyya said: "I found that what is in my womb prostrates to what is in your womb." That is His saying ﴿"confirming a word from God"﴾.
⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: They say that he breathed only into the opening of her shift and her sleeve.

* *

As for His saying ﴿"So she withdrew with him to a remote place"﴾:
It means: she secluded herself with the one she had conceived, who is ʿIsa, and withdrew with him from the people to a remote place, ﴿"a remote place"﴾ meaning a far-off place distant from the people. It is said: "He is in a qasiy place" and "qassiy" with the same meaning, as the rajaz poet said:
"You will surely sit in the seat of the distant one... from me, the foul-smelling, the hated one."[[The two verses are by Ru'ba ibn al-'Ajjaj, the rajaz poet (see Fawa'id al-Qala'id of al-'Ayni, pp. 115–116), and two further verses follow them...]]

It is said of it: qasa al-makan yaqsu qusuwwan, meaning: it became distant. And I made something distant (aqsaytu al-shay') when I removed it far away and delayed it.

The people of interpretation said likewise to what we have said.

Those who said this:
⁕ Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿"So she withdrew with him to a remote place"﴾: he said, "a far-off place."
⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿"a remote place"﴾: he said, "far-off."
⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.
⁕ Musa narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When the time of Maryam's delivery came, she went out to the side of the eastern prayer niche of the sanctuary and went to its farthest end.

* *

As for His saying ﴿"Then the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree"﴾:
Exalted is His mention says: the pains of childbirth brought her to the trunk of the palm tree. Then it was said: when the hamza was removed from it, [it became] ajaʾaha, as one says: "I brought you Zayd" (ataytuka bi-Zayd), and when the bi is dropped it is said "ataytuka Zayda," as His exalted saying: ﴿"Bring me blocks of iron"﴾ [ātūnī zubar al-ḥadīd], meaning: bring me with blocks of iron; but the alif was lengthened when the bi was dropped. Likewise they say: "I went out with him" and "I took him out," and "I went with him" and "I made him go." It is actually the causative form of "to come," as one says: "he came," and "I brought him" (ajaʾtuhu): that is, I brought him. And an Arab proverb: "Worst of what brought you to the marrow of Ur'ub" (shurra mā ajāʾanī ilā mukhkhat ʿurqūb), and "ashaʾa" is also said; it is said: "Worst of what brings you and drives you to that." From it is the saying of Zuhayr:

"And a neighbor who traveled, intending toward you, / fear and hope brought him (ajāʾathu al-makhāfatu wa'l-rajāʾ)."[[The verse is by Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma (Lisan: jay'a)...]]

That is: "he brought it," and "ajaʾahu ilaynā" and "ashaʾaka" is the dialect of Tamim, while "ajaʾaka" is the dialect of the people of al-ʿĀliya. Whoever interpreted it as "compelled her" (alja'aha) did so because when the labor pains came to her at the trunk of the palm, they had compelled her to it.

The people of interpretation said likewise to what we have said.

Those who said this:
⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿"the pains of childbirth"﴾: he said, "The pains compelled her."
⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: The pains compelled her. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn ʿAbbas said: The pains compelled her to the trunk of the palm tree.
⁕ Musa narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿"Then the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree"﴾: he says, "The pains compelled her to the trunk of the palm tree."
⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿"Then the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree"﴾: he said, "They forced her to the trunk of the palm tree."

They differed about the place where Maryam, with ʿIsa, withdrew and where the pains drove her to give birth. Some said: That was in the lowest land of Egypt and the farthest land of Syria, because she fled from her people when she became pregnant, heading toward Egypt, fleeing from them.

Those who said this:
⁕ Muhammad ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: Ismaʿil ibn ʿAbd al-Karim narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Samad ibn Maʿqil narrated to me, that he heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say: When Maryam was pregnant, she had with her a relative called Yusuf the Carpenter, and they were going to the mosque beside Mount Zion, which at that time was one of their greatest mosques. Maryam and Yusuf served in that mosque in that era, and service to it had great merit, so they were eager for it, and they would personally tend to its affairs: its whitewashing, sweeping, cleaning, and every task done in it. No one of their time was more diligent in worship than they. The first to notice Maryam's pregnancy was her companion Yusuf; when he saw what was upon her, he was appalled, it weighed heavily on him, and he was horrified by it, not knowing how to resolve her matter. When Yusuf wished to accuse her, he recalled her righteousness and innocence, and that she had never been absent from him for a single hour; and when he wished to exonerate her, he saw what had appeared on her. When this grew severe for him, he spoke to her. The first thing he said to her was: "A matter has arisen in my soul concerning you, which I feared; I was eager to suppress it and keep it hidden within myself, but it overcame me, and I saw that speaking of it would ease my heart." She said: "Then say a good word." He said: "I would say nothing but that. Tell me: does seed sprout without a sowing? " She said: "Yes." He said: "Does a tree grow without rain falling on it?" She said: "Yes." He said: "Can a child be born without a male?" She said: "Yes. Do you not know that God, blessed and exalted, caused the crop to grow on the day He created it without seed, and the seed on that day came into being from the crop that God had made grow without seed? Or do you not know that by His power God caused the tree to grow without rain, and that by that same power He made rain a life for the tree after each of them had been created separately? Or do you say that God cannot cause the tree to grow until He is assisted by water, and that without that He could not make it grow?" Yusuf said to her: "I do not say this; rather, I know that God, blessed and exalted, by His power over what He wills, says to it 'Be,' and it is." Maryam said: "Do you not know that God, blessed and exalted, created Adam and his wife without female or male?" He said: "Yes." When she said that to him, it came into his mind that what was in her was something from God, blessed and exalted, and that he could not ask her about it, because he saw how she kept it secret. Then Yusuf took over the service of the mosque and relieved her of every task she had been doing, because he saw the delicacy of her body, the yellowing of her complexion, the darkening of her face, the swelling of her belly, the weakness of her strength, and the fixed gaze of her eyes; and Maryam had not been like this before. When her time of childbirth drew near, God revealed to her: "Leave the land of your people, for if they overpower you they will reproach you and kill your child." That matter reached her sister, and her sister was then pregnant, and had been given good news of Yahya. When they met, the mother of Yahya found that what was in her womb had fallen prostrate to ʿIsa in submission. Yusuf carried her to the land of Egypt on a donkey of his, with nothing between her and the saddle when she mounted. Yusuf set out with her until, when they were near the borders of Egypt, at the edge of her people's lands, the pains of childbirth seized Maryam. He brought her to the stall of a donkey (ariyy himar, meaning the manger of the donkey) and the root of a palm tree, at a time I think was either cold or hot ("the doubt is from Abu Ja'far"). The pains grew severe for Maryam; when she felt their intensity, she clung to the palm tree and embraced it, and the angels surrounded her, standing in rows encircling her.

A different account has also been transmitted from Wahb ibn Munabbih, namely:
⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated it to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from one I do not suspect, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: When her delivery drew near, that is Maryam, and she experienced what a woman experiences of labor, she went out of the city westward from Iliya, until childbirth overtook her at a village of Iliya six miles away called Bethlehem; the pains of childbirth drove her to the root of a palm tree beneath which was a cattle manger and a stream of water, and she gave birth to him there.

Others said: Rather, when the time of her delivery of what was in her womb came, she went out to the side of the eastern prayer niche of the sanctuary and went to its farthest end, and the pains drove her to the trunk of a palm tree; this is the statement of al-Suddi, whose narration has been mentioned before.
⁕ Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'ida narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Al-Mughira ibn ʿUthman informed me, saying: I heard Ibn ʿAbbas say: It was nothing more than that she conceived and gave birth.
⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Al-Mughira ibn ʿUthman ibn ʿAbd Allah informed me that he heard Ibn ʿAbbas say: It was nothing more than that she conceived and bore.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿"Would that I had died before this"﴾:
It is mentioned that she said this in the state of labor, out of shame before the people.

As related:
⁕ Musa narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: She said, while in the pangs of labor, out of shame before the people: ﴿"Would that I had died before this and had become a thing forgotten and out of mind!"﴾ She means: "Would that I had died before this distress I am in, and before the grief of bearing a child without a husband. And would that I had been a 'nasy mansiyya': a thing that was forgotten and then left unsought, like menstrual rags which, once cast away, are neither sought nor remembered. Everything that is forgotten and abandoned and not sought is 'nasy'." The forms "nasy" and "nisy" (with fatha and kasra on the nun) are two well-known dialects of the Arabs with the same meaning, like "watr" and "witr," and "jasr" and "jisr." Whichever of them a reciter reads, it is correct in our view. Reading with kasra was the practice of most readers of the Hijaz, Medina, and Basra and some people of Kufa; reading with fatha was the practice of the people of Kufa. From it is the saying of the poet:

"As if for her in the earth there were a nasy she traces, / when she goes forth; and if she speaks to you, she is firm (tablat)."[[The verse is by al-Shanfara (Lisan: nasiya). It is said: al-nasy is the forgotten thing that is not remembered... Al-Farra said: al-nasy and al-nisy are two dialects, referring to rags a woman casts off from her menstrual blood, like watr and witr. He said: if he meant by nasy (with fatha) the verbal noun of forgetting, it would be correct.]]

By His saying "tuqussuhu" he means: she seeks it, because she had forgotten it until it was lost, then remembered it and sought it. By "tablat" he means: she is good and truthful.

If "nasy" is taken as a verbal noun of forgetting, it would be correct as well, since the Arabs, as is reported of them, say: "nasiytuhu nisyanan wa nasyan," just as some say "from obedience to the Lord and disobedience to Satan," meaning "and disobedience" (ʿisyan); and as you say "atayhu ityanan wa atyan," as the poet said:

"Its wickedness is well known among them, / and they see the doing of noble deeds as forbidden."[[In Lisan (atā): al-itiyan is coming... The author cites the verse to show that the Arabs say "nasiytuhu nisyanan wa nasyan" as they say "ataytuhu ityanan wa atyan." His word "ma'ruofa" is feminine because the subject, al-atī, is masculine, but it was made feminine by its annexation to al-fawahish, the plural of fahisha.]]

* *

As for His saying ﴿"mansiyyan"﴾:
It is the passive participle of "nasiytu al-shay'," as if she said: "Would that I had been the thing that is cast away, forgotten and abandoned."

Those who said likewise to what we have said among the people of interpretation:

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verses 20–23 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: ʿAtaʾ al-Khurasani informed me, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Would that I had died before this and had been a thing forgotten, utterly forgotten!﴾ "I had not been created, and I had not been anything."

⁕ Musa narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿and had been a thing forgotten, utterly forgotten﴾, he said: "Nisyan (a thing forgotten): my remembrance was forgotten. Mansiyyan (utterly forgotten): it is said, my trace was forgotten, so no trace or substance of mine is seen."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding ﴿and had been a thing forgotten, utterly forgotten﴾: "That is, a thing that is neither known nor mentioned."

⁕ al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding his saying ﴿and had been a thing forgotten, utterly forgotten﴾, he said: "I am not known, and it is not known who I am."

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Abu Jaʿfar, from al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas regarding ﴿nisyan mansiyyan﴾, he said: "It is the miscarriage (al-saqt)."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Would that I had died before this and had been a thing forgotten, utterly forgotten!﴾: "I had never been anything on the earth at all."

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 19, verses 24–25 (part 1 of 2)**

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Then he called to her from beneath her: "Do not grieve. Your Lord has placed beneath you a stream (sariyyan).﴾ (24) ﴿And shake toward yourself the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you fresh ripe dates.﴾ (25)

The reciters (qurra') differed concerning the reading of this. The majority of the reciters of the Hijaz and Iraq read ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ (fa-nadaha min tahtiha, with a kasra on the ha' of min tahtiha), meaning: "Jibril called to her from before her," with differing views among them on its interpretation. Among those who interpreted it this way, when they read ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ they read it so. Among others, they held that it was ʿIsa, and that he called to her from beneath her after she had given birth to him. Some reciters of Kufa and Basra read ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مَنْ تَحْتَهَا﴾ (fa-nadaha man tahtaha, with a fatha on the mim of man and on the ta' of tahta), meaning: "The one beneath her called to her," on the basis that the one beneath her was ʿIsa, and that he was the one who called to his mother.

*Those who said that the one who called to her from beneath her was the angel:*

Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Mu'min related to us, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbas recite: ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾, meaning: Jibril.

Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah Ahmad ibn Yunus related to me, he said: ʿAbthar informed us, he said: Husayn related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Maymun al-Awdi, he said: The one who called to her was the angel.

Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abu Ahmad related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrahim, from ʿAlqama, that he recited: "Then he addressed her from beneath her."

Abu Hisham al-Rifaʿi related to us, he said: Yahya related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrahim, from ʿAlqama, that he recited: "Then he addressed her from beneath her."

al-Rifaʿi related to us, he said: Waki' related to us, from his father, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrahim, from ʿAlqama, that he recited it so.

Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abu ʿAmir related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ he said: Jibril.

Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abu ʿAsim related to us, from Sufyan, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, the like of it.

Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Saʿid related to us, from Qatada: ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾: that is, from beneath the palm tree.

Musa related to us, he said: ʿAmr related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿فَنَادَاهَا﴾ Jibril ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا أَلا تَحْزَنِي﴾.

al-Hasan related to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾, he said: the angel.

I was told from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾: that is, Jibril, who was lower than her.

Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾, he said: Jibril called to her, and ʿIsa did not speak until she came to her people.

*Those who said: ʿIsa (ﷺ) called to her:*

Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abu ʿAsim related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾, he said: ʿIsa ibn Maryam.

Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abu ʿAmir related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, he said: Abu ʿAsim related to us, he said: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Saʿid related to us, from Qatada, from al-Hasan: ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ her son.

al-Hasan related to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatada, he said: al-Hasan said: He is her son.

Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salama related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from one whom no one doubts, from Wahb ibn Munabbih: ﴿فَنَادَاهَا﴾ ʿIsa ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا أَلا تَحْزَنِي﴾.

Abu Hamid Ahmad ibn al-Mughira al-Himsi related to me, he said: Uthman ibn Saʿid related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Muhajir related to us, from Thabit ibn ʿAjlan, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, regarding His words ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾, he said: ʿIsa. Do you not hear God say: ﴿فَأَشَارَتْ إِلَيْهِ﴾ ("So she pointed to him")?

Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾, he said: ʿIsa; he called to her ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا أَلا تَحْزَنِي قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾.

I was told from ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Jaʿfar, from his father, from al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas, from Abu al-ʿAliyah al-Riyahi, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who said: The one who addressed her was the one she had carried in her womb, and who entered through her mouth.

Abu Jaʿfar (al-Tabari) said: The more preferable of the two views in this matter, in our opinion, is the view of the one who said: The one who called to her was her son ʿIsa. This is because the reference to him is closer than the reference to Jibril, and to return the pronoun to the nearer referent is more preferable than returning it to the more distant one. Do you not see, in the context of His words ﴿فَحَمَلَتْهُ فَانْتَبَذَتْ بِهِ مَكَانًا قَصِيًّا﴾ ("So she conceived him, and withdrew with him to a remote place"), that it means: she bore ʿIsa and withdrew with him; then it says ﴿فَنَادَاهَا﴾ in sequence with that, referring to ʿIsa and the report about him? There is another reason as well: His words ﴿فَأَشَارَتْ إِلَيْهِ﴾ ("So she pointed to him"). She would not have pointed to him, God willing, unless she knew that he was speaking in that state, and because of what she had come to know and trust of him through his addressing her with his words: ﴿أَنْ لا تَحْزَنِي قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾, and what God informed us He said to her: "Point him out to the people." If that had been speech from Jibril, it would have been more fitting for the apparent report to make clear that ʿIsa would speak and argue on her behalf to the people, and that he commanded her to point to him for the people when they asked her about her condition and his.

Since that is the correct interpretation which we have explained, it becomes clear that both readings, namely ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ with a kasra and ﴿مَنْ تَحْتَهَا﴾ with a fatha, are correct. For when it is read with a kasra, the mention of ʿIsa is in His words ﴿فَنَادَاهَا﴾; and when it is read ﴿مَنْ تَحْتَهَا﴾ with a fatha, the verb belongs to the one beneath her, who is ʿIsa. The meaning of the statement then is: "The newborn beneath her called to her: Do not grieve, O mother, ﴿Your Lord has placed beneath you a stream﴾."

As related by:
Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مِنْ تَحْتِهَا أَلا تَحْزَنِي﴾: She said: "How could I not grieve, when you are with me, neither a married woman for whom I could say 'from a husband,' nor a slave woman for whom I could say 'from my master'? What excuse will I have before the people?" ﴿يَالَيْتَنِي مِتُّ قَبْلَ هَذَا وَكُنْتُ نَسْيًا مَنْسِيًّا﴾ ("Would that I had died before this, and had been a thing forgotten, utterly forgotten"). So ʿIsa said to her: "I will suffice you in speech."

The people of interpretation differed concerning what is meant by al-sariyy (the stream) in this place. Some of them said: It means the small river.

*Those who said that:*

Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abu ʿAsim related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara' ibn ʿAzib, regarding ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾: he said: al-jadwal (the stream).

Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar related to us, he said: Shuʿba related to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Bara' say regarding this verse ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾: he said: al-jadwal.

ʿAli related to me, he said: ʿAbd Allah related to us, he said: Muʿawiya related to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾: it is the river of ʿIsa.

Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾: he said: al-sariyy is the river which was beneath Maryam when she bore him; it was flowing and was called Sariyya.

Abu Husayn related to me, he said: ʿAbthar related to us, he said: Husayn related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Maymun al-Awdi, who said regarding this verse ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾: al-sariyy is a river from which one drinks.

Yaʿqub and Abu Kurayb related to us, both said: Hushaym related to us, he said: Husayn informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Maymun, regarding His words: ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾: he said: it is the jadwal.

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to us, he said: Abu ʿAsim related to us, he said: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿سَرِيًّا﴾: he said: a river in Syriac.

al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it. Ibn Juraij said: a river beside her.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abu Dawud related to us, he said: Shuʿba related to us, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾: he said: It was a stream. Then Humayd ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman said: The sariyy is the jadwal. He said: The rulers have overcome us regarding you.

al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Abu Bakr ibn ʿAyyash related to us, from Abu Husayn, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾: he said: It is the jadwal, the small river; and in the Nabataean language it is sariyy.

Abu Hamid al-Himsi related to me, he said: Uthman ibn Saʿid related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Muhajir related to us, from Thabit ibn ʿAjlan, who said: I asked Saʿid ibn Jubayr about the sariyy, and he said: It is a river.

Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Hushaym related to us, from Mughira, from Ibrahim, who said: It is the small river.

Yaʿqub related to me, he said: Hushaym related to us, he said: Mughira informed us, from Ibrahim, that he said: It is the small river, meaning the jadwal, meaning His words ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾.

Ibn Waki' related to us, he said: my father related to us, from Salama ibn Nubayt, from al-Dahhak, who said: A small stream in Syriac.

I was told from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd ibn Sulayman informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾: the small stream of the rivers.

Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Saʿid related to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾: and the sariyy is the jadwal, which the people of the Hijaz call it.

al-Hasan related to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq related to us, he said: Maʿmar informed us, regarding His words ﴿سَرِيًّا﴾: he said: It is a jadwal.

Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salama related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from one whom no one doubts, and from Wahb ibn Munabbih, regarding ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾: meaning the spring of water.

Musa ibn Harun related to us, he said: ʿAmr related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾: and the sariyy is the river.

Others said: It means ʿIsa.

*Those who said that:*

Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Saʿid related to us, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾: and the sariyy is ʿIsa himself.

Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾: meaning himself. He said: And what is more sariyy (noble) than him? He said: As for those who say the sariyy is the river, it is not like that; if it were a river, it would be beside her, not beneath her.

Abu Jaʿfar (al-Tabari) said: The more correct of the two views in this matter, in my opinion, is the view of those who said: It means the jadwal. That is because He informed her of the water which God had placed beside her; and He said to her: ﴿وَهُزِّي إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ تُسَاقِطْ عَلَيْكِ رُطَبًا جَنِيًّا فَكُلِي﴾ ("And shake toward yourself the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you fresh ripe dates, so eat") from this fresh date, ﴿وَاشْرَبِي﴾ ("and drink") from this water, ﴿وَقَرِّي عَيْنًا﴾ ("and be comforted in your eye") by your child. The sariyy is known in the speech of the Arabs as the small river. Among what proves this is the saying of Labid:

*So they passed through the middle of the sariyy's side and split it, a sealed spring with its reeds bordering it.*[[The verse is by Labid ibn Rabiʿa al-ʿAmiri, from his famous Muʿallaqa (see al-Zawzani's commentary on the Seven Muʿallaqat, al-Tibrizi's commentary on the Ten Odes, and Jamharat Ashʿar al-ʿArab, pp. 63–74). The author of the Jamhara said: tawassata means they entered its middle; ʿArd al-sariyy means the side of the river; the people of the Hijaz call the river sariyy. Sadaʿa means they split it. Masjura means a spring filled with water, as God said: "and the sea that is filled (al-bahr al-masjur)." Aqlamuha, also narrated as qalamuha, is a kind of brackish shrub; al-aqlam are the reeds of the flute. Al-Zawzani says: he means the wild ass and the she-ass crossed the side of the small river and split a spring filled with water, whose reeds had spread along it. The sense is: they came to a spring full of water, entered it from the side of its river, and its plants bordered it. The evidence is in the word "sariyy," which is the name of the small river.]]

It is also narrated as fina masjura (a variant reading in the manuscript without dots, of which we have not found this narration), and also as: fa-ghadara.

* *

Regarding His words: ﴿وَهُزِّي إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ﴾

It is mentioned that the trunk was a dry trunk, and she was commanded to shake it, and that was in the winter. Her shaking it means moving it.

As related by:
Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿وَهُزِّي إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ﴾: he said: move it.

*Those who said that:*

Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿وَهُزِّي إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ﴾, he said: It was a dry trunk, and he said to her: "Shake it," ﴿تُسَاقِطْ عَلَيْكِ رُطَبًا جَنِيًّا﴾.

Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Mu'min related to us, he said: I heard Abu Nuhayk say: It was a dry palm tree.

Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn ʿAskar related to me, he said: Ismaʿil ibn ʿAbd al-Karim related to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Samad ibn Maʿqil related to me, he said: I heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say regarding His words: ﴿وَهُزِّي إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ﴾: the dates would drop upon her, and that was in winter.

Musa ibn Harun related to us, he said: ʿAmr related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿وَهُزِّي إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ﴾: it was a trunk cut from it; she shook it, and behold, it was a palm tree; and a stream was made to flow for her in the sanctuary, and the palm tree dropped fresh ripe dates, and he said to her: ﴿فَكُلِي وَاشْرَبِي وَقَرِّي عَيْنًا﴾.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: "And shake toward yourself the palm tree."

*Those who said that:*

Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, he said: Mujahid said regarding ﴿وَهُزِّي إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ﴾: the palm tree.

Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abu Ahmad related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from ʿIsa ibn Maymun, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿وَهُزِّي إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ﴾: he said: the ʿajwa (a kind of date).

Yaʿqub related to me, he said: Hushaym related to us, he said: Husayn informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Maymun, that he recited this verse: ﴿وَهُزِّي إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ تُسَاقِطْ عَلَيْكِ رُطَبًا جَنِيًّا﴾, and he said: ʿAmr said: There is nothing better for a woman after childbirth than dates and fresh ripe dates. The letter bāʾ (with) was introduced in His words ﴿وَهُزِّي إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ﴾, as one says: "I married you to so-and-so" and "I married you with so-and-so"; and as He said ﴿تَنْبُتُ بِالدُّهْنِ﴾ ("it grows with oil"), meaning: it grows the oil.

The Arabs do this because verbs are expressed by means of the bāʾ; so when you refer to "I struck ʿAmr," you say "I did to him," and so with every verb. Therefore the bāʾ enters and exits verbs, and its entry and exit have the same meaning. The sense of the statement is: "And shake toward yourself the trunk of the palm tree." It would also have been a valid interpretation, had the commentators interpreted it so: "And shake toward yourself fresh dates with the trunk of the palm tree," meaning: "upon the trunk of the palm tree." But I do not know of anyone who explained it that way. Among the evidence for the bāʾ entering and exiting in the same place with the same meaning is the saying of the poet:

*In a Yemeni valley whose upper part grows sidr (lote trees), and whose lower part grows with al-markh and al-shabahan.*[[In (Lisan al-ʿArab: sadr) sidr is the lote tree, its singular being sidra... al-marakh is a tree of abundant but quick-growing foliage. In (Lisan al-ʿArab: shabah) al-shabahan is a plant resembling thyme, also called al-shabahan. Ibn Sayyida said: al-shabahan (with a vowel on the middle letter) and al-shabahan (with two damma) are a kind of thorny tree; it is said it is thyme, of Yemeni origin, as transmitted by Ibn Duraid. A man of ʿAbd al-Qays said: "In a Yemeni valley that grows the shath along its upper part..." The verse is cited by Ibn Bari, who said Abu ʿUbayda said: the verse belongs to al-Ahwal al-Yashkuri, whose name is Yaʿla. He said: its meaning is: and its lower part grows al-marakh, with the bāʾ being superfluous.]]

And [if you wish, you may consider it] as: "and it [the palm] causes to grow at its base [with the mirkh tree]," so that the bāʾ (ب) is transitive (lit. "causing to reach" or "making transitive"), since you have construed the verb as triliteral.

In the Sihah (al-Sihah, the lexicon of al-Jawhari): al-shubhan is the thyme (thumam) among fragrant plants. In Lisan al-Arab (under sh-th-th): al-shath is a kind of tree, according to Ibn Duraid, and he cited the verse: "In a Yemeni valley where its branch grows the shath."

Others said: al-shath is a tree of pleasant scent, bitter in taste, with which hides are tanned. Abu al-Duqaysh said: it grows in the mountains of al-Ghawr, Tihama and Najd.

The verse is evidence that the bāʾ in His words "bi-al-mirkh" is superfluous (zāʾida); its presence and absence are the same. It is like the bāʾ in the words of God, Exalted: ﴿And shake toward yourself the trunk of the palm tree﴾ [19:25]. In Lisan al-Arab (under h-z-z): al-hazz is the moving of a thing, as one shakes a spear so that it trembles and sways. "Hazzahu yahuzzuhu hazzan" and "hazza bihi" [both mean he shook it]. In the Revelation: ﴿And shake toward yourself the trunk of the palm tree﴾, meaning move it. The Arabs say: "hazzahu" and "hazza bihi" when he moved it. Similar are: "khudh al-khitam" and "khudh bi-al-khitam" (take the halter), and "taʿallaqa Zaydan" and "taʿallaqa bi-Zayd" (he clung to Zayd). Ibn Sayyidah said: he made it transitive with the bāʾ because in hazzi there is the sense of pulling (from jarr, "to pull").

The reciters differed regarding the reading of His words ﴿tasāqaṭu﴾. Most of the reciters of Madinah, Basra and Kufa read it ﴿tassāqaṭu﴾ with a tāʾ, from tasāqaṭa, and with a doubled sīn, meaning: "the palm tree drops upon you ripe, fresh dates," then one of the two tāʾs is assimilated into the other, so it is doubled. [The Jalalayn's expression: with two tāʾs, the second being changed to a sīn and assimilated into the sīn.] Those who read it thus appear to have directed the meaning as: "And shake toward yourself the trunk of the palm tree; the palm tree drops upon you ripe dates."

Some of the reciters of Kufa read it ﴿tasāqaṭu﴾ with a tāʾ and a light sīn, and they directed the meaning toward the same as the doubled reading, differing only in recitation.

It is narrated from al-Bara ibn Azib that he read it ﴿yusāqiṭu﴾ with a yāʾ.
⁕ Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated this to me, saying: al-Qasim told us, saying: Yazid told us, from Jarir ibn Hazim, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Bara ibn Azib reciting it thus. He apparently directed the meaning to: "And shake toward yourself the trunk of the palm tree; the trunk drops upon you ripe, fresh dates."

It is narrated from Abu Nahik that he read it ﴿tusqiṭu﴾ with a tāʾ bearing a damma and without the alif.
⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated this to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Muʾmin told us, saying: I heard Abu Nahik reciting it thus. He apparently directed the meaning to: "The palm tree drops upon you ripe, fresh dates."

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct view in this matter, in my opinion, is that these three readings, namely ﴿tassāqaṭu﴾ with a tāʾ and doubled sīn, with a tāʾ and light sīn, and with a yāʾ and doubled sīn, are readings of close meanings, and reciters who had knowledge of the Qur'an read each of them. Whichever of these a reader recites, he is correct, because when the trunk drops ripe dates while it remains intact and uncut, the palm tree has dropped ripe dates; and when the palm tree drops ripe dates, the palm tree has dropped all of it, its trunk and what is other than its trunk. This is because the palm tree, as long as it stands on its root, is only trunk, fronds and palm leaves; when it is cut, it becomes a trunk. The trunk which Mary was commanded to shake was not, to our knowledge, anyone who said it was a cut trunk except al-Suddi, who claimed that by her shaking it, it returned to being a palm tree. So the meaning of the one who said "the trunk dropped upon her" and the meaning of the one who said "the palm tree dropped upon her" is one palm tree. Thus the soundness of what we have said becomes clear.

* *

As for His words ﴿janiyyan﴾ [ripe, fresh]: it means "majniyyan" (picked); its original form was a passive participle (maf'ul), but it was shifted to the form faʿil. Al-majni is that which is taken fresh, and whatever is taken from a fruit, or moved from its place while still fresh, has been "ijtuniya" (picked); hence it is said: "So-and-so gathers truffles" (yajtani al-kamʾah). From it is the saying of the nephew of Judhayma:

"This is my picking, and its choicest part is in it, since every picker brings his hand to his mouth."

[The verse is cited in Lisan al-Arab (under j-n-y). Abu ʿUbayd said: this is struck as a proverb for a man who prefers his companion with the best of what he has. Abu ʿUbayd said: Ibn al-Kalbi mentioned that the proverb belongs to ʿAmr ibn ʿAdi al-Lakhmi, the nephew of Judhayma, and he was the first to say it. Judhayma stopped at a place and commanded the people to gather truffles for him; some of them kept the best of what they found and ate its good part, while ʿAmr brought him the best of what he found and ate none of it. When he came to his maternal uncle Judhayma, he said: "This..." (the verse). Al-janā is what is picked from a tree. It is also narrated as "hadhā janāy wa-hijānuhu fīhi", i.e., its choicest. He said: "Janaytu al-thamar, ajnīhā, wa-ajtaniyhā" have the same meaning. Ibn Sayyidah: "Janā al-thamara wa-nahwahu wa-tajannāhā" all mean: he took it from its tree. On this the author cited the verse.]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 19, verses 24–25 (part 1 of 2)**

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Then he called to her from beneath her: "Do not grieve. Your Lord has placed beneath you a stream (sariyyan).﴾ (24) ﴿And shake toward yourself the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you fresh ripe dates.﴾ (25)

The reciters (qurra') differed concerning the reading of this. The majority of the reciters of the Hijaz and Iraq read ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ (fa-nadaha min tahtiha, with a kasra on the ha' of min tahtiha), meaning: "Jibril called to her from before her," with differing views among them on its interpretation. Among those who interpreted it this way, when they read ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ they read it so. Among others, they held that it was ʿIsa, and that he called to her from beneath her after she had given birth to him. Some reciters of Kufa and Basra read ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مَنْ تَحْتَهَا﴾ (fa-nadaha man tahtaha, with a fatha on the mim of man and on the ta' of tahta), meaning: "The one beneath her called to her," on the basis that the one beneath her was ʿIsa, and that he was the one who called to his mother.

*Those who said that the one who called to her from beneath her was the angel:*

Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Mu'min related to us, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbas recite: ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾, meaning: Jibril.

Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah Ahmad ibn Yunus related to me, he said: ʿAbthar informed us, he said: Husayn related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Maymun al-Awdi, he said: The one who called to her was the angel.

Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abu Ahmad related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrahim, from ʿAlqama, that he recited: "Then he addressed her from beneath her."

Abu Hisham al-Rifaʿi related to us, he said: Yahya related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrahim, from ʿAlqama, that he recited: "Then he addressed her from beneath her."

al-Rifaʿi related to us, he said: Waki' related to us, from his father, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrahim, from ʿAlqama, that he recited it so.

Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abu ʿAmir related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ he said: Jibril.

Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abu ʿAsim related to us, from Sufyan, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, the like of it.

Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Saʿid related to us, from Qatada: ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾: that is, from beneath the palm tree.

Musa related to us, he said: ʿAmr related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿فَنَادَاهَا﴾ Jibril ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا أَلا تَحْزَنِي﴾.

al-Hasan related to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾, he said: the angel.

I was told from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾: that is, Jibril, who was lower than her.

Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾, he said: Jibril called to her, and ʿIsa did not speak until she came to her people.

*Those who said: ʿIsa (ﷺ) called to her:*

Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abu ʿAsim related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾, he said: ʿIsa ibn Maryam.

Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abu ʿAmir related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, he said: Abu ʿAsim related to us, he said: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Saʿid related to us, from Qatada, from al-Hasan: ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ her son.

al-Hasan related to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatada, he said: al-Hasan said: He is her son.

Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salama related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from one whom no one doubts, from Wahb ibn Munabbih: ﴿فَنَادَاهَا﴾ ʿIsa ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا أَلا تَحْزَنِي﴾.

Abu Hamid Ahmad ibn al-Mughira al-Himsi related to me, he said: Uthman ibn Saʿid related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Muhajir related to us, from Thabit ibn ʿAjlan, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, regarding His words ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾, he said: ʿIsa. Do you not hear God say: ﴿فَأَشَارَتْ إِلَيْهِ﴾ ("So she pointed to him")?

Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾, he said: ʿIsa; he called to her ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا أَلا تَحْزَنِي قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾.

I was told from ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Jaʿfar, from his father, from al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas, from Abu al-ʿAliyah al-Riyahi, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who said: The one who addressed her was the one she had carried in her womb, and who entered through her mouth.

Abu Jaʿfar (al-Tabari) said: The more preferable of the two views in this matter, in our opinion, is the view of the one who said: The one who called to her was her son ʿIsa. This is because the reference to him is closer than the reference to Jibril, and to return the pronoun to the nearer referent is more preferable than returning it to the more distant one. Do you not see, in the context of His words ﴿فَحَمَلَتْهُ فَانْتَبَذَتْ بِهِ مَكَانًا قَصِيًّا﴾ ("So she conceived him, and withdrew with him to a remote place"), that it means: she bore ʿIsa and withdrew with him; then it says ﴿فَنَادَاهَا﴾ in sequence with that, referring to ʿIsa and the report about him? There is another reason as well: His words ﴿فَأَشَارَتْ إِلَيْهِ﴾ ("So she pointed to him"). She would not have pointed to him, God willing, unless she knew that he was speaking in that state, and because of what she had come to know and trust of him through his addressing her with his words: ﴿أَنْ لا تَحْزَنِي قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾, and what God informed us He said to her: "Point him out to the people." If that had been speech from Jibril, it would have been more fitting for the apparent report to make clear that ʿIsa would speak and argue on her behalf to the people, and that he commanded her to point to him for the people when they asked her about her condition and his.

Since that is the correct interpretation which we have explained, it becomes clear that both readings, namely ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ with a kasra and ﴿مَنْ تَحْتَهَا﴾ with a fatha, are correct. For when it is read with a kasra, the mention of ʿIsa is in His words ﴿فَنَادَاهَا﴾; and when it is read ﴿مَنْ تَحْتَهَا﴾ with a fatha, the verb belongs to the one beneath her, who is ʿIsa. The meaning of the statement then is: "The newborn beneath her called to her: Do not grieve, O mother, ﴿Your Lord has placed beneath you a stream﴾."

As related by:
Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مِنْ تَحْتِهَا أَلا تَحْزَنِي﴾: She said: "How could I not grieve, when you are with me, neither a married woman for whom I could say 'from a husband,' nor a slave woman for whom I could say 'from my master'? What excuse will I have before the people?" ﴿يَالَيْتَنِي مِتُّ قَبْلَ هَذَا وَكُنْتُ نَسْيًا مَنْسِيًّا﴾ ("Would that I had died before this, and had been a thing forgotten, utterly forgotten"). So ʿIsa said to her: "I will suffice you in speech."

The people of interpretation differed concerning what is meant by al-sariyy (the stream) in this place. Some of them said: It means the small river.

*Those who said that:*

Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abu ʿAsim related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara' ibn ʿAzib, regarding ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾: he said: al-jadwal (the stream).

Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar related to us, he said: Shuʿba related to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Bara' say regarding this verse ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾: he said: al-jadwal.

ʿAli related to me, he said: ʿAbd Allah related to us, he said: Muʿawiya related to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾: it is the river of ʿIsa.

Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾: he said: al-sariyy is the river which was beneath Maryam when she bore him; it was flowing and was called Sariyya.

Abu Husayn related to me, he said: ʿAbthar related to us, he said: Husayn related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Maymun al-Awdi, who said regarding this verse ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾: al-sariyy is a river from which one drinks.

Yaʿqub and Abu Kurayb related to us, both said: Hushaym related to us, he said: Husayn informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Maymun, regarding His words: ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾: he said: it is the jadwal.

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to us, he said: Abu ʿAsim related to us, he said: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿سَرِيًّا﴾: he said: a river in Syriac.

al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it. Ibn Juraij said: a river beside her.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abu Dawud related to us, he said: Shuʿba related to us, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾: he said: It was a stream. Then Humayd ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman said: The sariyy is the jadwal. He said: The rulers have overcome us regarding you.

al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Abu Bakr ibn ʿAyyash related to us, from Abu Husayn, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾: he said: It is the jadwal, the small river; and in the Nabataean language it is sariyy.

Abu Hamid al-Himsi related to me, he said: Uthman ibn Saʿid related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Muhajir related to us, from Thabit ibn ʿAjlan, who said: I asked Saʿid ibn Jubayr about the sariyy, and he said: It is a river.

Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Hushaym related to us, from Mughira, from Ibrahim, who said: It is the small river.

Yaʿqub related to me, he said: Hushaym related to us, he said: Mughira informed us, from Ibrahim, that he said: It is the small river, meaning the jadwal, meaning His words ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾.

Ibn Waki' related to us, he said: my father related to us, from Salama ibn Nubayt, from al-Dahhak, who said: A small stream in Syriac.

I was told from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd ibn Sulayman informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾: the small stream of the rivers.

Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Saʿid related to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾: and the sariyy is the jadwal, which the people of the Hijaz call it.

al-Hasan related to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq related to us, he said: Maʿmar informed us, regarding His words ﴿سَرِيًّا﴾: he said: It is a jadwal.

Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salama related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from one whom no one doubts, and from Wahb ibn Munabbih, regarding ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾: meaning the spring of water.

Musa ibn Harun related to us, he said: ʿAmr related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾: and the sariyy is the river.

Others said: It means ʿIsa.

*Those who said that:*

Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Saʿid related to us, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾: and the sariyy is ʿIsa himself.

Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾: meaning himself. He said: And what is more sariyy (noble) than him? He said: As for those who say the sariyy is the river, it is not like that; if it were a river, it would be beside her, not beneath her.

Abu Jaʿfar (al-Tabari) said: The more correct of the two views in this matter, in my opinion, is the view of those who said: It means the jadwal. That is because He informed her of the water which God had placed beside her; and He said to her: ﴿وَهُزِّي إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ تُسَاقِطْ عَلَيْكِ رُطَبًا جَنِيًّا فَكُلِي﴾ ("And shake toward yourself the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you fresh ripe dates, so eat") from this fresh date, ﴿وَاشْرَبِي﴾ ("and drink") from this water, ﴿وَقَرِّي عَيْنًا﴾ ("and be comforted in your eye") by your child. The sariyy is known in the speech of the Arabs as the small river. Among what proves this is the saying of Labid:

*So they passed through the middle of the sariyy's side and split it, a sealed spring with its reeds bordering it.*[[The verse is by Labid ibn Rabiʿa al-ʿAmiri, from his famous Muʿallaqa (see al-Zawzani's commentary on the Seven Muʿallaqat, al-Tibrizi's commentary on the Ten Odes, and Jamharat Ashʿar al-ʿArab, pp. 63–74). The author of the Jamhara said: tawassata means they entered its middle; ʿArd al-sariyy means the side of the river; the people of the Hijaz call the river sariyy. Sadaʿa means they split it. Masjura means a spring filled with water, as God said: "and the sea that is filled (al-bahr al-masjur)." Aqlamuha, also narrated as qalamuha, is a kind of brackish shrub; al-aqlam are the reeds of the flute. Al-Zawzani says: he means the wild ass and the she-ass crossed the side of the small river and split a spring filled with water, whose reeds had spread along it. The sense is: they came to a spring full of water, entered it from the side of its river, and its plants bordered it. The evidence is in the word "sariyy," which is the name of the small river.]]

It is also narrated as fina masjura (a variant reading in the manuscript without dots, of which we have not found this narration), and also as: fa-ghadara.

* *

Regarding His words: ﴿وَهُزِّي إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ﴾

It is mentioned that the trunk was a dry trunk, and she was commanded to shake it, and that was in the winter. Her shaking it means moving it.

As related by:
Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿وَهُزِّي إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ﴾: he said: move it.

*Those who said that:*

Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿وَهُزِّي إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ﴾, he said: It was a dry trunk, and he said to her: "Shake it," ﴿تُسَاقِطْ عَلَيْكِ رُطَبًا جَنِيًّا﴾.

Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Mu'min related to us, he said: I heard Abu Nuhayk say: It was a dry palm tree.

Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn ʿAskar related to me, he said: Ismaʿil ibn ʿAbd al-Karim related to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Samad ibn Maʿqil related to me, he said: I heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say regarding His words: ﴿وَهُزِّي إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ﴾: the dates would drop upon her, and that was in winter.

Musa ibn Harun related to us, he said: ʿAmr related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿وَهُزِّي إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ﴾: it was a trunk cut from it; she shook it, and behold, it was a palm tree; and a stream was made to flow for her in the sanctuary, and the palm tree dropped fresh ripe dates, and he said to her: ﴿فَكُلِي وَاشْرَبِي وَقَرِّي عَيْنًا﴾.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: "And shake toward yourself the palm tree."

*Those who said that:*

Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, he said: Mujahid said regarding ﴿وَهُزِّي إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ﴾: the palm tree.

Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abu Ahmad related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from ʿIsa ibn Maymun, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿وَهُزِّي إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ﴾: he said: the ʿajwa (a kind of date).

Yaʿqub related to me, he said: Hushaym related to us, he said: Husayn informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Maymun, that he recited this verse: ﴿وَهُزِّي إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ تُسَاقِطْ عَلَيْكِ رُطَبًا جَنِيًّا﴾, and he said: ʿAmr said: There is nothing better for a woman after childbirth than dates and fresh ripe dates. The letter bāʾ (with) was introduced in His words ﴿وَهُزِّي إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ﴾, as one says: "I married you to so-and-so" and "I married you with so-and-so"; and as He said ﴿تَنْبُتُ بِالدُّهْنِ﴾ ("it grows with oil"), meaning: it grows the oil.

The Arabs do this because verbs are expressed by means of the bāʾ; so when you refer to "I struck ʿAmr," you say "I did to him," and so with every verb. Therefore the bāʾ enters and exits verbs, and its entry and exit have the same meaning. The sense of the statement is: "And shake toward yourself the trunk of the palm tree." It would also have been a valid interpretation, had the commentators interpreted it so: "And shake toward yourself fresh dates with the trunk of the palm tree," meaning: "upon the trunk of the palm tree." But I do not know of anyone who explained it that way. Among the evidence for the bāʾ entering and exiting in the same place with the same meaning is the saying of the poet:

*In a Yemeni valley whose upper part grows sidr (lote trees), and whose lower part grows with al-markh and al-shabahan.*[[In (Lisan al-ʿArab: sadr) sidr is the lote tree, its singular being sidra... al-marakh is a tree of abundant but quick-growing foliage. In (Lisan al-ʿArab: shabah) al-shabahan is a plant resembling thyme, also called al-shabahan. Ibn Sayyida said: al-shabahan (with a vowel on the middle letter) and al-shabahan (with two damma) are a kind of thorny tree; it is said it is thyme, of Yemeni origin, as transmitted by Ibn Duraid. A man of ʿAbd al-Qays said: "In a Yemeni valley that grows the shath along its upper part..." The verse is cited by Ibn Bari, who said Abu ʿUbayda said: the verse belongs to al-Ahwal al-Yashkuri, whose name is Yaʿla. He said: its meaning is: and its lower part grows al-marakh, with the bāʾ being superfluous.]]

And [if you wish, you may consider it] as: "and it [the palm] causes to grow at its base [with the mirkh tree]," so that the bāʾ (ب) is transitive (lit. "causing to reach" or "making transitive"), since you have construed the verb as triliteral.

In the Sihah (al-Sihah, the lexicon of al-Jawhari): al-shubhan is the thyme (thumam) among fragrant plants. In Lisan al-Arab (under sh-th-th): al-shath is a kind of tree, according to Ibn Duraid, and he cited the verse: "In a Yemeni valley where its branch grows the shath."

Others said: al-shath is a tree of pleasant scent, bitter in taste, with which hides are tanned. Abu al-Duqaysh said: it grows in the mountains of al-Ghawr, Tihama and Najd.

The verse is evidence that the bāʾ in His words "bi-al-mirkh" is superfluous (zāʾida); its presence and absence are the same. It is like the bāʾ in the words of God, Exalted: ﴿And shake toward yourself the trunk of the palm tree﴾ [19:25]. In Lisan al-Arab (under h-z-z): al-hazz is the moving of a thing, as one shakes a spear so that it trembles and sways. "Hazzahu yahuzzuhu hazzan" and "hazza bihi" [both mean he shook it]. In the Revelation: ﴿And shake toward yourself the trunk of the palm tree﴾, meaning move it. The Arabs say: "hazzahu" and "hazza bihi" when he moved it. Similar are: "khudh al-khitam" and "khudh bi-al-khitam" (take the halter), and "taʿallaqa Zaydan" and "taʿallaqa bi-Zayd" (he clung to Zayd). Ibn Sayyidah said: he made it transitive with the bāʾ because in hazzi there is the sense of pulling (from jarr, "to pull").

The reciters differed regarding the reading of His words ﴿tasāqaṭu﴾.
