Most of the reciters of Madinah, Basra and Kufa read it ﴿tassāqaṭu﴾ with a tāʾ, from tasāqaṭa, and with a doubled sīn, meaning: "the palm tree drops upon you ripe, fresh dates," then one of the two tāʾs is assimilated into the other, so it is doubled. [The Jalalayn's expression: with two tāʾs, the second being changed to a sīn and assimilated into the sīn.] Those who read it thus appear to have directed the meaning as: "And shake toward yourself the trunk of the palm tree; the palm tree drops upon you ripe dates."

Some of the reciters of Kufa read it ﴿tasāqaṭu﴾ with a tāʾ and a light sīn, and they directed the meaning toward the same as the doubled reading, differing only in recitation.

It is narrated from al-Bara ibn Azib that he read it ﴿yusāqiṭu﴾ with a yāʾ.
⁕ Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated this to me, saying: al-Qasim told us, saying: Yazid told us, from Jarir ibn Hazim, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Bara ibn Azib reciting it thus. He apparently directed the meaning to: "And shake toward yourself the trunk of the palm tree; the trunk drops upon you ripe, fresh dates."

It is narrated from Abu Nahik that he read it ﴿tusqiṭu﴾ with a tāʾ bearing a damma and without the alif.
⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated this to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Muʾmin told us, saying: I heard Abu Nahik reciting it thus. He apparently directed the meaning to: "The palm tree drops upon you ripe, fresh dates."

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct view in this matter, in my opinion, is that these three readings, namely ﴿tassāqaṭu﴾ with a tāʾ and doubled sīn, with a tāʾ and light sīn, and with a yāʾ and doubled sīn, are readings of close meanings, and reciters who had knowledge of the Qur'an read each of them. Whichever of these a reader recites, he is correct, because when the trunk drops ripe dates while it remains intact and uncut, the palm tree has dropped ripe dates; and when the palm tree drops ripe dates, the palm tree has dropped all of it, its trunk and what is other than its trunk. This is because the palm tree, as long as it stands on its root, is only trunk, fronds and palm leaves; when it is cut, it becomes a trunk. The trunk which Mary was commanded to shake was not, to our knowledge, anyone who said it was a cut trunk except al-Suddi, who claimed that by her shaking it, it returned to being a palm tree. So the meaning of the one who said "the trunk dropped upon her" and the meaning of the one who said "the palm tree dropped upon her" is one palm tree. Thus the soundness of what we have said becomes clear.

* *

As for His words ﴿janiyyan﴾ [ripe, fresh]: it means "majniyyan" (picked); its original form was a passive participle (maf'ul), but it was shifted to the form faʿil. Al-majni is that which is taken fresh, and whatever is taken from a fruit, or moved from its place while still fresh, has been "ijtuniya" (picked); hence it is said: "So-and-so gathers truffles" (yajtani al-kamʾah). From it is the saying of the nephew of Judhayma:

"This is my picking, and its choicest part is in it, since every picker brings his hand to his mouth."

[The verse is cited in Lisan al-Arab (under j-n-y). Abu ʿUbayd said: this is struck as a proverb for a man who prefers his companion with the best of what he has. Abu ʿUbayd said: Ibn al-Kalbi mentioned that the proverb belongs to ʿAmr ibn ʿAdi al-Lakhmi, the nephew of Judhayma, and he was the first to say it. Judhayma stopped at a place and commanded the people to gather truffles for him; some of them kept the best of what they found and ate its good part, while ʿAmr brought him the best of what he found and ate none of it. When he came to his maternal uncle Judhayma, he said: "This..." (the verse). Al-janā is what is picked from a tree. It is also narrated as "hadhā janāy wa-hijānuhu fīhi", i.e., its choicest. He said: "Janaytu al-thamar, ajnīhā, wa-ajtaniyhā" have the same meaning. Ibn Sayyidah: "Janā al-thamara wa-nahwahu wa-tajannāhā" all mean: he took it from its tree. On this the author cited the verse.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 26:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So eat and drink and be comforted. And if you see any human, say, "Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast, so I will not speak today to any human being."﴾ (19:26)

His saying, exalted is He, means: "Eat from the fresh dates that fall upon you, and drink from the water of the stream that your Lord has placed beneath you; do not fear hunger or thirst." ﴿And be comforted﴾ means: be content in soul, rejoice at your giving birth to me, and do not grieve. The word "eye" (ʿayn) is in the accusative because it is the thing described as "settling" (qarar). The meaning of the speech is: "so let your eye be settled with your son," and then the verb was transferred from the eye to the woman who owns the eye, so "eye" was put in the accusative as a specification (tafsir), since the verb originally belonged to her. This is like His saying, ﴿And if they give you willingly something of it, [then consume it]﴾, whose original sense is: "If their souls are pleased with you."

* *

And His saying, ﴿and his breast became constricted﴾

Among this is His saying, ﴿It will drop upon you fresh ripe dates﴾, which originally means: "it will drop upon you the ripe dates of the trunk," so the verb was transferred to the trunk (jidhʿ), according to the reading of the one who reads it with the yāʾ. According to the reading of the one who reads ﴿tusāqiṭ﴾ with the tāʾ, the meaning is: "the ripe dates of the palm tree will drop upon you," and then the verb was transferred to the palm tree.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His saying ﴿wa-qarrī﴾.

As for the people of Medina, they recited it ﴿waqarri﴾ with a fatha on the qāf, according to the dialect of those who say qarirtu bil-makān uqarr bihi, and qarirtu ʿaynan, uqarru bihi qarūran. This, as was related to me, is the dialect of Quraysh, and the recitation is upon it.

As for the people of Najd, they say qarrartu bihi ʿaynan, uqarru bihi qarāran, and qarrartu bil-makān uqarru bihi. So the recitation according to their dialect is ﴿wa-qiri ʿaynan﴾ with a kasra on the qāf. The recitation with us is according to the dialect of Quraysh, with a fatha on the qāf.

* *

And His saying, ﴿If you see any human among mankind﴾

He says: if you see among the sons of Adam anyone who speaks to you or asks you about something, concerning your affair, the affair of your son, and the cause of your giving birth to him, ﴿then say, "Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast"﴾, meaning: say, "I have obligated myself to God to observe silence, that I will not speak to any of the sons of Adam today." ﴿So I will not speak today to any human being﴾.

The people of interpretation said the same as what we said concerning the meaning of fasting.

Those who said that:

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us, saying: Muʿtamir ibn Sulaymān related to us, from his father, who said: I heard Anas ibn Mālik say concerning this verse, ﴿Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast﴾, "silence."

Zakariyyā ibn Yahyā ibn Abī Zāʾida related to me, saying: Ḥajjāj related to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: al-Mughīra ibn ʿUthmān informed me, saying: I heard Anas ibn Mālik say, ﴿Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast﴾, he said: "silence."

Muḥammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding his saying, ﴿Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast﴾, he said: by fasting he means silence.

Yaʿqūb related to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayya related to us, from Sulaymān al-Taymī, who said: I heard Anas recite, ﴿Wa-innī nadhartu lil-Raḥmān ṣawman wa-ṣamtā﴾.

al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah, concerning ﴿Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast﴾: as for His saying, ﴿ṣawman﴾, she fasted from food, drink and speech.

I was told from al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say concerning His saying, ﴿I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast﴾: among the Children of Israel there was one who, when he exerted himself, would fast from speech just as he fasts from food, except for the remembrance of God. So he said that to her, and she said: "Indeed, I fast from speech as I fast from food, except for the remembrance of God." When they spoke to her she gestured to him, and they said ﴿How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?﴾, and he answered them and said ﴿Indeed, I am the servant of God; He has given me the Scripture﴾, until ﴿That is Jesus, son of Mary, the word of truth about which they dispute﴾.

They differed concerning the reason for which she was commanded to fast from speaking to humans. Some of them said: she was commanded to do so because she had no clear proof before the people, for she had come with a child out of wedlock, so she was commanded to abstain from speech so that her son would speak for her.

Those who said that:

Hārūn ibn Isḥāq al-Hamadhānī related to us, saying: Muṣʿab ibn al-Miqdām related to us, saying: Isrāʾīl related to us, saying: Abū Isḥāq related to us, from Ḥārithah, who said: I was with Ibn Masʿūd when two men came, one of whom greeted him and the other did not. He said: "What is your matter?" His companions said: "He has sworn not to speak to people today." ʿAbdullāh said: "Speak to the people and greet them, for that is a woman who knew that no one would believe her that she had conceived without a husband," meaning by that Mary, peace be upon her.

Yūnus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: when Jesus said to Mary, ﴿Do not grieve﴾, she said: "How could I not grieve when you are with me, neither having a husband nor being a slave? What excuse do I have before the people?" ﴿Oh, I wish I had died before this and had been forgotten and out of mind﴾. Then Jesus said to her: "I will suffice you in speech." ﴿And if you see any human, say, "Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast, so I will not speak today to any human being."﴾ He said: all of this is the speech of Jesus to his mother.

Ibn Ḥumayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from one who is not accused, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, concerning ﴿And if you see any human, say, "Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast, so I will not speak today to any human being."﴾: "for I will suffice you in speech."

Others said: that was only a sign for Mary and her son.

Those who said that:

al-Ḥasan related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah, concerning His saying, ﴿Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast﴾, he said, in some readings: "ṣamtā." That is because you would not meet an ignorant woman who says, "I have vowed as Mary vowed," meaning not to speak until night. Rather, God made that a sign for Mary and her son, and it is not permitted for anyone to vow silence for a day until night.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazīd related to us, saying: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah, and he recited ﴿Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast﴾, and he used to recite in the first reading: "ṣamtā," and it was only a sign that God sent for Mary and her son.

Others said: rather, she was fasting on that day, and the one who fasted in that era would abstain from food, drink and people's speech, so Mary was permitted to speak only this much on that day while she was fasting.

Those who said that:

Mūsā related to us, saying: ʿAmr related to us, saying: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī, concerning ﴿If you see any human﴾, who speaks to you, ﴿then say, "Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast, so I will not speak today to any human being."﴾ He said: whoever fasted in that era would not speak until evening, so she was told: "Do not add to this."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 27:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Then she brought him to her people, carrying him. They said, "O Mary, you have certainly done something unprecedented (shay'an fariyyan)."﴾

He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: So when Jesus said that to his mother, her soul was reassured and she submitted to the command of God. She carried him until she came to her people with him.

As related:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us from Ibn Ishaq, from someone who is not accused of falsehood, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: "He made her forget (i.e., Mary) the distress of the trial and the fear of people, what she had heard from the angels of the glad tidings about Jesus, until, when he (i.e., Jesus) spoke to her and the fulfilment of what God had promised her came to her, she carried him and then came with him to her people."

As for al-Suddi, regarding this he said:

Musa narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: "When she gave birth to him, Satan departed and informed the Children of Israel that Mary had given birth. So they came running and called out to her, ﴿Then she brought him to her people, carrying him.﴾"

* *

As for His saying, ﴿They said, "O Mary, you have certainly done something unprecedented."﴾

He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: When they saw Mary, and saw the child she had borne with her, they said to her, "O Mary, you have come with a matter that is strange, and you have produced a great innovation." Every doer who performs a deed well and excellently is said to have "afra" it (did it excellently). As the rajaz poet said:

"She has fed me dequl hujri (a poor kind of dates), / You used to make great claims (tafrin) about it, the fariyya."

[In Lisan al-Arab (dql): "dequl" is a kind of date, said to be the worst of its varieties. In Lisan al-Arab (fry): Tahdhib says: it is said of a man who is earnest and strong in a matter, "leave him to perform the afra and qadd." The Arabs say, "leave him to perform the afra" when he does a work or irrigation and does it well... Al-Farra' recited for Zurarah ibn Sa'b, addressing the woman from the Amir clan: "She has fed me dequl hawli (a year-old date), / Infested, wormy, hujri." / "You used to make great claims about it, the fariyya." That is, you used to speak much and magnify it. It is said: "So-and-so affra al-fara" when he brings a wonder in his work. Then he said: In the Mighty Revelation, in the story of Mary: "You have certainly done something unprecedented (shay'an fariyyan)." Al-Farra' said: al-fariy is a great matter, meaning you have done something great. It was also said: "You have come with shay'an fariyyan," meaning fabricated and invented.]

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Mentioning those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, both from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God, ﴿fariyyan﴾, he said: "Great."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding his saying, ﴿You have certainly done something unprecedented (shay'an fariyyan)﴾, he said: "Great."

Musa narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, ﴿You have certainly done something unprecedented﴾, he said: "Great."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from someone who is not accused of falsehood, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: When they saw her and saw him with her, they said, "O Mary, ﴿you have certainly done something unprecedented﴾": that is, the indecency that is not approached.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 28:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿O sister of Harun, your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother an unchaste woman﴾ (19:28).

The exegetes differed concerning the reason why she was addressed as "O sister of Harun," and who this Harun was whom God mentioned, and whom He informed that they attributed Mary to being his sister. Some of them said: she was addressed as ﴿O sister of Harun﴾ as an attribution by them to her of righteousness, because among the people of righteousness there were those called Harun, and this was not Harun the brother of Musa.

Mention of those who said this:

Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿O sister of Harun﴾, he said: He was a righteous man among the Children of Israel called Harun, so they likened her to him, and said: "O you who resemble Harun in righteousness."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿O sister of Harun, your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother an unchaste woman﴾, he said: She was from a household known for righteousness and not known for corruption. Among people there are those known for righteousness and who beget [children] by it, and others known for corruption and who beget [children] by it. Harun was a reformer, beloved among his kinsfolk, and he was not Harun the brother of Musa, but another Harun. He said: It was mentioned to us that forty thousand people attended his funeral on the day he died, all of them named Harun from among the Children of Israel.

Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sadaqah, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: It was reported to me that Ka'b said: Indeed His words ﴿O sister of Harun﴾ are not [about] Harun the brother of Musa. He said: 'A'ishah said to him: "You have lied." He said: O Mother of the Believers, if the Prophet ﷺ said it, then he is more knowledgeable and more informed; otherwise, I find that between them there are six hundred years. He said: So she fell silent.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿O sister of Harun﴾: "A name that coincided with a name; how many nations lay between Harun and them, many nations."

Abu Kurayb, Ibn al-Muthanna, Sufyan, Ibn WakI' and Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Idris al-Awdi narrated to us, saying: I heard my father mention, from Simak ibn Harb, from 'Alqamah ibn Wa'il, from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ sent me to the people of Najran. They said to me: "Do you not recite ﴿O sister of Harun﴾?" I said: "Yes, and you know what was between 'Isa and Musa." I returned to the Messenger of God ﷺ and informed him, and he said: "Why did you not inform them that they used to name themselves after their prophets and their righteous predecessors?"

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Bashir narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from 'Alqamah ibn Wa'il, from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, who said: The Prophet ﷺ sent me on some of his errands to the people of Najran. They said: "Does your prophet not claim that Harun, the sister of Maryam, is the brother of Musa?" I did not know how to answer them until I returned to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned that to him. He said: "Indeed they used to name [their children] after the names of those who were before them."

Others said: What was meant was Harun the brother of Musa, and Mary was attributed to being his sister because she was of his descendants, just as one says to a man of Tamim: "O brother of Tamim," and to a man of Mudar: "O brother of Mudar."

Mention of those who said this:

Musa narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿O sister of Harun﴾, he said: She was from the descendants of Harun the brother of Musa, and it is like when you say: "O brother of the sons of so-and-so."

Others said: Rather, he was a man among them, a wicked man openly known for wickedness, and they attributed her to him.

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter is what the report from the Messenger of God ﷺ that we have mentioned indicates, and that she was attributed to a man of her people.

* *

As for His words ﴿your father was not a man of evil﴾:

That is, your father was not a wicked man who committed abominations. ﴿Nor was your mother an unchaste woman﴾: that is, your mother was not a fornicator.

As related:

Musa narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿nor was your mother an unchaste woman﴾, he said: a fornicator. And He said ﴿bagiyy﴾ and did not say ﴿baghiyyah﴾, because that is something attributed to women and not to men, so it took the course of "a woman who is menstruating (ha'id)" and "a divorced woman (talaq)." Some of them compared that to their saying: "a new cloak (mil-hafah jadidah)" and "a woman slain (imra'at qatil)."

**On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: "So she pointed to him. They said, 'How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?'"** (19:29)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: When her people said that to her, she told them what 'Isa had instructed her to say to them. Then she pointed to 'Isa for them, [telling them] to speak to him.

As related:

* Musa narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When they said to her, "Your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother an unchaste woman" [19:28], she told them what Allah had commanded her to say. Then, when they wanted her to speak to him after that, she pointed to him, to 'Isa.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words, "So she pointed to him," that he said: She commanded them to speak to him.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from one whom no suspicion attaches to, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, regarding "So she pointed to him," that he said: She pointed to him, [telling them] to speak to him.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His words, "So she pointed to him," [meaning] to speak to him.

* * *

As for His words, "They said, 'How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?'"

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Her people said to her, "How can we speak to one who was found in the cradle?" In His words, "one who is in the cradle, a child," the kana (was) is used in the sense of completeness (tamam), not in the sense that requires a predicate. This is similar in meaning to the kana in His words, "Am I anything but a human messenger?" [17:93, cf. 17:93 "Hal kuntu illa basharan rasulan"]. The meaning there is: "Am I anything but a human, a messenger?" And [it means] "Have I been found or sent?" As Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma said:

*Zajartu 'alayhi hurratan arhabiyyatan... wa qad kana lawnu al-layli mithla al-arandaj*

I drove upon it a noble she-camel of Arhab,
while the color of the night was like the arandaj.

[Editor's note in the source: The verse is in Diwan Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma (Dar al-Kutub al-Misriyyah edition, with the commentary of Abu al-'Abbas Tha'lab, p. 323). The reading in the original is "ajarat," which is a distortion. His phrase "'alayhi" means "upon that road." "Hurrah" means a noble [she-camel]; "arhabiyyah" is attributed to Arhab, a clan of Hamdan, to whom noble racing camels are attributed; it is also said to be a place. al-Azhari said: It may be that Arhab was a stallion to whom the noble camels are attributed, because they are of his progeny. "Al-arandaj" and "al-yarandaj" refer to the black dye with which a hoof is blackened, or it is a black hide. That is, he drove this she-camel along this road, and the night was black like the arandaj.]

The meaning is: "And it had become or been found [black]." It is also said that by "the cradle" in this passage is meant the lap of his mother.

Those who said so:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding "one who is in the cradle, a child," that he said: The cradle is the lap.

Abu Ja'far [al-Tabari] said: We have already explained the meaning of the cradle earlier, with its evidences, so there is no need to repeat it in this place.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 30–31:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿He said, "Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet. And He has made me blessed wherever I am, and He has enjoined upon me prayer and zakah as long as I remain alive."﴾

Says He, may His remembrance be exalted: When the people of Mary said to her, ﴿How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?﴾ and they thought that this was from her as mockery of them, Jesus spoke on her behalf, saying: ﴿Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture.﴾ And they had become angry when she pointed to them toward Jesus, as is reported about them.

As follows:

* Musa narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When she pointed to them toward Jesus, they became angry and said: Her mockery of us, when she orders us to speak to this child, is more grievous to us than her fornication. ﴿They said, "How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?"﴾

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from one whom he does not suspect, from Wahb ibn Munabbih: ﴿They said, "How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?"﴾ So Jesus answered them, and said to them: ﴿Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet﴾... the verse.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿They said, "How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?" He said to them: "Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet"﴾ and he recited until he reached ﴿and has not made me a tyrant, wretched﴾. They said: Indeed, this is a great matter.

* It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say: ﴿How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?" He said, "Indeed, I am the servant of Allah"﴾. Jesus did not speak except at that time, when ﴿they said, "How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?"﴾

And His words ﴿He has given me the Scripture﴾.

Someone says: Did he receive the Scripture and revelation before he was created in his mother's womb? The meaning of that is contrary to what is supposed. Rather its meaning is: And He decreed, on the day He decreed the affairs of His creation, that He would give me the Scripture.

As follows:

* Bishr ibn Adam narrated to me, saying: al-Dahhak, meaning Ibn Mukhallad, narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Simak, from Ikrimah, regarding ﴿He has given me the Scripture﴾: He said: He decreed that He would give me the Scripture in what had passed.

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Sufyan informed us, from Simak, from Ikrimah, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture﴾: He said: It is the decree.

* al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Isra'il, from Simak, from Ikrimah, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture﴾: He said: He decreed that He would give me the Scripture.

* * *

And His words ﴿and made me a prophet﴾.

I have already explained the meaning of "prophet" (nabi) and the disagreement of those who differ about it, and the correct statement regarding it in our view, with its evidences, previously, in a way that suffices without repeating it.

Mujahid used to say, regarding the meaning of "prophet" alone, that:

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: The prophet alone is one who speaks and to whom revelation descends, but is not sent.

* * *

And His words ﴿and made me blessed﴾.

The interpreters differed regarding the meaning of that. Some of them said: its meaning is: and made me beneficial (naffa').

Those who said that:

* Sulayman ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad al-Talhi narrated to me, saying: al-Ala' narrated to us, from Aishah, wife of Layth, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and made me blessed﴾: He said: beneficial.

Others said: His blessing was the enjoining of good and the forbidding of evil.

Those who said that:

* Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Khunays al-Makhzumi narrated to us, saying: I heard Wuhayb ibn al-Ward, client of Banu Makhzum, say: A scholar met another scholar who was above him in knowledge, and he said to him: May Allah have mercy on you, what is the most manifest of my knowledge? He said: Enjoining good and forbidding evil, for it is the religion of Allah with which He sent His prophets to His servants. The jurists have agreed upon the saying of Allah: ﴿and made me blessed wherever I am﴾. It was said: What is its blessing? He said: Enjoining good and forbidding evil wherever it may be.

Others said the meaning of that is: He made me a teacher of good.

Those who said that:

* Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to us regarding ﴿and made me blessed wherever I am﴾: He said: a teacher of good.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿and made me blessed wherever I am﴾: He said: a teacher of good wherever I am.

* * *

And His words ﴿and has enjoined upon me prayer and zakah﴾.

He says: and He decreed that He would enjoin upon me prayer and zakah, meaning guarding the limits of prayer and establishing it as He prescribed it for me. Regarding zakah there are two meanings: the first is the zakah of wealth, that he pay it; the second is the purification of the body from the filth of sins, so its meaning would be: and He enjoined upon me abandoning sins and avoiding acts of disobedience.

* * *

And His words ﴿as long as I remain alive﴾.

He says: as long as I was alive and existing in this world. This shows that the meaning of zakah in this place is the purification of the body from sins, because what Jesus, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, is described as is that he did not store anything for tomorrow, so zakah of wealth would not be obligatory upon him, unless the zakah that was prescribed for him was the giving in charity of everything beyond his sustenance, in which case that would be a sound interpretation.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 30–31:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿He said, "Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet. And He has made me blessed wherever I am, and He has enjoined upon me prayer and zakah as long as I remain alive."﴾

Says He, may His remembrance be exalted: When the people of Mary said to her, ﴿How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?﴾ and they thought that this was from her as mockery of them, Jesus spoke on her behalf, saying: ﴿Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture.﴾ And they had become angry when she pointed to them toward Jesus, as is reported about them.

As follows:

* Musa narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When she pointed to them toward Jesus, they became angry and said: Her mockery of us, when she orders us to speak to this child, is more grievous to us than her fornication. ﴿They said, "How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?"﴾

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from one whom he does not suspect, from Wahb ibn Munabbih: ﴿They said, "How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?"﴾ So Jesus answered them, and said to them: ﴿Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet﴾... the verse.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿They said, "How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?" He said to them: "Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet"﴾ and he recited until he reached ﴿and has not made me a tyrant, wretched﴾. They said: Indeed, this is a great matter.

* It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say: ﴿How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?" He said, "Indeed, I am the servant of Allah"﴾. Jesus did not speak except at that time, when ﴿they said, "How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?"﴾

And His words ﴿He has given me the Scripture﴾.

Someone says: Did he receive the Scripture and revelation before he was created in his mother's womb? The meaning of that is contrary to what is supposed. Rather its meaning is: And He decreed, on the day He decreed the affairs of His creation, that He would give me the Scripture.

As follows:

* Bishr ibn Adam narrated to me, saying: al-Dahhak, meaning Ibn Mukhallad, narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Simak, from Ikrimah, regarding ﴿He has given me the Scripture﴾: He said: He decreed that He would give me the Scripture in what had passed.

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Sufyan informed us, from Simak, from Ikrimah, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture﴾: He said: It is the decree.

* al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Isra'il, from Simak, from Ikrimah, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture﴾: He said: He decreed that He would give me the Scripture.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verses 32–33:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And dutiful to my mother; and He has not made me arrogant or wretched. (32) And peace is upon me the day I was born, and the day I die, and the day I am raised alive.﴾ (33)

Our Lord, the Exalted, says, reporting the words of Jesus to his people: "And made me blessed" and "dutiful" — that is, He made me dutiful to my mother. Al-barr is the same as al-bar (the dutiful one). It is said: he is barr (dutiful) to his father, and bar (dutiful) toward him. The readers of the major cities (qurra' al-amsar) recited this letter with a fatha on the ba'. It is narrated from Abu Nuhayk that:

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, who said: Abd al-Mu'min narrated to us, from Abu Nuhayk, that he recited ﴿and dutiful to my mother﴾ as part of the words of Jesus, peace be upon him. Abu Nuhayk said: He enjoined upon me the prayer, the zakat and dutifulness to the parents, just as He enjoined it upon me.

So it seems that Abu Nuhayk understood the meaning of the statement ﴿and dutiful to my mother﴾ to be a report from Jesus about the command of God to him regarding it, just as His words ﴿and He has enjoined upon me the prayer and zakat﴾ are a report from him about God's command to him concerning those. According to this view, the accusative of al-barr must be governed by the sense of "enjoining" in it, because the prayer and zakat, though they are in the genitive in form, are in the accusative in meaning on account of being objects of it.

* *

As for His words ﴿and He has not made me arrogant or wretched﴾:

He says: and He has not made me arrogant toward God in what He commanded me and forbade me, wretched; rather He made me submissive to His obedience and made me humble.

As related:

* Bishr narrated to us, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that he, meaning Jesus, used to say: "Ask me, for my heart is soft, and I am small in myself because of the humility God has given me."

* And Bishr narrated to us, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿and dutiful to my mother and He has not made me arrogant or wretched﴾: It was mentioned to us that a woman saw the son of Mary giving life to the dead and healing the blind and the leper, among signs which God empowered him to perform and permitted him to do. She said: "Blessed is the womb that bore you, and the breast from which you were nursed." The Prophet of God, the son of Mary, replied to her: "Blessed is the one who recites the Book of God and follows what is in it, ﴿and He has not made me arrogant or wretched﴾."

* Al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to us, from Abd Allah ibn Wahid Abu Raja', from some of the people of knowledge, who said: You will not find a disobedient son (aqq) except that you will find him arrogant and wretched. Then he recited ﴿and dutiful to my mother and He has not made me arrogant or wretched﴾. He said: And you will not find one who mistreats his slaves except that you will find him conceited and boastful; then he recited ﴿Indeed, God does not love whoever is conceited and boastful﴾ [4:36].

* *

As for His words ﴿And peace is upon me the day I was born, and the day I die, and the day I am raised alive﴾:

He says: and security from God for me from Satan and his troops on the day I was born, that they should not inflict upon me what they inflict upon those who are born at birth, by striking him; and on the day I die, from the terror of the final moment; and on the day I am raised alive on the Day of Resurrection, that the terror which people feel upon witnessing the horrors of that day should not reach me.

As related:

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from one who is not accused, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, concerning ﴿And peace is upon me the day I was born, and the day I die, and the day I am raised alive﴾: He informs them in the account of his own story, that he has no father and that he will die and then be raised alive. God, blessed and exalted, says ﴿That is Jesus, son of Mary, the word of truth about which they dispute﴾ [19:34].

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 34:

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That is Jesus, son of Mary—a statement of truth about which they dispute.﴾ (19:34)

Exalted is He says: This is what I have explained to you of his description and informed you of his account, concerning the boy whom Mary carried: he is Jesus son of Mary, and this description is his description and this report is his report. And ﴿a statement of truth﴾ means that this report which I have related to you is a statement of truth, and the speech I have recited to you is the word and report of God, not any other report, in which there is no doubt, suspicion, addition or subtraction. Thus God, Exalted is He, says: So say about Jesus, O people, this statement which God has told you about him, not what the Jews said, who claimed that he was born out of wedlock and that he was a sorcerer and a liar, nor what the Christians said, that he was a son of God. God has not taken a son, and it is not befitting for Him to do so.

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) have said things similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿That is Jesus, son of Mary, a statement of the truth﴾: "The truth" is God.

Yahya ibn Ibrahim al-Mas'udi told me, saying: my father told me, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, who said: They used to recite this word in the reading of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud) as ﴿alladhi fihi yamtarun﴾, and he said: "the Word of God."

If the interpretation of that were directed to: "That is Jesus son of Mary, the true statement," meaning "that true statement," and then the alif and lam were removed from "the statement" and it was made an annexation to "the truth," as is said: ﴿Indeed, this is the true certainty﴾ (56:95), and as is said: ﴿the promise of truth which they were promised﴾ (46:16), it would be a correct interpretation.

The reciters differed in reading this. The majority of the reciters of the Hijaz and Iraq read ﴿qawlu al-haqq﴾ with the nominative "qawl," in accordance with the meaning I have described, and they took it grammatically as following Jesus, as an epithet for him. In my view, the grammatical analysis is not as those claimed who said it is nominative as an epithet for Jesus, unless "qawl" means "word" (kalima), as we mentioned from Ibrahim's interpretation of it in that way; then it would be correct for it to be an epithet for Jesus. Otherwise, its nominative is, in my view, governed by an implied element: "this is the statement of truth," as a new inceptive sentence (mubtada'), because the report about the story of Jesus and his mother has ended at His saying ﴿That is Jesus, son of Mary﴾, and then the report begins anew, that the truth concerning what the nations dispute about the matter of Jesus is this statement which God has told His servants about him, and not other than it. 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud and Abdullah ibn Amir read it in the accusative, and it seems they intended by it the verbal noun: "That is Jesus son of Mary, a true statement," then the alif and lam were introduced into it. As for what is reported from Ibn Mas'ud's reading ﴿Dhalika Isa ibn Maryam qalu al-haqq﴾, it means "qawl al-haqq," like al-'ab and al-'ayb, and al-dhaam and al-dhaym.

Abu Ja'far said: The correct reading in this, in our view, is the nominative, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters upon it. As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿about which they dispute﴾, it means: about which they quarrel and differ, from the expression "I disputed (mariitu) with so-and-so," meaning: when I argued with him and contended with him.

The exegetes have said things similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿That is Jesus, son of Mary, a statement of truth about which they dispute﴾: The Jews and Christians disputed about him. As for the Jews, they claimed he was a sorcerer and a liar; as for the Christians, they claimed he was the son of God, and the third of three, and a god. They all lied, but he was the servant of God and His messenger, and His word and His spirit.

Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying ﴿about which they dispute﴾: They differed. One group said: he is the servant of God and His prophet, so they believed in him. Another group said: he is God. Another group said: he is the son of God, may He be exalted far above what they say. He said: That is His saying ﴿so the factions differed among themselves﴾ (43:65). And what is in az-Zukhruf: Diqyus, Nastur and Mar Ya'qub. One of them said, when God raised Jesus: he is God. The other said: the son of God. Another said: the word of God and His servant. The two who said "my word is more like yours, and yours like mine, than the word of this one; come, let us fight them." They fought them and trampled Israel upon them, and they drove out four men from among them, each group expelling its scholar. They disputed about Jesus when he was raised. One of them said: he is God, who descended to earth, gave life to whomever he gave life, caused to die whomever he caused to die, then ascended to heaven; these are the Nestorians. The two said: you lie. Then one of the two said to the other: say about him. He said: he is the third of three: God is a god, he is a god, and his mother is a god; these are the Israelites, the kings of the Christians. The fourth said: you lie, he is the servant of God, His messenger, His spirit and His word; these are the Muslims. Each man had followers according to what he said, so they fought, and the Muslims were overcome. That is God's saying: ﴿and kill those who enjoin justice from among the people﴾ (3:21). Qatada said: they are those whom God mentioned: ﴿so the factions differed﴾; they differed about him and became factions.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verses 35–36:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿It is not for God to take a son; glory be to Him. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ (35) ﴿Indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.﴾ (36)

His words, may His remembrance be exalted, mean: Certainly those who said, "Jesus is the son of God," have disbelieved, and they have uttered a monstrous slander against Him. It is not fitting for God to take a son; that is not suitable for Him and does not come to be. Rather, everything other than Him is His creation. This is similar to the words of Amr ibn Ahmar:

"On the summit of a smooth rock of an 'anqa' lofty and elevated, no plain or mountain can be sought beyond it."[[The verse is by Amr ibn Ahmar (Lisan: ʿnq). He said: As for the verse of Ibn Ahmar: "On the summit of a smooth rock of an 'anqa' lofty and elevated, no plain or mountain can be sought beyond it," it describes a mountain. He means: it is not fitting that there be above it any plain or mountain more impregnable than it. End. I say: al-khalqa' is the smooth rock; al-'anqa' is that which is far in the sky; and al-mushrifa is the high one. The narration of the second hemistich in the original is: "no plain or mountain is fitting beyond it."

.]]

And the "an" in His words ﴿an yattakhidha﴾ is in a nominative position as the subject of kana (it is).

* *

As for His words, ﴿subhanahu﴾:

He says: Exalted and absolved is God, and free from what the disbelievers who say, "Jesus is the son of God," attribute to Him. As for His words, ﴿When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ His majestic praise says: God only began the creation of Jesus as a beginning, and brought him into being without a stallion mounting his mother. Rather, He said to him, ﴿"Be," and it is,﴾ because that is how He originates and invents things. He only says, when He decrees the creation or bringing into being of a thing: "Be," and it is existent and newly come into being. Its creation is not difficult for Him, since He does not create it with toil and hardship, nor bring it into being with effort and strain.

* *

As for His words ﴿Indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him﴾:

The readers differed over the recitation of this. The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra recited it ﴿wa-anna Allaha rabbi wa-rabbukum﴾ (with fath on "anna"). The grammarians differed over the reason for the fath of "anna" when it is opened. Some Kufan grammarians said: it is opened in response to (the preceding word) Jesus and as a conjunction with him, meaning: that is Jesus son of Mary, and that God is my Lord and your Lord. If that is the case, "anna" is in the nominative position, but it is in the sense of a genitive, as He said: ﴿That is because your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly﴾. He said: If it were opened on His words ﴿and He has enjoined upon me﴾ as "that God," it would be a valid reading. Some Basran grammarians said: this has also been reported from Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala', who was among those who recited it with fath: "anna" is opened in the sense of ﴿and He has decreed﴾ that God is my Lord and your Lord. The majority of the Kufan readers recited it ﴿wa-inna Allah﴾ with kasra on "inna," in the sense of coordination with His words ﴿fa-innama yaqulu lahu﴾. It is reported from Ubayy ibn Ka'b that he recited it ﴿fa-innama yaqulu lahu kun fa-yakun inna Allaha rabbi wa-rabbukum﴾ without the waw.

Abu Ja'far said: The reading we choose in this is the kasra, as a new beginning. When it is read thus, it has no grammatical position. It is also possible that it is a conjunction with the "inna" that accompanies His words ﴿He said: Indeed I am the servant of God; He has given me the Scripture ... and indeed God is my Lord and your Lord﴾. Whoever among those who read it with naṣb (accusative) said: it is in the accusative as a conjunction with "the Scripture," meaning: He has given me the Scripture and given me that God is my Lord and your Lord, that would be a good interpretation. The meaning of the speech is: I and you, O people, all are servants of God, so worship Him alone, to the exclusion of anything else.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said similarly to what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from one who is not suspected, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: He charged them when He informed them about Himself, his birth, his death, and his resurrection: ﴿Indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.﴾ That is, I and you are servants of God, so worship Him and do not worship other than Him.

* *

As for His words ﴿This is a straight path﴾:

He says: This which I have enjoined upon you, and informed you that God commanded me with, is the straight path, whoever follows it is saved, and whoever travels it is guided, because it is the religion of God which He commanded His prophets with.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verses 35–36:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿It is not for God to take a son; glory be to Him. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ (35) ﴿Indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.﴾ (36)

His words, may His remembrance be exalted, mean: Certainly those who said, "Jesus is the son of God," have disbelieved, and they have uttered a monstrous slander against Him. It is not fitting for God to take a son; that is not suitable for Him and does not come to be. Rather, everything other than Him is His creation. This is similar to the words of Amr ibn Ahmar:

"On the summit of a smooth rock of an 'anqa' lofty and elevated, no plain or mountain can be sought beyond it."[[The verse is by Amr ibn Ahmar (Lisan: ʿnq). He said: As for the verse of Ibn Ahmar: "On the summit of a smooth rock of an 'anqa' lofty and elevated, no plain or mountain can be sought beyond it," it describes a mountain. He means: it is not fitting that there be above it any plain or mountain more impregnable than it. End. I say: al-khalqa' is the smooth rock; al-'anqa' is that which is far in the sky; and al-mushrifa is the high one. The narration of the second hemistich in the original is: "no plain or mountain is fitting beyond it."

.]]

And the "an" in His words ﴿an yattakhidha﴾ is in a nominative position as the subject of kana (it is).

* *

As for His words, ﴿subhanahu﴾:

He says: Exalted and absolved is God, and free from what the disbelievers who say, "Jesus is the son of God," attribute to Him. As for His words, ﴿When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ His majestic praise says: God only began the creation of Jesus as a beginning, and brought him into being without a stallion mounting his mother. Rather, He said to him, ﴿"Be," and it is,﴾ because that is how He originates and invents things. He only says, when He decrees the creation or bringing into being of a thing: "Be," and it is existent and newly come into being. Its creation is not difficult for Him, since He does not create it with toil and hardship, nor bring it into being with effort and strain.

* *

As for His words ﴿Indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him﴾:

The readers differed over the recitation of this. The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra recited it ﴿wa-anna Allaha rabbi wa-rabbukum﴾ (with fath on "anna"). The grammarians differed over the reason for the fath of "anna" when it is opened. Some Kufan grammarians said: it is opened in response to (the preceding word) Jesus and as a conjunction with him, meaning: that is Jesus son of Mary, and that God is my Lord and your Lord. If that is the case, "anna" is in the nominative position, but it is in the sense of a genitive, as He said: ﴿That is because your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly﴾. He said: If it were opened on His words ﴿and He has enjoined upon me﴾ as "that God," it would be a valid reading. Some Basran grammarians said: this has also been reported from Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala', who was among those who recited it with fath: "anna" is opened in the sense of ﴿and He has decreed﴾ that God is my Lord and your Lord. This is a straight path.﴾ That is, I and you are servants of God, so worship Him and do not worship other than Him.

He says: This which I have enjoined upon you, and informed you that God commanded me with, is the straight path, whoever follows it is saved, and whoever travels it is guided, because it is the religion of God which He commanded His prophets with.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 37:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then the factions differed among themselves, so woe to those who disbelieve from the scene of a great Day.﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: The disputants differed concerning Jesus, and they became factions scattered among his people.

As related:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to me, saying: Warqa related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿Then the factions differed among themselves﴾, he said: the People of the Book.

⁕ al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿Then the factions differed among themselves﴾: It was mentioned to us that when the son of Mary was raised up, the Children of Israel selected four of their jurists and said to the first: "What do you say about Jesus?" He said: "He is God, who descended to the earth, created what he created, gave life to whom he gave life, then ascended to the heaven." Some people followed him in this, and thus the Ya'qubiyya (Jacobites) became a sect among the Christians. The other three said: "We testify that you are a liar." They then said to the second: "What do you say about Jesus?" He said: "He is the son of God." Some people followed him in this, and thus the Nestorians became a sect among the Christians. The two others said: "We testify that you are a liar." They then said to the third: "What do you say about Jesus?" He said: "He is God, and his mother is God, and God is God." Some people followed him in this, and thus the Israelites became a sect among the Christians. The fourth said: "I testify that you are a liar, but he is the servant of God and His messenger, the word of God and His spirit." The people then disputed, and the Muslim man said: "I adjure you by God, do you not know that Jesus used to eat food, and that Almighty and Blessed God does not eat food?" They said: "Yes, by God." He said: "Do you know that Jesus used to sleep?" They said: "Yes, by God." He said: Thus the Muslim overcame them in argument. He said: Then the people fought one another. It was related to us that the Ya'qubiyya prevailed that day, and the Muslims were afflicted. So God revealed in that regard the Qur'an: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of God and kill the prophets without right, and kill those who enjoin justice among the people—give them tidings of a painful punishment.﴾

⁕ al-Hasan related to us, saying: Ishaq informed us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿Then the factions differed among themselves﴾: they differed concerning him and became factions.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So woe to those who disbelieve from the scene of a great Day﴾

He says: So a valley in Hell called "Wayl" is for those who disbelieve in God, among those who claim that Jesus is God's son, and others who disbelieve in Him, from their witnessing of a great Day, the greatness of which is immense, and that is the Day of Resurrection.

Qatada used to interpret that as follows:

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, who said, regarding God's saying: ﴿So woe to those who disbelieve from the scene of a great Day﴾: They will witness a terrible, great horror.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 38:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Hear them and see them the day they come to Us; but the wrongdoers today are in manifest error.﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says, informing about the state of the disbelievers in Him, who set up rivals to Him and claim that He has a son, on the day of their coming before Him in the Hereafter: "If they were blind in the world to seeing the truth and to looking at the proofs of God that indicate His oneness, and deaf to hearing His revealed verses and what His messengers called them to in them of affirming His oneness, and what He sent His prophets with, then how well would they hear and how well would they see on the day of their arrival before their Lord in the Hereafter, when hearing and seeing will not benefit them."

Similar to what we have said on this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿Hear them and see them﴾: "That, by God, is the Day of Resurrection. They will hear when hearing will not benefit them, and they will see when sight will not benefit them."

Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿Hear them and see them﴾, he said: "How well they hear and how well they see."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Abu Sufyan related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said regarding ﴿Hear them and see them the day they come to Us﴾: "On the Day of Resurrection."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, who said: ﴿Hear﴾ their speech today, ﴿and see﴾ how He will deal with them ﴿the day they come to Us﴾.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿Hear them and see them the day they come to Us﴾: "This is the Day of Resurrection. As for the world, no, for there was a veil over their sight and deafness in their ears in the world. When the Day of Resurrection came, they saw and heard but did not benefit." And he recited ﴿Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us that we may do righteousness; indeed, we are certain.﴾

And His words ﴿but the wrongdoers today are in manifest error﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: "But the disbelievers, who ascribed to Him what is not befitting of Him and fabricated lies against Him, today in the world, are in manifest error." He means: in departure from the path of truth, and taking a course not upright, clearly deviating from the way of right guidance and direction, for whoever contemplates it and reflects upon it, and is thus guided to his rectitude.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 39:

The explanation of the words of His, the Exalted: ﴿And warn them of the Day of Regret, when the matter will be decided, while they are in heedlessness and they do not believe﴾ (19:39).

He, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And warn these polytheists, O Muhammad, of the Day of their regret and remorse, for what they neglected concerning the right of God, and when the dwellings of the Garden will be inherited by the people of faith in God and obedience to Him, and they will be brought into the dwellings of the people of faith in God from the Fire, and both groups will be certain of eternal abiding and of a life after which there is no death. So, how great is their regret and remorse!

And the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, saying: Abu al-Za'ra' narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah, in a story he mentioned, saying: "There is no soul but that it looks at a house in the Garden and a house in the Fire, and that is the Day of Regret. The people of the Fire see the house that God had prepared for them had they believed, and it is said to them: Had you believed and done righteous deeds, this which you see in the Garden would have been yours. So regret seizes them. And the people of the Garden see the house that is in the Fire, and it is said: Had it not been that God had bestowed His favour upon you..."

Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Death will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and will be stopped between the Garden and the Fire, as if it were a white-speckled ram. It will be said: O people of the Garden, do you recognize this? They will crane their necks and look, and they will say: Yes, this is Death. Then it will be said: O people of the Fire, do you recognize this? They will crane their necks and look, and they will say: Yes, this is Death. Then it will be commanded, and it will be slaughtered. Then it will be said: O people of the Garden, eternity without death; and O people of the Fire, eternity without death." He said: Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) recited: ﴿And warn them of the Day of Regret, when the matter will be decided, while they are in heedlessness and they do not believe﴾, and he pointed with his hand toward this world.

Ubayd ibn Asbat ibn Muhammad narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning this verse, ﴿And warn them of the Day of Regret﴾, he said: "It will be called out: O people of the Garden! So they will crane their necks and look. Then it will be called out: O people of the Fire! So they will crane their necks and look. It will be said: Do you know death? He said: They will say: No. He said: Death will be brought in the form of a white-speckled ram, and it will be said: This is Death. Then it will be seized and slaughtered. He said: Then it will call out: O people of the Fire, eternity without death; and O people of the Garden, eternity without death." He said: Then he recited: ﴿And warn them of the Day of Regret, when the matter will be decided﴾.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said, concerning His words ﴿And warn them of the Day of Regret﴾: God will fashion Death in the form of a white-speckled ram, and it will be slaughtered. He said: The people of the Fire will despair of death, so they will not hope for it, and regret will seize them because of eternal abiding in the Fire. In it also is the Greatest Terror. And the people of the Garden will hope for death, so they will not fear it, and they will feel secure from death, which is the Greatest Terror, because they will abide forever in the Garden. Ibn Juraij said: The people of the Fire will be gathered when Death is slaughtered, while both groups look on. That is His words ﴿when the matter will be decided﴾. He said: The slaughtering of Death ﴿while they are in heedlessness﴾.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from his father, that he informed him that he heard Ubayd ibn 'Umayr in his storytelling say: Death will be brought as if it were an animal, and it will be slaughtered while the people look on.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words "And warn them of the Day of Regret": It is the Day of Resurrection. And he recited: ﴿lest a soul should say: Alas for my regret over what I neglected concerning the right of God﴾.

Ali narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿And warn them of the Day of Regret﴾: It is among the names of the Day of Resurrection, which God has magnified and warned His servants of.

* *

And His words ﴿when the matter will be decided﴾:

He says: when the judgment concerning the people of the Fire to abide in it forever, and concerning the people of the Garden to remain in it eternally, has been completed, through the slaughtering of Death.

* *

And His words ﴿while they are in heedlessness﴾:

He says: while these polytheists are in heedlessness of what God will do with them on the Day when they come out to Him from their graves, of His making them abide forever in Hell, and His giving their dwellings in the Garden to others. ﴿and they do not believe﴾: He, the Exalted, says: and they do not affirm the Resurrection and the Rising, and God's recompense for them for their evil deeds, by what He has informed that He will recompense them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 40–42:

On the interpretation of His words, "Indeed, We will inherit the earth and whoever is on it, and to Us they will be returned" (19:40):

He, exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Do not let the denial of these polytheists grieve you, O Muhammad, regarding what you have brought them of the truth. For to Us is their return, their final destination, and the final destination of all creation other than them. We are the inheritors of the earth and of whoever is upon it of mankind, when they perish from it, and it remains with no owner other than Us. Then upon Us is the recompense of every doer of them for his deeds, at his return to Us: the good-doer for his goodness, and the evildoer for his evil.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, "And mention in the Book Abraham. Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet" (19:41), "When he said to his father, 'O my father, why do you worship that which does not hear and does not see and cannot benefit you at all?'" (19:42):

He, exalted is He, says to His Prophet: "And mention" O Muhammad in the Book of God "Abraham," the Friend of the Most Merciful. So recount to these polytheists his story and the story of his father. "Indeed, he was a man of truth" means: he was of those who were truthful in his speech, his reports and his promises, never lying. And "ṣiddīq" is the form fa‘īl derived from "truth" (ṣidq).

We have already explained this earlier, in a way that suffices without repeating it in this place. "A prophet" means: God had informed him (nabba'ahu) and revealed to him.

* *

As for His words, "When he said to his father":

It means: mention him when he said to his father, "O my father, why do you worship that which does not hear" — that is, what do you gain by worshipping an idol which does not hear, "and does not see" anything, "and cannot benefit you at all" — that is, cannot ward off any harm from you. It is merely a fashioned image which neither harms nor benefits. He means: what do you do by worshipping one with these attributes? Worship the One who, when you call upon Him, hears your supplication, and when you are surrounded, sees you and helps you, and when harm befalls you, repels it from you.

The grammarians differed regarding the reason for the attaching of the hā' in His words "yā abatī" (O my father). Some grammarians of Basra said: when you stop on it you say "yā abah," and it is a hā' that was added, as in your saying "yā ummah" (O my mother), and then one says "yā umm" when connected. But since the word "ab" (father) has two letters, it was as though it were deficient, so the hā' became obligatory, and the yā' came to be as if after it. Therefore they said "yā abatu aqbil" (O father, come near), and the tā' was made the mark of the feminine. The truncation of "abā" to "ab" is permissible, since in meaning you may address what you attribute to yourself as ending in a ḍamma, as in the Arabs' saying, "yā rabbi ighfir lī" (O my Lord, forgive me). And in the Qur'an one stops, "yā abatah" in the Book.

Some Arabs stop on the hā' with a tā'. Some grammarians of Kufa said: the hā' with "abah" and "ummah" is a hā' of pause, which has become frequent in their speech until it resembles the hā' of the feminine, and they have added the genitive construction to it. Whoever seeks the genitive construction uses the tā' alone, because one then seeks a yā' after it, and the hā' is then none other than a tā', as in your saying "yā abat" only. Whoever says "yā abah" is the one who stops with the hā', because he does not seek a yā' after it. Whoever says "yā abatā" stops on it with a tā', and it is permissible with a hā'. As for the tā', it is for the sake of the vocative alif (alif al-nudbah), so the hā' became a tā' for that reason. Stopping with a hā' is rare, except for one who says, "yā umaymata nāṣibi" [this is part of a verse by al-Nābigha (cited earlier at 14:21), which is: "Leave me to a worry, O Umaymah, troubled one... and a night whose stars are slow, which I endure"], making this fatḥah a fatḥah of truncation, as though this were the end of the noun. He said: this is rare.
