On the interpretation of His words, "Indeed, We will inherit the earth and whoever is on it, and to Us they will be returned" (19:40):

He, exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Do not let the denial of these polytheists grieve you, O Muhammad, regarding what you have brought them of the truth. For to Us is their return, their final destination, and the final destination of all creation other than them. We are the inheritors of the earth and of whoever is upon it of mankind, when they perish from it, and it remains with no owner other than Us. Then upon Us is the recompense of every doer of them for his deeds, at his return to Us: the good-doer for his goodness, and the evildoer for his evil.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, "And mention in the Book Abraham. Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet" (19:41), "When he said to his father, 'O my father, why do you worship that which does not hear and does not see and cannot benefit you at all?'" (19:42):

He, exalted is He, says to His Prophet: "And mention" O Muhammad in the Book of God "Abraham," the Friend of the Most Merciful. So recount to these polytheists his story and the story of his father. "Indeed, he was a man of truth" means: he was of those who were truthful in his speech, his reports and his promises, never lying. And "ṣiddīq" is the form fa‘īl derived from "truth" (ṣidq).

We have already explained this earlier, in a way that suffices without repeating it in this place. "A prophet" means: God had informed him (nabba'ahu) and revealed to him.

* *

As for His words, "When he said to his father":

It means: mention him when he said to his father, "O my father, why do you worship that which does not hear" — that is, what do you gain by worshipping an idol which does not hear, "and does not see" anything, "and cannot benefit you at all" — that is, cannot ward off any harm from you. It is merely a fashioned image which neither harms nor benefits. He means: what do you do by worshipping one with these attributes? Worship the One who, when you call upon Him, hears your supplication, and when you are surrounded, sees you and helps you, and when harm befalls you, repels it from you.

The grammarians differed regarding the reason for the attaching of the hā' in His words "yā abatī" (O my father). Some grammarians of Basra said: when you stop on it you say "yā abah," and it is a hā' that was added, as in your saying "yā ummah" (O my mother), and then one says "yā umm" when connected. But since the word "ab" (father) has two letters, it was as though it were deficient, so the hā' became obligatory, and the yā' came to be as if after it. Therefore they said "yā abatu aqbil" (O father, come near), and the tā' was made the mark of the feminine. The truncation of "abā" to "ab" is permissible, since in meaning you may address what you attribute to yourself as ending in a ḍamma, as in the Arabs' saying, "yā rabbi ighfir lī" (O my Lord, forgive me). And in the Qur'an one stops, "yā abatah" in the Book.

Some Arabs stop on the hā' with a tā'. Some grammarians of Kufa said: the hā' with "abah" and "ummah" is a hā' of pause, which has become frequent in their speech until it resembles the hā' of the feminine, and they have added the genitive construction to it. Whoever seeks the genitive construction uses the tā' alone, because one then seeks a yā' after it, and the hā' is then none other than a tā', as in your saying "yā abat" only. Whoever says "yā abah" is the one who stops with the hā', because he does not seek a yā' after it. Whoever says "yā abatā" stops on it with a tā', and it is permissible with a hā'. As for the tā', it is for the sake of the vocative alif (alif al-nudbah), so the hā' became a tā' for that reason. Stopping with a hā' is rare, except for one who says, "yā umaymata nāṣibi" [this is part of a verse by al-Nābigha (cited earlier at 14:21), which is: "Leave me to a worry, O Umaymah, troubled one... and a night whose stars are slow, which I endure"], making this fatḥah a fatḥah of truncation, as though this were the end of the noun. He said: this is rare.

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: "O my father, indeed there has come to me of knowledge that which has not come to you, so follow me; I will guide you to a path, even and straight" (19:43).

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: Abraham said to his father, "O my father, indeed God has given me of knowledge that which He has not given you, so follow me": that is, accept my counsel. "I will guide you to a path, even and straight": that is, I will show you the right way of the straight road, which you will not go astray in if you keep to it, and it is the religion of God, in which there is no crookedness.

The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿O my father, do not worship Satan. Indeed, Satan has been disobedient to the Most Merciful﴾ (19:44)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "O my father, do not worship Satan. Indeed, Satan has been disobedient to Allah." The word *'aṣiyy* (disobedient) means one who possesses disobedience, just as *'alīm* (knowing) means one who possesses knowledge. Some of the people of Arabic grammar (*ahl al-'arabiyya*, the grammarians) said: *'aṣiyy* is *'āṣi* (the disobedient), *'alīm* is *'ālim* (the knowing), and *'arīf* is *'ārif* (the one who knows). They cited in support of their view the verse of Ṭarīf ibn Tamīm al-'Anbarī:

*Or whenever a tribe arrives at 'Ukāẓ, they send to me their 'arīf (leader), who seeks to discern (the matter)*

[The verse is cited in (Lisan al-'Arab, root *'-r-f*), attributed to Ṭarīf ibn Mālik al-'Anbarī, and it is said Ṭarīf ibn 'Amr. He said: *al-'arīf* and *al-'ārif* have the same meaning, like *'alīm* and *'ālim*. Sibawayh said: it is *fa'īl* in the sense of *fā'il*, as in the phrase *ḍarīb qidāḥ* (an arrow-maker). Its plural is *'urafā'*.]

They said: he said *'arīfuhum* while meaning *'ārifuhum* (their knower), and Allah knows best.

* *

The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿O my father, indeed I fear that a punishment from the Most Merciful will touch you, so you would become a friend of Satan﴾ (19:45)

He says: "O my father, indeed I know that if you die upon worshipping Satan, a punishment from the punishment of Allah will touch you, ﴿so you would become a friend of Satan﴾," meaning: you would become his friend apart from Allah, and Allah would disown you, and you would perish. The word "fear" (*khawf*) in this context means "knowledge," just as the word *khashya* (dread) means knowledge in His words: ﴿So We feared that it would overwhelm them with rebellion and disbelief﴾ (18:80).

* *

The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿He said, "Do you turn away from my gods, O Abraham? If you do not desist, I will surely stone you, so leave me for a long time"﴾ (19:46)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: the father of Abraham said to Abraham when Abraham called him to worship Allah, to abandon the worship of Satan, and to disown the idols and images: ﴿Do you turn away from my gods﴾, O Abraham, ﴿if you do not desist﴾ from mentioning them with evil ﴿I will surely stone you﴾, meaning: I will stone you with words, which is abuse and foul speech.

The people of interpretation (*ahl al-ta'wil*) have said what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

- Musa narrated to us, he said: 'Amr narrated to us, he said: Asbaṭ narrated to us, from al-Suddī, regarding ﴿He said, "Do you turn away from my gods, O Abraham? If you do not desist, I will surely stone you"﴾: with insult and speech.

- Al-Qāsim narrated to us, he said: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, he said: Ḥajjāj reported to me, he said: Ibn Juraij said, regarding His words ﴿If you do not desist, I will surely stone you﴾: with speech; I will curse you.

- It was reported to me from al-Ḥusayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'āḏ say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulaymān informed us, he said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say regarding His words ﴿I will surely stone you﴾: meaning, stoning with speech.

As for His words ﴿so leave me for a long time (*malīyyan*)﴾, the people of interpretation differed regarding its meaning. Some of them said: the meaning of that is: leave me for a long time and an age. They traced the meaning of *al-millī* to a long span of time, which is the lengthy part of it.

Mention of those who said that:

- Muḥammad ibn Bashshār narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, he said: Abu Dāwūd narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Abi al-Waḍḥ narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Karīm, from Mujāhid, regarding His words ﴿and leave me *malīyyan*﴾: an age.

- Muḥammad ibn 'Amr reported to me, he said: Abu 'Āṣim narrated to us, he said: 'Īsā narrated to us; and al-Ḥārith reported to me, he said: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, he said: Waraqā narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, regarding His words ﴿*malīyyan*﴾: a while.

- al-Qāsim narrated to us, he said: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, he said: Ḥajjāj reported to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujāhid, the like of it.

- Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazīd narrated to us, he said: Sa'īd narrated to us, from Qatādah, from al-Ḥasan, regarding ﴿and leave me *malīyyan*﴾: a long time.

- al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzāq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Ḥasan, regarding His words ﴿and leave me *malīyyan*﴾: a long time.

- Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, he said: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, regarding ﴿and leave me *malīyyan*﴾: he says: an age, and the *malī* age.

- Ibn Bashshār narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, he said: Isrā'īl narrated to us, from Abu Ḥuṣayn, from Sa'īd ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿and leave me *malīyyan*﴾: an age.

- Mūsā narrated to us, he said: 'Amr narrated to us, Asbaṭ narrated to us, from al-Suddī, regarding ﴿and leave me *malīyyan*﴾: forever.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: leave me *sawiyyan* (whole), safe from my punishment of you. They traced the meaning of *al-millī* to the saying of people: "So-and-so is *millī* with this matter," when he is capable of it and rich in it. It was as if the meaning of the speech, in their view, was: leave me, while your honor is abundant from my punishment, and your body is safe from my harm.

Mention of those who said that:

- 'Alī ibn Dāwūd reported to me, he said: 'Abdullāh ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, he said: Mu'āwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ reported to me, from 'Alī ibn Abi Ṭalḥa, from Ibn 'Abbās, regarding ﴿and leave me *malīyyan*﴾: he says: keep away from me *sawiyyan*.

- Muḥammad ibn Sa'd reported to me, he said: my father reported to me, he said: my paternal uncle reported to me, he said: my father reported to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbās, regarding His words ﴿and leave me *malīyyan*﴾: he said: keep away from me, safe, before my punishment reaches you.

- Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazīd narrated to us, he said: Sa'īd narrated to us, from Qatādah, regarding His words ﴿and leave me *malīyyan*﴾: he said: safe.

- al-Ḥasan narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzāq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatādah, the like of it.

- Ibn Bashshār narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā ibn Kathīr ibn Dirham Abu Ghassān narrated to us, he said: Qurra ibn Khālid narrated to us, from 'Aṭiyya al-Jadalī, regarding ﴿and leave me *malīyyan*﴾: he said: safe.

- It was reported to me from al-Ḥusayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'āḏ say: 'Ubayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say regarding His words ﴿and leave me *malīyyan*﴾: keep away from me safe, from which no harm from me will reach you.

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two views regarding the interpretation of the verse, in my opinion, is the view of the one who said: the meaning of that is: leave me *sawiyyan*, safe from my punishment, because it follows His words ﴿If you do not desist, I will surely stone you﴾. That is a threat from him to him: if he does not desist from mentioning his gods with evil, he will stone him with evil speech. What is more fitting to follow that warning, by urging him to desist from it before punishment reaches him, is (the call) to keep away. As for the command to a long-lasting abandonment, there is no basis for it.

- al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzāq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Ḥasan, regarding His words ﴿and leave me *malīyyan*﴾: a long time.

- Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, he said: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, regarding ﴿and leave me *malīyyan*﴾: he says: an age, and the *malī* age.

- Ibn Bashshār narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, he said: Isrā'īl narrated to us, from Abu Ḥuṣayn, from Sa'īd ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿and leave me *malīyyan*﴾: an age.

- Mūsā narrated to us, he said: 'Amr narrated to us, Asbaṭ narrated to us, from al-Suddī, regarding ﴿and leave me *malīyyan*﴾: forever.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: leave me *sawiyyan* (whole), safe from my punishment of you. They traced the meaning of *al-millī* to the saying of people: "So-and-so is *millī* with this matter," when he is capable of it and rich in it. It was as if the meaning of the speech, in their view, was: leave me, while your honor is abundant from my punishment, and your body is safe from my harm.

Mention of those who said that:

- 'Alī ibn Dāwūd reported to me, he said: 'Abdullāh ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, he said: Mu'āwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ reported to me, from 'Alī ibn Abi Ṭalḥa, from Ibn 'Abbās, regarding ﴿and leave me *malīyyan*﴾: he says: keep away from me *sawiyyan*.

- Muḥammad ibn Sa'd reported to me, he said: my father reported to me, he said: my paternal uncle reported to me, he said: my father reported to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbās, regarding His words ﴿and leave me *malīyyan*﴾: he said: keep away from me, safe, before my punishment reaches you.

- Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazīd narrated to us, he said: Sa'īd narrated to us, from Qatādah, regarding His words ﴿and leave me *malīyyan*﴾: he said: safe.

- al-Ḥasan narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzāq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatādah, the like of it.

- Ibn Bashshār narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā ibn Kathīr ibn Dirham Abu Ghassān narrated to us, he said: Qurra ibn Khālid narrated to us, from 'Aṭiyya al-Jadalī, regarding ﴿and leave me *malīyyan*﴾: he said: safe.

- It was reported to me from al-Ḥusayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'āḏ say: 'Ubayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say regarding His words ﴿and leave me *malīyyan*﴾: keep away from me safe, from which no harm from me will reach you.

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two views regarding the interpretation of the verse, in my opinion, is the view of the one who said: the meaning of that is: leave me *sawiyyan*, safe from my punishment, because it follows His words ﴿If you do not desist, I will surely stone you﴾. That is a threat from him to him: if he does not desist from mentioning his gods with evil, he will stone him with evil speech. What is more fitting to follow that warning, by urging him to desist from it before punishment reaches him, is (the call) to keep away. As for the command to a long-lasting abandonment, there is no basis for it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verses 47–48:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "Peace be upon you. I will ask forgiveness for you of my Lord. Indeed, He has always been gracious to me.﴾ (47) ﴿And I will leave you and what you invoke other than Allah, and I will invoke my Lord. Perhaps I will not be in invoking my Lord unhappy."﴾ (48)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Ibrahim said to his father when he threatened him, on account of his advice to him and his calling him to Allah, with harsh words and punishment: "Peace be upon you, O father." That is, "Safety from me for you: I will not return to you in what you dislike, nor to your calling me to what you threatened me with by punishment. But ﴿I will ask forgiveness for you of my Lord﴾," that is, "But I will ask my Lord to cover your sins by His pardoning you from your punishment for them. ﴿Indeed, He has always been gracious to me﴾," that is, "Indeed my Lord has been kind to me, responding to my supplication whenever I call upon Him." It is said from this: "Fulan was gracious to me" (tahaffa bi). I have explained this with its evidences earlier, in a way that makes repeating it here unnecessary.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said what we have said about this.

Those who said so:

- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, He has always been gracious to me﴾: he says, "Kind (latifan)."

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, He has always been gracious to me﴾: "Indeed He has been kind to me, for al-hafiy means al-latif (the Kind)."

* *

And His saying ﴿And I will leave you and what you invoke other than Allah﴾

That is: "And I will keep away from you and from what you invoke other than Allah, of idols and images." ﴿And I will invoke my Lord﴾, that is: "And I will invoke my Lord, sincerely devoting worship to Him and singling Him out in lordship." ﴿Perhaps I will not be in invoking my Lord unhappy﴾, that is: "Perhaps I will not be made wretched through the invocation of my Lord, but He will answer my supplication and give me what I ask of Him."

**The interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:** ﴿So when he had withdrawn from them and from what they worshipped besides Allah, We gave him Isaac and Jacob, and We made each of them a prophet﴾ [19:49] ﴿And We bestowed on them of Our mercy, and We made for them a tongue of truth, exalted﴾ [19:50].

His words, may He be remembered and exalted: When Abraham withdrew from his people and from worshipping what they worshipped besides Allah, namely the idols, We removed his loneliness caused by separation from them, and We replaced them for him with people better than they were and more honoured by Allah than they were. So We gave him his son Isaac, and the son of his son, Jacob son of Isaac. ﴿And We made each of them a prophet﴾: here it says "each" in the singular, and does not say "prophets," because the word *kull* ("each") is singular in form. ﴿And We bestowed on them of Our mercy﴾: He, may His praise be great, says: We provided for all of them, meaning Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, from Our mercy. What He bestowed on them of His mercy was the abundance of His provision that He spread out for them in the immediate life of this world, and the wealth He granted them by His bounty.

* *

And His words: ﴿And We made for them a tongue of truth, exalted﴾.

His words, may He be remembered and exalted: We provided them with good praise and a fine remembrance among people.

As follows:

⁕ My father ʿAlī narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, saying: Muʿāwiya narrated to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His words ﴿And We made for them a tongue of truth, exalted﴾: he said: "It means good praise."

He, may His praise be great, described the tongue that He made for them as "exalted" only because all the people of the religious communities speak well of them. The Arabs say: "The tongue of so-and-so has come to me," meaning his praise or his blame. From this is the verse of ʿĀmir ibn al-Ḥārith:

*"Indeed, a tongue came to me, by which I am not pleased,*
*from a height (of Najd), no wonder and no mockery."*

[The verse is by Aʿshā Bāhila, whose name is ʿĀmir ibn al-Ḥārith (Jamharat ashʿār al-ʿArab, p. 135), and it is one of the excellent elegies. In *Lisān al-ʿArab* (under l-s-n): *lisān* is the organ of speech, and it may be used as a metonym for the word, in which case it is feminine. Aʿshā Bāhila said: "Indeed a tongue came to me..." the verse. Ibn Barrī said: *lisān* here means message and statement, and it may also be understood in the sense of speech. Then he said: al-Laḥyānī said: *lisān* in the sense of speech is masculine and feminine; it is said: "Indeed the tongue of people toward you is good praise," meaning their praise. Ended. *Al-lisān* is praise, and His words, may He be mighty and majestic, ﴿and make for me a tongue of truth among the later generations﴾ mean: make for me a good praise that remains until the end of time. Ended. In *Tāj al-ʿArūs* (under ʿ-l-w): the words of Aʿshā Bāhila "min ʿuluw" are narrated with a *u*, *a* and *i* vowel on the *w*, meaning: news came to me from the heights of Najd. Ended. In *Jamharat ashʿār al-ʿArab*: *al-sukhr* means mockery. Ended. The author has cited the verse to show that *lisān* may come in the sense of praise, although the lexicographers explained it as meaning news, message or statement.]

And it is narrated: "Not a lie in it, nor mockery":

*"There came a rumour, which I used to fear,*
*if only fear and caution could benefit me."*

[This verse is also by Aʿshā Bāhila, and it follows the previous verse in the same poem, as in *Jamharat ashʿār al-ʿArab* (p. 136). *Murajjama* means conjectured, not verified about its reality; one says "a speech that is *murajjam*" when it is without certainty. Perhaps the poet meant that people all did not believe the news of this calamity that befell them, so they were divided between believers and deniers.]

*Murajjama*: it is supposed about it (i.e., conjectured).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 51:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And mention in the Book Moses; indeed, he was sincerely devoted, and he was a messenger and a prophet﴾ (19:51).

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet (ﷺ): And mention, O Muhammad, in Our Book which We have sent down to you, Moses son of Imran, and relate to your people that he was sincerely devoted.

The reciters differed regarding the reading of this. The majority of the reciters of Madinah and Basra, and some of the Kufans, recited ﴿innahu kana mukhlisan﴾ with a kasra on the lam of mukhlis (al-mukhlis, "the one who is sincere"), meaning: he used to make his worship sincerely for God, singling Him out in divinity, without ascribing any partner to Him in it. The majority of the reciters of Kufa, except ʿAsim, recited ﴿innahu kana mukhlasan﴾ with a fatha on the lam of mukhlas (al-mukhlas, "the one chosen"), meaning: God had purified and chosen Moses for His message, and made him a prophet and messenger.

Abu Jaʿfar (al-Tabari) said: The correct view in this matter, in my opinion, is that he (ﷺ) was sincere in the worship of God, and purified for the message and prophethood. Whichever of the two readings the reciter uses, he is correct.

﴿And he was a messenger﴾ means: he was a messenger of God to his people, the Children of Israel, and a prophet whom God sent.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 52–53:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And We called him from the right side of the Mount and brought him near as a confidant.﴾ [Q. 19:52] and ﴿And We granted him, out of Our mercy, his brother Harun as a prophet.﴾ [Q. 19:53]

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "And We called Musa from the side of the mountain." By "the right" (al-Ayman) is meant the right of Musa, because the mountain has no right or left; rather, it is as one says: "He stood to the right of the qibla and to its left."

Those who gave interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿from the side of the Mount, the right﴾, he said: "the right side of the mountain." We have already explained the meaning of al-Tur (the mountain) and the disagreement of those who differ concerning it, and we have indicated the correct view regarding it in what preceded, in a way that makes repeating it in this place unnecessary.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and brought him near as a confidant﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "And We brought him near, as a confidant (munajiyan)," just as one says: "So-and-so is the boon-companion (nadim) and drinking-companion (mudamih) of so-and-so, and the companion (jalis) and sitting-companion (mujalis) of so-and-so." It is mentioned that Allah, may His praise be exalted, brought him so near that he heard the scratching of the pen.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from ʿAta' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, ﴿and brought him near as a confidant﴾, he said: "He was brought near until he heard the scratching of the pen."

Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Tusi narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Bakr narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, who said: I think he narrated it from Mujahid, concerning His saying ﴿and brought him near as a confidant﴾, he said: "Between him and the fourth heaven, or he said: the seventh, and between him and the Throne were seventy thousand veils: a veil of light, a veil of darkness, a veil of light, a veil of darkness. So He kept bringing Musa near until there was between him and Him only a veil, and he heard the scratching of the pen. ﴿He said: My Lord, show me Yourself that I may look upon You.﴾"

ʿAli ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Jaʿfar, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-ʿAliyah, who said: "He brought him near to Himself until he heard the scratching of the pen."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from ʿAta', from Maysarah, ﴿and brought him near as a confidant﴾, he said: "He was brought near until he heard the scratching of the pen on the Tablet." Shu'bah said: "Jibril, peace be upon him, rode behind him (ardafahu)."

Qatadah said concerning this:

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated it to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿and brought him near as a confidant﴾, he said: "He was saved (naja) by his truthfulness."

* *

As for His saying ﴿And We granted him, out of Our mercy, his brother Harun﴾:

He says: "And We granted Musa, out of Our mercy, his brother Harun ﴿as a prophet﴾," meaning: We strengthened him with prophethood and aided him with it.

As:

Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, from Dawud, from ʿIkrimah, who said: Ibn ʿAbbas said: concerning His saying ﴿And We granted him, out of Our mercy, his brother Harun as a prophet﴾, he said: "Harun was older than Musa, but He meant: He granted him prophethood."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 54:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And mention in the Book Ishmael. Indeed, he was true to his promise, and he was a messenger and a prophet.﴾ (19:54)

Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "And mention, O Muhammad, in the Book, Ishmael son of Abraham, so relate his story: indeed he did not break his promise, nor did he fail to keep it, but whenever he promised his Lord, or one of His servants, a promise, he fulfilled it."

As:

- Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning His saying ﴿Indeed, he was true to his promise﴾, he said: "He never made a promise to his Lord without fulfilling it."

- Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me that Sahl ibn 'Aqil related to him that Ishmael, peace be upon him, promised a man to meet him at a certain place. The man came but forgot, so Ishmael waited for him, and he stayed there until the man came the next day. He said: "Have you not moved from here?" He said: "No." The man said: "I forgot." Ishmael said: "I would not have left until you came." Thus was he truthful.

The Almighty says to His Prophet (ﷺ): "These are the ones whose accounts I have related to you in this surah, O Muhammad, those upon whom God bestowed His favour through His guidance, and so He directed them to the path of rectitude: among the prophets, from the descendants of Adam, and from the descendants of those whom We carried with Noah in the ark, and from the descendants of Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful, and from the descendants of Israel, and from those whom We guided to belief in God and to acting in obedience to Him, and whom We chose (ijtaba): that is, whom We selected and chose for Our message and Our revelation."

So the one meant by the descendants of Adam is Idris. The one meant by the descendants of those carried with Noah is Abraham. The ones meant by the descendants of Abraham are Isaac, Jacob and Ishmael. The ones meant by the descendants of Israel are Moses, Aaron, Zechariah, Jesus and his mother Mary. God has therefore separated their lineages, although Adam includes them all, because among them is one who is not a son of those who were with Noah in the ship, and that is Idris, and Idris was the grandfather of Noah.

As for the words of the Almighty: ﴿When the signs of the Most Merciful are recited to them﴾, meaning: when the proofs and arguments of God that He sent down in His scriptures are recited to these prophets upon whom God bestowed His favour, ﴿they fall down prostrate﴾, out of humility before Him, abasement, and submission and obedience to His command, ﴿and weeping﴾. He means: they fall down prostrating while weeping. Al-bukiyy is the plural of bakin (weeping), just as al-utiyy is the plural of 'atin and al-juthiyy is the plural of jathin. The form fa'il is pluralised as fa'ul, just as al-qa'id is pluralised as qu'ud and al-jalis as julus. By analogy (al-qiyas), the plural should have been bukuww and utuww, but the waw was disliked after a damma, so it was changed into a ya', as is said for the plural of dalw as adal, and for the plural of al-bahw as abah. The original forms were adlu and abhu, and the waw was changed into a ya' because it came after a damma, out of distaste for the heaviness. There are two well-known dialects in this, and scholars among the readers (qurra') have recited the Qur'an with each of them: bukiyyan and utuwwan with a damma, and bukiyyan and utiyyan with a kasra. It is also possible that al-bukiyy is the same as al-bukaʾ (weeping).

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, who said: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrahim, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may God be pleased with him) recited Surat Maryam, then prostrated and said: "This is the prostration, so where is the bukiyy?" He meant: where is the weeping?

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Then there succeeded them a generation who neglected prayer and followed their desires, so they will meet error﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Then there came after those prophets whom I have mentioned, upon whom I bestowed favour, and whose description I gave in this surah, an evil generation on the earth, who neglected the prayer.

Then the people of ta'wil (interpretation, explanation of meaning) differed concerning the manner of their neglect of the prayer. Some of them said: Their neglect of it was delaying it beyond its appointed times and wasting its times.

Mention of those who said this:

Ali ibn Sa'd al-Kindi narrated to me, saying: Isa ibn Yunus related to us, from al-Awza'i, from Musa ibn Sulayman, from al-Qasim ibn Mukhaymira, regarding His saying, ﴿Then there succeeded them a generation who neglected the prayer﴾, that he said: They only neglected the appointed times; had it been abandonment, it would have been disbelief.

Ishaq ibn Zayd al-Khattabi related to us, saying: al-Firyabi related to us, from al-Awza'i, from al-Qasim ibn Mukhaymira, the like of it.

Abd al-Karim ibn Abi Umayr related to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to me, from Abu Amr, from al-Qasim ibn Mukhaymira, who said: They neglected the appointed times; and if they had abandoned it, they would have become disbelievers by abandoning it.

Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim related to us, from al-Awza'i, from al-Qasim, the like of it.

al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Isa related to us, from al-Awza'i, from Ibrahim ibn Yazid, that Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz sent a man to Egypt on a matter that was urgent for the Muslims. He went out to his guard, and he had previously instructed them not to stand up when they saw him. He said: So they made room for him, and he sat among them and said: Which of you knows the man whom we sent to Egypt? They said: We all know him. He said: Then let the youngest of you stand and call him. So the messenger came to him and said: Do not hurry me, let me put on my clothes. So he came to him and said: Today is Friday; do not leave until you have prayed. We have sent you on a matter that is urgent for the Muslims, but let not the urgency of what we sent you for lead you to delay the prayer beyond its time, for you will certainly pray it. Then he recited, ﴿Then there succeeded them a generation who neglected the prayer and followed their desires, so they will meet error﴾, then he said: Their neglect was not abandoning it, but they neglected the time.

Ibn Wakī' related to us, saying: My father related to us, from al-Mas'udi, from al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman and al-Hasan ibn Mas'ud, from Ibn Mas'ud, that it was said to him: Indeed God frequently mentions the prayer in the Qur'an: ﴿Those who are heedless of their prayer﴾, ﴿Those who are constant in their prayer﴾, ﴿Those who guard their prayer﴾. So Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: (It means) at its appointed times. They said: We did not think that meant anything but abandonment. He said: That is disbelief.

al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Umar Abu Hafs al-Abbar related to us, from Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir, who said: Masruq said: No one who guards the five prayers will be recorded among the heedless; and in their excess is ruin. Their excess is neglecting them outside their times.

Others said: Rather, their neglect of it was abandoning it.

Mention of those who said this:

Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Sakhr informed us, from al-Qurazi, that he said concerning this verse, ﴿Then there succeeded them a generation who neglected the prayer and followed their desires﴾, he says: They abandoned the prayer.

Abu Ja'far said: The more preferable of the two interpretations in my view, as an explanation of the verse, is the statement of the one who said that their neglect of it was their abandoning it, because of the words of God, may His remembrance be exalted, after it, which show that this is so; namely His saying, may His praise be great, ﴿except those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds﴾. Had those whom He described as having neglected it been believers, He would not have excepted from them those who believed, since they are believers. Rather, they were disbelievers who did not pray to God, nor did they perform His obligation; they were wicked, having preferred the desires of their souls over obedience to God. And it has been said: Those whom God described with this attribute are a people of this community who will exist at the end of time.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us. And al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, ﴿Then there succeeded them a generation who neglected the prayer and followed their desires, so they will meet error﴾, he said: At the approach of the Hour, and the passing of the righteous of the Muhammad's community, some of them will leap upon others in the alleys. Muhammad ibn Amr said: (They commit) adultery (zina). And al-Harith said: Adulterers.

al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it, and he said: Adultery, as Ibn Amr said.

al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Abu Tumayla related to us, from Abu Hamza, from Jabir, from Ikrimah, Mujahid and Ata ibn Abi Rabah, regarding ﴿Then there succeeded them a generation﴾ ... the verse, he said: They are the community of Muhammad.

Al-Harith also narrated to me, saying: al-Ashyab related to us, saying: Shurayk related to us, from Abu Tamim ibn Muhajir, concerning the words of God, ﴿Then there succeeded them a generation who neglected the prayer﴾, he said: They are in this community, mounting one another like cattle and donkeys in the roads, not fearing God in the heavens, nor being shy before people on earth.

As for His saying, ﴿so they will meet error﴾, it means that these successors who came after those whom God favoured among the prophets will enter into ghayy, which is the name of a valley among the valleys of Hell, or the name of a well among its wells.

As related:

Abbas ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ziyad ibn Razan [[The author of Taj al-Arus mentions: the memorizer Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Asim ibn Razan, with the chain of Isfahan known as Ibn al-Muqri, with an alif after the ra', so perhaps "Rizan" here is a corruption of "Razan".]] related to us, saying: Sharqi ibn Qutami related to us, from Luqman ibn Amir al-Khuza'i, who said: I went to Abu Umama Suday ibn Ajlan al-Bahili and said: Narrate to us a hadith you heard from the Messenger of God ﷺ. He called for food, then said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "If a rock weighing ten awqiyyah were hurled from the brink of Hell, it would not reach its bottom in fifty autumns. Then it would reach ghayy and athām." I said: What is ghayy and what is athām? He said: Two wells at the bottom of Hell, from which flows the pus of the people of the Fire; and they are the two that God mentioned in His Book: ﴿They neglected the prayer and followed their desires, so they will meet ghayy﴾, and His saying in al-Furqan: ﴿And they do not commit adultery; whoever does that will meet athām﴾.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Asim related to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman related to us, from his father, from Qatada, from Abu Ayyub, from Abdullah ibn Amr, regarding ﴿so they will meet ghayy﴾, he said: A valley in Hell.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Ubayda, from Abdullah, regarding ﴿so they will meet ghayy﴾, he said: A valley in the Fire.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'ba related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Ubayda, from Abdullah, that he said concerning this verse, ﴿so they will meet ghayy﴾, he said: A river in Hell, foul of taste and deep of bottom.

Muhammad ibn Ubayd al-Muharibi narrated to me, saying: Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Ubayda, from his father, concerning His saying, ﴿Then there succeeded them a generation who neglected the prayer and followed their desires, so they will meet ghayy﴾, he said: Ghayy is a river of Hell in the Fire, in which are tormented those who followed their desires.

al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Ubayda, from his father, concerning His saying, ﴿Then there succeeded them a generation who neglected the prayer and followed their desires, so they will meet ghayy﴾, he said: Ghayy is a river of Hell in the Fire, in which are tormented those who followed their desires.

al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Ubayda, from Abdullah, ﴿They neglected the prayer and followed their desires, so they will meet ghayy﴾, he said: A river in the Fire into which those who followed their desires will be cast.

Others said: Rather, by ghayy in this place is meant loss.

Mention of those who said this:

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abdullah related to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying, ﴿so they will meet ghayy﴾, he says: Loss.

Others said: Rather, by it is meant evil.

Mention of those who said this:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying, ﴿so they will meet ghayy﴾, he said: Ghayy: evil.

From this is the saying of the poet:

Whoever meets good, people will praise his affair,
and whoever goes astray will not lack a blamer for his error.

[[The verse is by al-Muraqqish al-Asghar: Rabi'a ibn Sulayman ibn Sa'd ibn Malik Dubay'a ibn Qays ibn Tha'laba, who was the nephew of al-Muraqqish al-Akbar and uncle of Tarafa ibn al-Abd (al-Mufaddaliyyat, Cairo edition, p. 118). In (Lisan al-Arab: gh-w-y) it is said: al-Ghayy: error and frustration. Ghawa (with fatha) ghayyan, and ghawa (with kasra) ghawaya; the latter from Abu Ubayd: he went astray. A man is ghaw, ghawi, ghawiy, or ghayyan: astray. And "aghwahu" means he caused him to err. He quoted al-Muraqqish: "Whoever meets..." the verse.]]

Abu Ja'far said: All these sayings are close in meaning, for whoever enters the two wells mentioned by the Prophet ﷺ, and the valley mentioned by Ibn Mas'ud in Hell, and enters it, has met loss and evil; it is enough as evil for him.

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds; those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged in the least.﴾

He, exalted is He, says: "Those successors of evil who have been described will meet with error (ghayy), except those who repent and return to the command of Allah and belief in Him and His Messenger. ﴿And do righteous deeds﴾ means: they obey Allah in what He has commanded and forbidden, perform His obligations, and avoid His prohibitions. As for those among them who perished in their disbelief, neglecting the prayer and following their desires..."

* *

As for His words: ﴿And will not be wronged in the least﴾

It means: they will not be deprived of any of the reward for their deeds. Nor will they be gathered together with those among the successors of evil who perished before their repentance from their misguidance and before their return to obedience to their Lord, into Hell. Rather, they will enter the abode of the people of faith.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 19, verses 61–62:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Gardens of Eden, which the Most Merciful has promised His servants in the unseen. Indeed, His promise is ever coming to pass.﴾ (19:61)

His, the Exalted's, saying means: "So those will enter Paradise, ﴿gardens of Eden.﴾" His saying ﴿gardens of Eden﴾ is in the accusative case as an apposition (tarjamah) for "Paradise." By ﴿gardens of Eden﴾ He means gardens of residence (iqamah). I have already explained this earlier, with its supporting evidence, which makes repeating it unnecessary.

* *

His saying ﴿which the Most Merciful has promised His servants in the unseen﴾

He says: these gardens are the gardens which the Most Merciful has promised His believing servants that they would enter, in the unseen, because they have not seen them nor witnessed them, so they are unseen (ghayb) to them.

* *

His saying ﴿Indeed, His promise is ever coming to pass﴾

His, the Exalted's, saying means: Indeed Allah's promise was (kana) and His promise here means that which was promised, namely Paradise, "coming to pass" (ma'tiyyan), which His friends and the people of His obedience, whom Allah will cause to enter it, will come to. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: the report was expressed in the form that the promise is "the one coming to pass" (al-ma'tiyy), meaning that it is the one that comes, and He did not say "and His promise was coming" (atiyan), because everything that reaches you is something you reach. He said: Do you not see that you say, "I reached fifty years" (ataytu 'ala khamsin sanah) and "fifty years reached me" (utat 'alayya khamsun sanah)? All of this is correct, and I have already explained the discussion of it. The pronoun in His saying ﴿Indeed (innahu)﴾ refers to "the Most Merciful."

* *

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿They will not hear therein any ill speech, but only "Peace." And they will have their provision therein morning and evening.﴾ (19:62)

His, the Exalted's, saying means: those who enter Paradise will not hear therein any vain speech (laghw), which is idle and false talk and speech, ﴿but only "Peace" (salaman)﴾. This is an exception of the disconnected kind (istithna' munqati'), meaning: rather, they will hear "peace," which is the greeting of the angels to them. His saying: ﴿And they will have their provision therein morning and evening﴾ means: they will have their food and what they desire of foods and drinks in the measure of the time of morning and the time of evening of the days of this world. What is meant is that the interval between their midday meal and their evening meal in Paradise is as the interval between one of us's midday meal and evening meal in this world, and likewise what lies between the evening meal and the midday meal, because there is no night or day in Paradise. This is like His saying ﴿He created the earth in two days﴾ and ﴿He created the heavens and the earth in six days﴾, meaning: days of this world.

As related:

* ʿAli ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: I asked Zuhayr ibn Muhammad about the saying of Allah: ﴿And they will have their provision therein morning and evening﴾. He said: There is no night in Paradise; they are in everlasting light, and they have a measure of night and day: they know the measure of night by the lowering of veils and the closing of doors, and they know the measure of day by the raising of veils and the opening of doors.

* ʿAli narrated to us, saying: al-Walid narrated to us, from Khulayd, from al-Hasan, and he mentioned the gates of Paradise, saying: gates whose outside is visible from the inside, and they speak and are spoken to, and [the gate] murmurs: "Open," "Close," and it does so.

* Ibn Harb narrated to me, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, saying: ʿAmir ibn Yasaf narrated to us, from Yahya, who said: In their time the Arabs considered whoever had a midday meal and an evening meal to be the one enjoying comfort among them. So Allah revealed ﴿And they will have their provision therein morning and evening﴾: the measure of what lies between your midday meal in this world and your evening meal.

* al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿And they will have their provision therein morning and evening﴾, he said: When one of the Arabs obtained a midday meal and an evening meal, he was amazed by it, so Allah informed them that they would have in Paradise a morning and an evening, equal to that midday meal and evening meal.

* al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: It is neither morning nor evening, but they are brought what they desired in this world.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿And they will have their provision therein morning and evening﴾: therein are two periods, morning and evening, and for them there is no night; there is only radiance and light.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 63–64:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is the Garden which We shall give as an inheritance to those of Our servants who were God-fearing (taqiyyan)﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: This Garden which I have described to you, O people, its attributes, is the Garden which We shall make to inherit, meaning: We shall make to inherit the dwellings of the people of the Fire therein. ﴿Among Our servants, those who were God-fearing﴾ meaning: those who were mindful of God's punishment by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and what is between that, and your Lord is not ever forgetful﴾

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning the Messenger of God's (ﷺ) being slow in receiving revelation from Jibril (Gabriel). Some of the narration has been mentioned, and we will mention, God willing, the rest of what has come to our attention that we have not mentioned before.

Mention of those who said that:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: 'Abdullah narrated to us, he said: 'Abdullah ibn Aban al-Ajli, Qabisah and Waki' narrated to us; and Sufyan ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: my father narrated to us, all of them from Umar ibn Dharr, who said: I heard my father mention from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that Muhammad said to Jibril: "What prevents you from visiting us more than you visit us?" So this verse was revealed: ﴿And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and what is between that, and your Lord is not ever forgetful﴾. He said: This is the answer to Muhammad (ﷺ).

Muhammad ibn Ma'mar narrated to me, he said: 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Amr narrated to us, he said: Umar ibn Dharr narrated to us, he said: my father narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to Jibril: "What prevents you from visiting us more than you visit us?" Then it was revealed: ﴿And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord﴾.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord﴾ up to ﴿and your Lord is not ever forgetful﴾: He said: Jibril was delayed from the Prophet (ﷺ), so the Messenger of God (ﷺ) felt that and was saddened, and Jibril came to him and said: O Muhammad, ﴿And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and what is between that, and your Lord is not ever forgetful﴾.

al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, who said: Jibril stayed away from the Prophet (ﷺ), so the Prophet seemed to be slow awaiting him, and when he came to him Jibril said to him ﴿And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord﴾ ... the verse.

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us﴾ He said: This is the speech of Jibril. Jibril was delayed in some of the revelation, so the Prophet of God (ﷺ) said: "You did not come until I longed for you," and Jibril said to him: ﴿And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us﴾.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God, blessed and exalted is He, ﴿And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord﴾: He said: It is the speech of the angels when Muhammad (ﷺ) asked them for help, like that in al-Duha.

al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: Jibril stayed away from Muhammad for twelve nights, and they were saying: he has forsaken him. So when he came to him, he said: O Jibril, you have been long away from me, so much so that the polytheists have entertained every suspicion. Then it was revealed: ﴿And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and what is between that, and your Lord is not ever forgetful﴾.

It was related from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord﴾: He was delayed from the Prophet of God (ﷺ) until the polytheists spoke about that, and that was difficult for the Prophet of God. So Jibril came to him and said: Our delay from you has been hard on you, and the polytheists have spoken about it, but I am only a servant of God and His messenger; when He commands me with a command, I obey it. ﴿And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord﴾: meaning, by the speech of your Lord.

Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the interpretation of His saying: ﴿To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and what is between that﴾. Some of them said: By His saying ﴿what is before us﴾ is meant the worldly life, by His saying ﴿what is behind us﴾ the Hereafter, and ﴿what is between that﴾ the two blowings of the Trumpet.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Hakkam narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi': ﴿To Him belongs what is before us﴾ meaning the worldly life, ﴿and what is behind us﴾ the Hereafter, ﴿and what is between that﴾ the two blowings.

al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, he said: ﴿What is before us﴾ from the worldly life, ﴿and what is behind us﴾ from the matters of the Hereafter, ﴿and what is between that﴾ what is between the two blowings.

Others said: ﴿What is before us﴾ is the Hereafter, ﴿what is behind us﴾ is the worldly life, ﴿and what is between that﴾ what is between the worldly life and the Hereafter.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿before us﴾ the Hereafter, ﴿and behind us﴾ the worldly life.

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿To Him belongs what is before us﴾ from the matters of the Hereafter, ﴿and what is behind us﴾ from the matters of the worldly life, ﴿and what is between that﴾ what is between the worldly life and the Hereafter, ﴿and your Lord is not ever forgetful﴾.

al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah: ﴿To Him belongs what is before us﴾ from the Hereafter, ﴿and what is behind us﴾ from the worldly life, ﴿and what is between that﴾ what is between the two blowings.

It was related from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿what is before us﴾ from the Hereafter, ﴿and what is behind us﴾ from the worldly life.

Others said concerning that:

al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿what is before us﴾, he said: what has passed ahead of us of the worldly life; (﴿and what is behind us﴾) what will be after us of the worldly life and the Hereafter; ﴿and what is between that﴾, he said: what is between what has passed ahead of them and what will be after them.

One of the grammarians of Basra used to interpret it as: ﴿what is before us﴾ before we were created, ﴿and what is behind us﴾ after annihilation, ﴿and what is between that﴾ when we were.

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these opinions, in my view, is the saying of the one who said: its meaning is: to Him belongs what is before us of the matters of the Hereafter, because that has not yet come, though it is coming; so what is before them is what has not come, and people, when they say "this matter is before you," generally mean what has not yet come, and that it has come. Therefore we say that this is more correct. And what is behind us is the matters of the worldly life, which is what they have left behind and passed, so it becomes behind them by their leaving it, and likewise the Arabs say of what a person has passed beyond and left behind him: it is behind him. And what is between that: what lies between what has not yet passed of the worldly life and the Hereafter, because that is what lies between those two times.

We have said that this is the most correct interpretation only because it is the apparent and most common meaning, and the interpretation of the Qur'an is taken according to its most common meanings, so long as nothing prevents that which must be accepted. So consider the speech: O Muhammad, do not consider us slow in our delay from you, for we do not descend from the heaven to the earth except by the command of your Lord to us to descend to it. To Him belongs what is newly occurring of the matters of the Hereafter that have not come yet though they are coming, and what has passed and we have left behind of the matters of the worldly life, and what lies between this time of ours and the establishment of the Hour; all of that is in His hand. He is its Owner and Disposer, and no one else possesses it. So it is not for us to introduce any matter into His dominion except by His command to us. ﴿And your Lord is not ever forgetful﴾: meaning, your Lord was not one who forgets, so that our descent to you would be delayed by His forgetting you. Rather, He is the One from whom nothing is hidden in the heavens or the earth, blessed and exalted is He; but He is most knowing of what He arranges and decrees for His creation, exalted is His praise.

And the people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿And your Lord was not forgetful﴾: your Lord has not forgotten you.

Then it was revealed: ﴿And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and what is between that, and your Lord is not ever forgetful﴾.

It was related from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord﴾: He was delayed from the Prophet of God (ﷺ) until the polytheists spoke about that, and that was difficult for the Prophet of God. So Jibril came to him and said: Our delay from you has been hard on you, and the polytheists have spoken about it, but I am only a servant of God and His messenger; when He commands me with a command, I obey it. ﴿And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord﴾: meaning, by the speech of your Lord.

Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the interpretation of His saying: ﴿To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and what is between that﴾. Some of them said: By His saying ﴿what is before us﴾ is meant the worldly life, by His saying ﴿what is behind us﴾ the Hereafter, and ﴿what is between that﴾ the two blowings of the Trumpet.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Hakkam narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi': ﴿To Him belongs what is before us﴾ meaning the worldly life, ﴿and what is behind us﴾ the Hereafter, ﴿and what is between that﴾ the two blowings.

al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, he said: ﴿What is before us﴾ from the worldly life, ﴿and what is behind us﴾ from the matters of the Hereafter, ﴿and what is between that﴾ what is between the two blowings.

Others said: ﴿What is before us﴾ is the Hereafter, ﴿what is behind us﴾ is the worldly life, ﴿and what is between that﴾ what is between the worldly life and the Hereafter.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿before us﴾ the Hereafter, ﴿and behind us﴾ the worldly life.

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿To Him belongs what is before us﴾ from the matters of the Hereafter, ﴿and what is behind us﴾ from the matters of the worldly life, ﴿and what is between that﴾ what is between the worldly life and the Hereafter, ﴿and your Lord is not ever forgetful﴾.

al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah: ﴿To Him belongs what is before us﴾ from the Hereafter, ﴿and what is behind us﴾ from the worldly life, ﴿and what is between that﴾ what is between the two blowings.

It was related from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿what is before us﴾ from the Hereafter, ﴿and what is behind us﴾ from the worldly life.

Others said concerning that:

al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿what is before us﴾, he said: what has passed ahead of us of the worldly life; (﴿and what is behind us﴾) what will be after us of the worldly life and the Hereafter; ﴿and what is between that﴾, he said: what is between what has passed ahead of them and what will be after them.

One of the grammarians of Basra used to interpret it as: ﴿what is before us﴾ before we were created, ﴿and what is behind us﴾ after annihilation, ﴿and what is between that﴾ when we were.

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these opinions, in my view, is the saying of the one who said: its meaning is: to Him belongs what is before us of the matters of the Hereafter, because that has not yet come, though it is coming; so what is before them is what has not come, and people, when they say "this matter is before you," generally mean what has not yet come, and that it has come. Therefore we say that this is more correct. And what is behind us is the matters of the worldly life, which is what they have left behind and passed, so it becomes behind them by their leaving it, and likewise the Arabs say of what a person has passed beyond and left behind him: it is behind him. And what is between that: what lies between what has not yet passed of the worldly life and the Hereafter, because that is what lies between those two times.

We have said that this is the most correct interpretation only because it is the apparent and most common meaning, and the interpretation of the Qur'an is taken according to its most common meanings, so long as nothing prevents that which must be accepted. So consider the speech: O Muhammad, do not consider us slow in our delay from you, for we do not descend from the heaven to the earth except by the command of your Lord to us to descend to it. To Him belongs what is newly occurring of the matters of the Hereafter that have not come yet though they are coming, and what has passed and we have left behind of the matters of the worldly life, and what lies between this time of ours and the establishment of the Hour; all of that is in His hand. He is its Owner and Disposer, and no one else possesses it. So it is not for us to introduce any matter into His dominion except by His command to us. ﴿And your Lord is not ever forgetful﴾: meaning, your Lord was not one who forgets, so that our descent to you would be delayed by His forgetting you. Rather, He is the One from whom nothing is hidden in the heavens or the earth, blessed and exalted is He; but He is most knowing of what He arranges and decrees for His creation, exalted is His praise.

And the people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿And your Lord was not forgetful﴾: your Lord has not forgotten you.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 65:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, so worship Him and be steadfast in His worship. Do you know of any namesake for Him?﴾ (19:65)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Your Lord, O Muhammad, is not forgetful of the Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, for if He were forgetful, that would not be sound, and [the heavens and earth] would perish were it not for His preserving them. So "the Lord" is in the nominative case as a response to His saying ﴿your Lord﴾. As for His saying ﴿so worship Him﴾, He means: keep to His obedience and submit to His command and prohibition. ﴿And be steadfast in His worship﴾ means: restrain yourself in submitting to His command and prohibition and in acting in accordance with His obedience, so that you will attain His good pleasure, for He is the God who has no equal, no peer, and no likeness in His generosity, bounty, and grace. ﴿Do you know of any namesake for Him?﴾ means: Do you know, O Muhammad, of anyone who is a likeness of your Lord, whom We have commanded you to worship and to be steadfast in obeying, in His generosity and bounty, such that you would worship him in hope of His grace and favour instead of Him? No, that does not exist.

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ali narrated to me, he said: Abdullah narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Do you know of any namesake for Him?﴾: he means, do you know of a likeness or a counterpart to the Lord.

- Sa'id ibn Uthman al-Tanukhi narrated to me, he said: Ibrahim ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Abbad ibn Awwam, from Shu'ba, from al-Hasan ibn Imarah, from a man, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Do you know of any namesake for Him?﴾, he said: a counterpart.

- Yahya ibn Ibrahim al-Mas'udi narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid regarding this verse ﴿Do you know of any namesake for Him?﴾, he said: Do you know of a counterpart to Him, do you know of a likeness to Him, blessed and exalted is He.

- Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿Do you know of any namesake for Him?﴾: There is no namesake of God and no equal to Him. All His creation acknowledges Him and confesses that He is their Creator, and knows this, then he recited this verse ﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say, "God."﴾

- Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, regarding His saying ﴿Do you know of any namesake for Him?﴾, he said: He says: no partner to Him and no likeness.

**The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Man says, "When I have died, shall I really be brought out alive?" (66) Does not man remember that We created him before, when he was nothing? (67)﴾**

The Exalted says: ﴿And man says﴾, meaning the disbeliever who does not affirm the Resurrection after death, denying it and saying, "Shall I be brought out alive, after death, after decay and annihilation?" God, the Exalted, says: ﴿Does not man﴾, meaning the one who is astonished at that denier, ﴿remember﴾ God's power to bring him back to life after his annihilation and to produce him after his non-existence, through the creation of his own self, that God created him before his death, bringing him into being as a sound human from nothing, ﴿and he was not﴾ before his creation ﴿anything﴾. So let him take heed of this and know that the One who originated him from nothing is not incapable of bringing him back to life after his death and producing him after his annihilation.

The reciters (qurra', those specialised in the transmitted recitations, or qira'at) differed over the reading of His saying ﴿Does not man remember﴾. Some reciters of Madina and Kufa read ﴿أَوَلا يَذْكُرُ﴾ (awa-la yadhkuru) with the dhal lightly pronounced. The majority of reciters of Kufa, Basra and the Hijaz read ﴿أَوَلا يَذَّكَّرُ﴾ (awa-la yadhdhakkaru) with the dhal and the kaf both doubled, meaning "does he not reflect?" I consider the doubled form more preferable, although the other reading is permissible, because the meaning is: "Does he not reflect and so take heed?"

* *

**The interpretation of His saying, ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely gather them and the devils, then We will surely bring them forth around Hell, on their knees (jithiyy).﴾ (68)**

The Exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): By your Lord, O Muhammad, We will surely gather those who said, "When we have died, shall we really be brought out alive?" on the Day of Resurrection from their graves, paired with their companions among the devils. ﴿Then We will surely bring them forth around Hell, on their knees.﴾ The word jithiyy (on their knees) is the plural of jathi (one who kneels).

As related:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Then We will surely bring them forth around Hell, on their knees﴾: it means sitting, and it is like His saying, ﴿And you will see every nation kneeling﴾.
