As related:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Then We will surely bring them forth around Hell, on their knees﴾: it means sitting, and it is like His saying, ﴿And you will see every nation kneeling﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 69:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿Then We will surely drag out from every group whichever of them was most insolent toward the Most Merciful﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Then We will surely seize from every group among them the most insolent and rebellious against God, and We will begin with them.

Those versed in interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from ʿAli ibn al-Aqmar, from Abu al-Ahwas, regarding ﴿Then We will surely drag out from every group whichever of them was most insolent toward the Most Merciful﴾, he said: "We will begin with the greatest of them in rank, then the greatest in crime."

Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿Then We will surely drag out from every group whichever of them was most insolent toward the Most Merciful﴾, he said: "Whichever of them was most disobedient to the Most Merciful, and that is their disobedience in associating partners with God."

ʿAli narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to us, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿whichever of them was most insolent toward the Most Merciful﴾, he said: "Who disobeyed."

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿from every group﴾, he said: "Community (umma)."

And regarding His saying ﴿ʿitiyyan﴾, he said: "Disbelief."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it, and Ibn Jurayj added in it: "Then We will surely begin with them."

Abu Jaʿfar (al-Tabari) said: The shiʿah are the group cooperating in a matter of affairs. It is said of this: tashayyaʿa al-qawm (the people supported one another) when they cooperate; and from it is their saying of a brave man: innahu lamushayyaʿ (he is indeed one who is supported), meaning one who is helped. So the meaning of the statement is: Then We will surely seize from every group that has united in disbelief in God the most insolent of them against God, and We will begin with casting them into Hell. Tashayyuʿ in other places means dispersal; from it is the saying of God, mighty is His remembrance: ﴿and they became sects (shiya)﴾, meaning factions; and from it is the saying of Ibn Masʿud or Saʿd: "I dislike that I should come to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and he says: 'You have split (shayyaʿta) among my community,'" meaning: you have divided.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verses 70–71 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of the words of the Exalted: ﴿Then We are most knowing of those most deserving of burning therein﴾ [19:70].

The Exalted says: Then We are more knowing of those among these who We drag out from every party, those most deserving of the severest punishment and most worthy of the greatest retribution.

It is related from Ibn Jurayj that he used to say about this:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿Then We are most knowing of those most deserving of burning therein﴾: "Most deserving of abiding eternally in Hell."

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: What Ibn Jurayj said is an opinion without meaning, because God the Exalted informed that those whom He drags out from every party of disbelievers are the most intense in their disbelief, and there is no doubt that no one who disbelieves in God is anything but eternally abiding in the Fire. So there is no sense in it, since all of them abide eternally in Hell, for it would be said: "Then We are most knowing of those who are most deserving of eternal abiding, out of these eternal abiders." But the meaning in this is what we have mentioned. It may also be that its meaning is: "Then We are most knowing of those who are most deserving of some of the levels of Hell to burn therein." The ṣaliyy (burning) is a verbal noun of ṣallaytu, tuṣallī, ṣaliyyan, and ṣaliyy is on the pattern fa'ūl, but its waw was changed to yā', and it was assimilated into the following yā', which is the lam of the verb, becoming a doubled yā'.

* *

The interpretation of the words of the Exalted: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it. That is ever, with your Lord, a decree that must be carried out﴾ [19:71].

The Exalted says: And there is none of you, O people, but will come upon Hell; it was, O Muhammad, a decree decided by your Lord, which He had decreed and made obligatory in the Mother of the Book.

The scholars differed regarding the meaning of "coming upon" (wurūd) which God mentioned in this place. Some of them said: it means entering.

Those who said that:

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn 'Uyayna informed us, from 'Amr, saying: One who heard Ibn 'Abbas debating Nafi' ibn al-Azraq told me: Ibn 'Abbas said: "Wurūd" means entering. Nafi' said: No. Ibn 'Abbas then recited: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are the fuel of Hell; you are to it bound to come﴾ [21:98]. "Is it coming or not? And He said: ﴿He will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection and lead them to the Fire, and wretched is the place to which they are led﴾ [11:98]. Is it coming or not? As for you and me, we will enter it. So see whether we come out of it or not. I do not think God will bring you out of it for your denial." He said: Nafi' laughed.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, who said: Abu Rashid al-Harūrī said: They mentioned this, and the Harūrī said: "They do not hear its hissing." Ibn 'Abbas said: "Woe to you! Are you mad? Where is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿He will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection and lead them to the Fire, and wretched is the place to which they are led﴾ and ﴿And We will drive the criminals to Hell in a thirsty herd﴾ [19:86], and His saying ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾? By God, if it were a supplication of those who passed away: 'O God, bring me out of the Fire safe, and admit me to Paradise victorious'..."

Ibn Jurayj said: He means: the wurūd mentioned by God in the Qur'an is entering. Everyone, pious and wicked, will come to it. In the Qur'an there are four instances of wurūd: ﴿He leads them to the Fire﴾, ﴿Indeed, you are to it bound to come﴾, ﴿And We will drive the criminals to Hell in a thirsty herd﴾, and His saying ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, His saying ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it, that is ever, with your Lord, a decree that must be carried out﴾: he means the pious and the wicked. Have you not heard the saying of God to Pharaoh: ﴿He will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection and lead them to the Fire, and wretched is the place to which they are led﴾, and He said ﴿And We will drive the criminals to Hell in a thirsty herd﴾? So He named the wurūd into the Fire "entering," though it is not "departing."

Al-Hasan ibn 'Arafa narrated to us, saying: Marwan ibn Mu'awiya narrated to us, from Bukayr ibn Abi Marwan, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, who said: The people of Paradise, after they had entered Paradise, said: Did our Lord not promise us the wurūd upon the Fire? He said: You have passed by it while it was extinguished.

Ibn 'Arafa said: Marwan ibn Mu'awiya said: Bukayr ibn Abi Marwan said, or he said: "motionless."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Marhum ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Imran al-Jawni narrated to me, from Abu Khalid, who said: A day will come when the earth will be fire; what have you prepared for it? He said: That is the saying of God: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it, that is ever, with your Lord, a decree that must be carried out. Then We will save those who were righteous and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees﴾ [19:72].

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, from al-Jurayri, from Abu al-Sulayl, from Ghunaym ibn Qays, who said: They mentioned the wurūd of the Fire, and Ka'b said: The Fire will be held for the people as if it were the fat of a sheep's hide, until the feet of creation, pious and wicked, stand upon it. Then a caller will call to it: "Hold back your companions and leave my companions." Then everyone who is its ally will be swallowed up, and it knows them better than a man knows his child, and the believers will emerge with their bodies moist. He said: Ka'b also said: Between the shoulders of the keeper of its guardians is a journey of a year, and each of them carries a staff with two prongs, with which he pushes once, and by it seven hundred thousand are cast into the Fire.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Malik ibn Mighwal, from Abu Ishaq, who said: When Abu Maysara went to his bed, he would say: "Would that my mother had not borne me," and then weep. It was said to him: "What makes you weep, Abu Maysara?" He said: "He told us that we will come upon it, and He did not tell us that we will depart from it."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Isma'il, from Qays, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Rawaha wept during his illness, and his wife wept. He said: "What makes you weep?" She said: "I saw you weeping, so I wept." Ibn Rawaha said: "I know that I will come upon the Fire, and I do not know whether I will be saved from it or not."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Amr Dawud ibn al-Zabarqan narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Suddi relate from Murra al-Hamdani, from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾: "He will enter it."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾: "He will enter it."

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ibn 'Uyayna, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Rawaha was resting his head in his wife's lap, and he wept, and his wife wept. He said: "What makes you weep?" She said: "I saw you weeping, so I wept." He said: "I remembered the saying of God: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾, and I do not know whether I will be saved from it or not."

Others said: Rather, it is passing over it.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾: he means Hell; the people pass over it.

Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾: "It is passing over it."

Khallad ibn Aslam narrated to us, saying: al-Nadr informed us, saying: Israel informed us, saying: Abu Ishaq informed us, from Abu al-Ahwas, from 'Abd Allah, regarding His saying ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾: "The Sirat over Hell is like the edge of a sword. The first tier passes like lightning, the second like the wind, the third like the best of horses, and the fourth like the best of beasts. Then they pass while the angels say: 'O God, grant safety, grant safety.'"

Others said: Rather, wurūd is entering, but it refers to the disbelievers, not the believers.

Those who said that:

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Sa'ib informed me, from a man who heard Ibn 'Abbas recite ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾, meaning the disbelievers: "No believer will enter it."

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn al-Walid al-Shanni narrated to us, saying: I heard 'Ikrima say: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾, meaning the disbelievers.

Others said: Rather, wurūd is general to every believer and disbeliever, except that the wurūd of the believer is passing by, and the wurūd of the disbeliever is entering.

Those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾: the wurūd of the Muslims is passing over the bridge in its midst, and the wurūd of the polytheists is entering it. He said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Those who slip and stumble that day are many, and two rows of angels surround the bridge, and their supplication that day is: O God, grant safety."

Others said: The wurūd of the believer is what befalls him in this world of fever and sickness.

Those who said that:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Uthman ibn al-Aswad, from Mujahid, who said: "Fever is the portion of every believer from the Fire," then he recited ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾.

Imran ibn Bakkar al-Kalla'i narrated to me, saying: Abu al-Mughira narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Tamim narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ went out to visit a man of his companions who had a fever, and I was with him. Then he said: "God says: It is My Fire, which I impose upon My believing servant, so that it may be his portion of the Fire in the Hereafter."

Others said: All of them will come to it, then the believers will depart from it by their deeds.

Those who said that:

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Shu'ba, who said: al-Suddi narrated to me, from Murra, from 'Abd Allah ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾: "They will come to it, then they will depart from it by their deeds."

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Murra, from 'Abd Allah, in similar words.

Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd al-Muharibi narrated to me, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik, from 'Ubayd Allah, from Mujahid, who said: I was with Ibn 'Abbas when a man called Abu Rashid, who was Nafi' ibn al-Azraq, came to him and said: "O Ibn 'Abbas, what do you say about the saying of God: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it, that is ever, with your Lord, a decree that must be carried out﴾?" He said: "As for you and me, O Abu Rashid, we will pass over it, so see whether we depart from it or not."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Zubayr informed us that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah being asked about the wurūd, and he said: "We will be on the Day of Resurrection upon a hillock or a height above the people. The nations will be called with their idols, and whatever each used to worship, first to last, will go forth with them, and they will follow it. Every hypocrite and believer will be given a light, and darkness will cover them, and then they will follow it. Upon the bridge of Hell are hooks that seize whomever God wills. The light of the hypocrite will be extinguished, and the believers will be saved. The first group will be saved like the full moon on the night of its fullness, seventy thousand with no reckoning for them, then those after them like the lights of a star in the sky, and so on. Then intercession will come, and they will intercede. Whoever said 'There is no god but God' and had in his heart a weight of a barleycorn of good will be brought out of the Fire. Then they will be met at the gate of Paradise, and the people of Paradise will pour water over them, and they will sprout like a seed in a flood. Then they will be asked, and they will be given this world and ten times its like."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn al-Mubarak, from al-Hasan, who said: A man said to his brother: "Has it reached you that you will come upon the Fire?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Has it reached you that you will depart from it?" He said: "No." He said: "Then why laugh?" It is said he was never seen laughing until he met God.

Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed us that Bukayr told him that he said to Busr ibn Sa'id: "So-and-so says that the wurūd of the Fire is standing over it." Busr said: "As for Abu Hurayra, I heard him say: 'When the Day of Resurrection comes, the people will gather, and a caller will call: Let every people join what they used to worship. So this one will go to the stone, this one to the horse, this one to the wood, until only those who worshipped God remain, and God will come to them. When they see Him, they will stand up toward Him, and He will take them and lead them onto the Sirat, and there are thorns on it. At that point intercession will be permitted, and the people will pass, and the prophets will say: O God, grant safety, grant safety.'" Bukayr said: Ibn 'Umayra used to say: "Saved and Muslim, and thrown headlong into Hell and torn, then saved."

The most correct of these opinions, in our view, is the opinion of those who said: all of them will come to it, then the believers will depart from it, and God will save them, and the disbelievers will plunge into it. Their wurūd is what is attested by the reports from the Messenger of God ﷺ regarding their passing over the Sirat set up on the back of Hell, so one is saved and another is thrown headlong into it.

Mention of the reports transmitted from the Messenger of God ﷺ on this: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, from Umm Mubashshir, the wife of Zayd ibn Haritha, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said while he was in the house of Hafsa: "No one who fought at Badr or al-Hudaybiya will enter the Fire." She said: Hafsa said: "O Messenger of God, does not God say: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾?" The Messenger of God said: "Hold on, [for] ﴿Then We will save those who were righteous﴾."

Al-Hasan ibn Mudrik narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Awana narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, from Umm Mubashshir, from the Messenger of God ﷺ, with the like of it.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, from Umm Mubashshir, from Hafsa, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "I truly hope that no one who fought at Badr or al-Hudaybiya will enter the Fire." She said: I said: "O Messenger of God, does not God say: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾?" He said: "Did you not hear Him say: ﴿Then We will save those who were righteous and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees﴾?"

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: 'Ubayd Allah ibn al-Mughira ibn Mu'aygib narrated to me, from Sulayman ibn 'Amr ibn 'Abd al-'Itwari, one of the Banu Layth, who had been raised in the care of Abu Sa'id, who said: I heard Abu Sa'id al-Khudri say: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: "The Sirat will be placed between the backs of Hell, with thorns like the thorns of al-sa'dan upon it. Then the people will seek to cross. Some are saved and unharmed, and some are saved but wounded by it, and some are held back and thrown headlong into it. When God has finished judging among the servants, the believers will look for men who were with them in the world, who prayed their prayer, paid their zakat, fasted their fasts, performed their pilgrimage, and fought their battles. They will say: 'O our Lord, servants of Yours were with us in the world, praying our prayer, paying our zakat, fasting our fasts, performing our pilgrimage, and fighting our battles, but we do not see them.' He will say: 'Go to the Fire, and whomever of them you find in it, bring him out.' They will find them, the Fire having seized them according to their deeds. Some of them the Fire has seized up to their feet, some up to the middle of their shins, some up to their knees, some up to their chests, some up to their necks, but it has not covered their faces. They will bring them out of it and cast them into the water of life." It was said: "What is the water of life, O Messenger of God?" He said: "The washing of the people of Paradise. They will sprout as a seed sprouts in the debris of a flood. Then the prophets will intercede for everyone who used to testify that there is no god but God sincerely, and they will bring them out of it. Then God, in His mercy, will have compassion upon those within it, and He will not leave in it any servant who has in his heart a weight of an atom's weight of faith, but He will bring him out of it."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verses 70–71 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam narrated to me, saying: My father and Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth narrated to us, from al-Layth ibn Khalid, from Yazid ibn Abi Hilal, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Bridge (al-Jisr) will be brought – meaning on the Day of Resurrection – and it will be placed between the back of Hell." We said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the Bridge?" He said: "It is slippery and unstable, upon it are hooks, claws, and a flattened thorn-bush with a crooked thorn, found in Najd, called al-Sa'dan. The believers will pass over it like the glance of an eye, like lightning, like the wind, and like the finest horses and riding camels. Some will be saved and unharmed, some will be scratched and saved, and some will be thrown into Hell. Then the last of them will pass, being dragged along. You are no more insistent in pleading with me for the truth which has become clear to you than the believers will be on that day before the Almighty, blessed and exalted, when they see that those (of their brothers) have been saved while their brothers remain."

⁕ Ahmad ibn Isa narrated to me, saying: Sa'id ibn Kathir ibn Ufayr narrated to us, saying: Ibn Lahi'a narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, who said: I asked Jabir ibn Abd Allah about the wurud (coming to the Fire), and he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "It is the entering. They will come to the Fire until they come out of it. The last one to remain will be a man on the Bridge, crawling. Allah will raise a tree for him." He said: "He will say: 'O Lord, bring me close to it.' So Allah, blessed and exalted, will bring him close to it." He said: "Then he will say: 'O Lord, admit me to Paradise.' He will say: 'Ask.' So he will ask. He will say: 'That is yours, and ten times its like, or thereabouts.' He will say: 'O Lord, are You mocking me?'" He said: "Then He will laugh until His uvula and molars are visible."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yahya ibn Ayyub informed me; "ḥ"; and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Rushdayn, all from Ziyad ibn Fa'id, from Sahl ibn Mu'adh, from his father, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "Whoever stands guard behind the Muslims in the cause of Allah voluntarily, and is not seized by a ruler for guard duty, will not see the Fire with his eye except for the tahillat al-qasam (the brief touch of the oath), for Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass through it﴾."

⁕ Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, saying: al-Zuhri informed me, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayra, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has three (children) who die, the Fire will not touch him except for the tahillat al-qasam," meaning: the wurud.

As for His saying ﴿It was a decree decided by your Lord﴾, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding its interpretation. Some of them said its meaning is: "It was a decree of your Lord, decreed."

Those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿hatman﴾: "Qada' (a decree)."

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿hatman maqdiyyan﴾: "Qada'."

Others said: rather, its meaning is: "It was an oath obligatory upon your Lord."

Those who said that:

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Amr Dawud ibn al-Zabarqan narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Suddi mention, from Murra al-Hamdani, from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding ﴿It was a decree decided by your Lord﴾: "An obligatory oath."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿It was a decree decided by your Lord﴾, he says: "An obligatory oath."

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: I have already set out the explanation of this matter.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verses 70–71 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of the words of the Exalted: ﴿Then We are most knowing of those most deserving of burning therein﴾ [19:70].

The Exalted says: Then We are more knowing of those among these who We drag out from every party, those most deserving of the severest punishment and most worthy of the greatest retribution.

It is related from Ibn Jurayj that he used to say about this:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿Then We are most knowing of those most deserving of burning therein﴾: "Most deserving of abiding eternally in Hell."

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: What Ibn Jurayj said is an opinion without meaning, because God the Exalted informed that those whom He drags out from every party of disbelievers are the most intense in their disbelief, and there is no doubt that no one who disbelieves in God is anything but eternally abiding in the Fire. So there is no sense in it, since all of them abide eternally in Hell, for it would be said: "Then We are most knowing of those who are most deserving of eternal abiding, out of these eternal abiders." But the meaning in this is what we have mentioned. It may also be that its meaning is: "Then We are most knowing of those who are most deserving of some of the levels of Hell to burn therein." The ṣaliyy (burning) is a verbal noun of ṣallaytu, tuṣallī, ṣaliyyan, and ṣaliyy is on the pattern fa'ūl, but its waw was changed to yā', and it was assimilated into the following yā', which is the lam of the verb, becoming a doubled yā'.

* *

The interpretation of the words of the Exalted: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it. That is ever, with your Lord, a decree that must be carried out﴾ [19:71].

The Exalted says: And there is none of you, O people, but will come upon Hell; it was, O Muhammad, a decree decided by your Lord, which He had decreed and made obligatory in the Mother of the Book.

The scholars differed regarding the meaning of "coming upon" (wurūd) which God mentioned in this place. Some of them said: it means entering.

Those who said that:

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn 'Uyayna informed us, from 'Amr, saying: One who heard Ibn 'Abbas debating Nafi' ibn al-Azraq told me: Ibn 'Abbas said: "Wurūd" means entering. Nafi' said: No. Ibn 'Abbas then recited: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are the fuel of Hell; you are to it bound to come﴾ [21:98]. "Is it coming or not? And He said: ﴿He will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection and lead them to the Fire, and wretched is the place to which they are led﴾ [11:98]. Is it coming or not? As for you and me, we will enter it. So see whether we come out of it or not. I do not think God will bring you out of it for your denial." He said: Nafi' laughed.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, who said: Abu Rashid al-Harūrī said: They mentioned this, and the Harūrī said: "They do not hear its hissing." Ibn 'Abbas said: "Woe to you! Are you mad? Where is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿He will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection and lead them to the Fire, and wretched is the place to which they are led﴾ and ﴿And We will drive the criminals to Hell in a thirsty herd﴾ [19:86], and His saying ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾? By God, if it were a supplication of those who passed away: 'O God, bring me out of the Fire safe, and admit me to Paradise victorious'..."

Ibn Jurayj said: He means: the wurūd mentioned by God in the Qur'an is entering. Everyone, pious and wicked, will come to it. In the Qur'an there are four instances of wurūd: ﴿He leads them to the Fire﴾, ﴿Indeed, you are to it bound to come﴾, ﴿And We will drive the criminals to Hell in a thirsty herd﴾, and His saying ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, His saying ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it, that is ever, with your Lord, a decree that must be carried out﴾: he means the pious and the wicked. Have you not heard the saying of God to Pharaoh: ﴿He will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection and lead them to the Fire, and wretched is the place to which they are led﴾, and He said ﴿And We will drive the criminals to Hell in a thirsty herd﴾? So He named the wurūd into the Fire "entering," though it is not "departing."

Al-Hasan ibn 'Arafa narrated to us, saying: Marwan ibn Mu'awiya narrated to us, from Bukayr ibn Abi Marwan, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, who said: The people of Paradise, after they had entered Paradise, said: Did our Lord not promise us the wurūd upon the Fire? He said: You have passed by it while it was extinguished.

Ibn 'Arafa said: Marwan ibn Mu'awiya said: Bukayr ibn Abi Marwan said, or he said: "motionless."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Marhum ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Imran al-Jawni narrated to me, from Abu Khalid, who said: A day will come when the earth will be fire; what have you prepared for it? He said: That is the saying of God: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it, that is ever, with your Lord, a decree that must be carried out. Then We will save those who were righteous and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees﴾ [19:72].

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, from al-Jurayri, from Abu al-Sulayl, from Ghunaym ibn Qays, who said: They mentioned the wurūd of the Fire, and Ka'b said: The Fire will be held for the people as if it were the fat of a sheep's hide, until the feet of creation, pious and wicked, stand upon it. Then a caller will call to it: "Hold back your companions and leave my companions." Then everyone who is its ally will be swallowed up, and it knows them better than a man knows his child, and the believers will emerge with their bodies moist. He said: Ka'b also said: Between the shoulders of the keeper of its guardians is a journey of a year, and each of them carries a staff with two prongs, with which he pushes once, and by it seven hundred thousand are cast into the Fire.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Malik ibn Mighwal, from Abu Ishaq, who said: When Abu Maysara went to his bed, he would say: "Would that my mother had not borne me," and then weep. It was said to him: "What makes you weep, Abu Maysara?" He said: "He told us that we will come upon it, and He did not tell us that we will depart from it."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Isma'il, from Qays, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Rawaha wept during his illness, and his wife wept. He said: "What makes you weep?" She said: "I saw you weeping, so I wept." Ibn Rawaha said: "I know that I will come upon the Fire, and I do not know whether I will be saved from it or not."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Amr Dawud ibn al-Zabarqan narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Suddi relate from Murra al-Hamdani, from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾: "He will enter it."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾: "He will enter it."

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ibn 'Uyayna, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Rawaha was resting his head in his wife's lap, and he wept, and his wife wept. He said: "What makes you weep?" She said: "I saw you weeping, so I wept." He said: "I remembered the saying of God: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾, and I do not know whether I will be saved from it or not."

Others said: Rather, it is passing over it.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾: he means Hell; the people pass over it.

Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾: "It is passing over it."

Khallad ibn Aslam narrated to us, saying: al-Nadr informed us, saying: Israel informed us, saying: Abu Ishaq informed us, from Abu al-Ahwas, from 'Abd Allah, regarding His saying ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾: "The Sirat over Hell is like the edge of a sword. The first tier passes like lightning, the second like the wind, the third like the best of horses, and the fourth like the best of beasts. Then they pass while the angels say: 'O God, grant safety, grant safety.'"

Others said: Rather, wurūd is entering, but it refers to the disbelievers, not the believers.

Those who said that:

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Sa'ib informed me, from a man who heard Ibn 'Abbas recite ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾, meaning the disbelievers: "No believer will enter it."

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn al-Walid al-Shanni narrated to us, saying: I heard 'Ikrima say: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾, meaning the disbelievers.

Others said: Rather, wurūd is general to every believer and disbeliever, except that the wurūd of the believer is passing by, and the wurūd of the disbeliever is entering.

Those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾: the wurūd of the Muslims is passing over the bridge in its midst, and the wurūd of the polytheists is entering it. He said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Those who slip and stumble that day are many, and two rows of angels surround the bridge, and their supplication that day is: O God, grant safety."

Others said: The wurūd of the believer is what befalls him in this world of fever and sickness.

Those who said that:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Uthman ibn al-Aswad, from Mujahid, who said: "Fever is the portion of every believer from the Fire," then he recited ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾.

Imran ibn Bakkar al-Kalla'i narrated to me, saying: Abu al-Mughira narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Tamim narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ went out to visit a man of his companions who had a fever, and I was with him. Then he said: "God says: It is My Fire, which I impose upon My believing servant, so that it may be his portion of the Fire in the Hereafter."

Others said: All of them will come to it, then the believers will depart from it by their deeds.

Those who said that:

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Shu'ba, who said: al-Suddi narrated to me, from Murra, from 'Abd Allah ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾: "They will come to it, then they will depart from it by their deeds."

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Murra, from 'Abd Allah, in similar words.

Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd al-Muharibi narrated to me, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik, from 'Ubayd Allah, from Mujahid, who said: I was with Ibn 'Abbas when a man called Abu Rashid, who was Nafi' ibn al-Azraq, came to him and said: "O Ibn 'Abbas, what do you say about the saying of God: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it, that is ever, with your Lord, a decree that must be carried out﴾?" He said: "As for you and me, O Abu Rashid, we will pass over it, so see whether we depart from it or not."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Zubayr informed us that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah being asked about the wurūd, and he said: "We will be on the Day of Resurrection upon a hillock or a height above the people. The nations will be called with their idols, and whatever each used to worship, first to last, will go forth with them, and they will follow it. Every hypocrite and believer will be given a light, and darkness will cover them, and then they will follow it. Upon the bridge of Hell are hooks that seize whomever God wills. The light of the hypocrite will be extinguished, and the believers will be saved. The first group will be saved like the full moon on the night of its fullness, seventy thousand with no reckoning for them, then those after them like the lights of a star in the sky, and so on. Then intercession will come, and they will intercede. Whoever said 'There is no god but God' and had in his heart a weight of a barleycorn of good will be brought out of the Fire. Then they will be met at the gate of Paradise, and the people of Paradise will pour water over them, and they will sprout like a seed in a flood. Then they will be asked, and they will be given this world and ten times its like."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn al-Mubarak, from al-Hasan, who said: A man said to his brother: "Has it reached you that you will come upon the Fire?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Has it reached you that you will depart from it?" He said: "No." He said: "Then why laugh?" It is said he was never seen laughing until he met God.

Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed us that Bukayr told him that he said to Busr ibn Sa'id: "So-and-so says that the wurūd of the Fire is standing over it." Busr said: "As for Abu Hurayra, I heard him say: 'When the Day of Resurrection comes, the people will gather, and a caller will call: Let every people join what they used to worship. So this one will go to the stone, this one to the horse, this one to the wood, until only those who worshipped God remain, and God will come to them. When they see Him, they will stand up toward Him, and He will take them and lead them onto the Sirat, and there are thorns on it. At that point intercession will be permitted, and the people will pass, and the prophets will say: O God, grant safety, grant safety.'" Bukayr said: Ibn 'Umayra used to say: "Saved and Muslim, and thrown headlong into Hell and torn, then saved."

The most correct of these opinions, in our view, is the opinion of those who said: all of them will come to it, then the believers will depart from it, and God will save them, and the disbelievers will plunge into it. Their wurūd is what is attested by the reports from the Messenger of God ﷺ regarding their passing over the Sirat set up on the back of Hell, so one is saved and another is thrown headlong into it.

Mention of the reports transmitted from the Messenger of God ﷺ on this: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, from Umm Mubashshir, the wife of Zayd ibn Haritha, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said while he was in the house of Hafsa: "No one who fought at Badr or al-Hudaybiya will enter the Fire." She said: Hafsa said: "O Messenger of God, does not God say: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾?" The Messenger of God said: "Hold on, [for] ﴿Then We will save those who were righteous﴾."

Al-Hasan ibn Mudrik narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Awana narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, from Umm Mubashshir, from the Messenger of God ﷺ, with the like of it.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, from Umm Mubashshir, from Hafsa, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "I truly hope that no one who fought at Badr or al-Hudaybiya will enter the Fire." She said: I said: "O Messenger of God, does not God say: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾?" He said: "Did you not hear Him say: ﴿Then We will save those who were righteous and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees﴾?"

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: 'Ubayd Allah ibn al-Mughira ibn Mu'aygib narrated to me, from Sulayman ibn 'Amr ibn 'Abd al-'Itwari, one of the Banu Layth, who had been raised in the care of Abu Sa'id, who said: I heard Abu Sa'id al-Khudri say: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: "The Sirat will be placed between the backs of Hell, with thorns like the thorns of al-sa'dan upon it. Then the people will seek to cross. Some are saved and unharmed, and some are saved but wounded by it, and some are held back and thrown headlong into it. When God has finished judging among the servants, the believers will look for men who were with them in the world, who prayed their prayer, paid their zakat, fasted their fasts, performed their pilgrimage, and fought their battles. They will say: 'O our Lord, servants of Yours were with us in the world, praying our prayer, paying our zakat, fasting our fasts, performing our pilgrimage, and fighting our battles, but we do not see them.' He will say: 'Go to the Fire, and whomever of them you find in it, bring him out.' They will find them, the Fire having seized them according to their deeds. Some of them the Fire has seized up to their feet, some up to the middle of their shins, some up to their knees, some up to their chests, some up to their necks, but it has not covered their faces. They will bring them out of it and cast them into the water of life." It was said: "What is the water of life, O Messenger of God?" He said: "The washing of the people of Paradise. They will sprout as a seed sprouts in the debris of a flood. Then the prophets will intercede for everyone who used to testify that there is no god but God sincerely, and they will bring them out of it. Then God, in His mercy, will have compassion upon those within it, and He will not leave in it any servant who has in his heart a weight of an atom's weight of faith, but He will bring him out of it."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verses 70–71 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam narrated to me, saying: My father and Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth narrated to us, from al-Layth ibn Khalid, from Yazid ibn Abi Hilal, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Bridge (al-Jisr) will be brought – meaning on the Day of Resurrection – and it will be placed between the back of Hell." We said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the Bridge?" He said: "It is slippery and unstable, upon it are hooks, claws, and a flattened thorn-bush with a crooked thorn, found in Najd, called al-Sa'dan. The believers will pass over it like the glance of an eye, like lightning, like the wind, and like the finest horses and riding camels. Some will be saved and unharmed, some will be scratched and saved, and some will be thrown into Hell. Then the last of them will pass, being dragged along. You are no more insistent in pleading with me for the truth which has become clear to you than the believers will be on that day before the Almighty, blessed and exalted, when they see that those (of their brothers) have been saved while their brothers remain."

⁕ Ahmad ibn Isa narrated to me, saying: Sa'id ibn Kathir ibn Ufayr narrated to us, saying: Ibn Lahi'a narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, who said: I asked Jabir ibn Abd Allah about the wurud (coming to the Fire), and he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "It is the entering. They will come to the Fire until they come out of it. The last one to remain will be a man on the Bridge, crawling. Allah will raise a tree for him." He said: "He will say: 'O Lord, bring me close to it.' So Allah, blessed and exalted, will bring him close to it." He said: "Then he will say: 'O Lord, admit me to Paradise.' He will say: 'Ask.' So he will ask. He will say: 'That is yours, and ten times its like, or thereabouts.' He will say: 'O Lord, are You mocking me?'" He said: "Then He will laugh until His uvula and molars are visible."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yahya ibn Ayyub informed me; "ḥ"; and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Rushdayn, all from Ziyad ibn Fa'id, from Sahl ibn Mu'adh, from his father, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "Whoever stands guard behind the Muslims in the cause of Allah voluntarily, and is not seized by a ruler for guard duty, will not see the Fire with his eye except for the tahillat al-qasam (the brief touch of the oath), for Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass through it﴾."

⁕ Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, saying: al-Zuhri informed me, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayra, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has three (children) who die, the Fire will not touch him except for the tahillat al-qasam," meaning: the wurud.

As for His saying ﴿It was a decree decided by your Lord﴾, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding its interpretation. Some of them said its meaning is: "It was a decree of your Lord, decreed."

Those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿hatman﴾: "Qada' (a decree)."

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿hatman maqdiyyan﴾: "Qada'."

Others said: rather, its meaning is: "It was an oath obligatory upon your Lord."

Those who said that:

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Amr Dawud ibn al-Zabarqan narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Suddi mention, from Murra al-Hamdani, from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding ﴿It was a decree decided by your Lord﴾: "An obligatory oath."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿It was a decree decided by your Lord﴾, he says: "An obligatory oath."

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: I have already set out the explanation of this matter.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 72:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then We will deliver those who feared Allah, and We will leave the wrongdoers therein kneeling.﴾ (72)

Exalted is He, mentioning: ﴿Then We will deliver﴾ from the Fire, after all of them have arrived at it, ﴿those who feared﴾ (alladhina ittaqaw), who feared Him by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions. ﴿And We will leave the wrongdoers therein kneeling.﴾ He, glorified is His praise, says: And We will leave those who wronged themselves, worshipping other than Allah, disobeying their Lord, and opposing His command and prohibition, in the Fire, kneeling (jithiyyan), meaning: crouching upon their knees.

Those whom the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have cited said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and We will leave the wrongdoers therein kneeling﴾: upon their knees.

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and We will leave the wrongdoers therein kneeling﴾: upon their knees.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and We will leave the wrongdoers therein kneeling﴾: "Al-juthiyy is the worst of sitting; a man does not sit kneeling except at a distress that befalls him."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Then We will deliver those who feared Allah, and We will leave the wrongdoers therein kneeling﴾: that people will come to Hell, and it is black and dark. As for the believers, their good deeds will light the way for them, so they will be saved from it. As for the disbelievers, their deeds will destroy them, and they will be held back by their sins.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 73:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who disbelieved say to those who believed: "Which of the two groups is better in station and finer in assembly?"﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿And when they are recited﴾ to the people ﴿Our verses﴾ which We sent down to Our Messenger Muhammad ﴿clear﴾, meaning manifest to whoever reflects upon them and contemplates them, that they are proofs of what Allah has made them proofs of for His servants. ﴿Those who disbelieved in Allah﴾, in His Book and His signs, and they are Quraysh, ﴿said to those who believed﴾, who affirmed it, and they are the Companions of Muhammad: ﴿"Which of the two groups is better in station"﴾. By "station" is meant the place of their residence, which is their dwellings and homes. ﴿And finer in assembly﴾, and this is the majlis (gathering place). It is said from it: "I gathered the people (nadawtu al-qawm) and I gather them (undu-hum) nadwan," meaning: when you gather them in a majlis. And it is said: "He is in the nadi (assembly) of his people and in their nadi," with the same meaning. And from the word nadi is the verse of Hatim:

"I was called among the people of the nadi, and they did not look at me with narrow eyes"
[[The line is by Hatim al-Ta'i, from his poetry in the book (Poets of Christianity: First Part, p. 115). In (Lisan: nada): al-nada is sitting together; nadaytuhu means I sat with him; tanadaw means they sat together in the nadi; al-nadi is the majlis, as long as they remain gathered in it; when they disperse from it, it is no longer a nadi. It is said: al-nadi is the people's gathering by day, on the authority of Kura'. Al-nadi is like al-nadi. Al-Tahdhib: al-nadi is the majlis, to which those around it gather; it is not called a nadi until its people are in it, and when they disperse it is not a nadi; it is al-nadi, and the plural is al-andiya. Ends. Al-khazar: plural of khazra', from al-khazar, which, as in (Lisan: khazar), is a natural squint of the eye. It is also said it is narrowness and smallness of the eye. It is also said it is a look as if it were in one of the two sides. Then he cited the line of Hatim, which the author cited as evidence that the meaning of nadi is the gathering of people.]]

The meaning of the speech is: "When Our clear verses are recited to them, those who disbelieved say to those who believed: which of the two groups, us or you, is wider in livelihood, more comfortable in ease, better in dwelling, finer in gathering, and more numerous in number and in those who attend the gathering: we or you?"

Those of the scholars of interpretation who said the same as what we have said include:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'ammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Zabyan, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿better in station and finer in assembly﴾: He said: "The station is the dwelling, and the nadi is the gathering."

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Shu'ba, from Sulayman, from Abu Zabyan, from Ibn Abbas, with the same.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who disbelieved say to those who believed: "Which of the two groups is better in station and finer in assembly"﴾: He said: "The station is the residence, and the nadi is the gathering, and the blessing and splendor in which they were." This is as Allah said to the people of Pharaoh, when He destroyed them and related their affair in the Qur'an, saying ﴿How many gardens and springs did they leave, and treasures and a noble station and blessings in which they had been delighted?﴾ So al-maqam is the residence and the bounty, and al-nadi is the gathering and assembly where they used to meet. And Allah said, regarding the matter of Lut, when He said ﴿and you commit the evil in your nadi﴾, and the Arabs call the gathering "al-nadi."

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿and finer in nadi﴾: he said: "a gathering."

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding Allah's saying ﴿which of the two groups﴾: he said: "Quraysh say it to the Companions of Muhammad ﷺ," ﴿and finer in nadi﴾: he said: "their gatherings; they say it too."

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, similarly.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who disbelieved say to those who believed: "Which of the two groups is better in station and finer in assembly"﴾: "They saw the Companions of Muhammad ﷺ in their living as roughness, and among them was austerity, so the people of polytheism alluded to them with what you hear."

* *

Regarding His saying ﴿and finer in nadi﴾:

He says: "a gathering."

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿which of the two groups is better in station and finer in nadi﴾: he said: "al-nadi is the gathering," and he recited the saying of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿then let him call his nadi﴾, and said: "his gathering."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 74:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And how many generations We destroyed before them, who were better in equipment and in appearance﴾

He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: And how many generations We destroyed, O Muhammad, before these disbelievers who say to the believers, when the verses of the Most Merciful are recited to them: "Which of the two groups is better in station and finer in assembly?" — generations that had more goods and dwellings than these, and were finer in appearance and more beautiful in form. So We destroyed their wealth and changed their forms. Among the poetry on this is the verse of 'Alqamah ibn 'Abdah:

*A bay horse the color of purple dye, I unfolded it [a garment] for sale in the box-chest of the cabinet...* [[The verse is by 'Alqamah ibn 'Abdah, the twenty-second verse of his ode that begins: *"You departed in distance, in no direction..."*

(Mukhtar al-Shi'r al-Jahili, Halabi edition with the commentary of Mustafa al-Saqqa, p. 436). In it, "al-ridaʾ" (the cloak) is used in place of al-riyy. Its commentator said: al-kumayt: a horse whose color is between black and red. Al-arjuwan: a deep, saturated red dye; here it means a red garment. Al-sawan: a cloth in which garments are kept, also called al-takht (chest). Al-mukaʿʿab here means garments with woven patterns, and it is a description of the cloak. It is also said that al-mukaʿʿab means folded and tied up; everything you fold is "kaʿʿabtu," and from this comes al-fataat al-kaʿib, the girl whose breasts have become firm and protruding. In Lisan al-'Arab (root r-'-y): al-riyy (on the pattern fa'il) and al-riyy (on the pattern fa'l, with the first letter vowelled with kasra) are a garment displayed for sale, according to 'Ali. The Tahdhib says: al-riyy, with a softened hamza, is a precious garment that is spread out so that its beauty may be seen.]] By al-sawan he means the chest in which garments are kept.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of interpretation) said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Those who said so:

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'ammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Zabyan, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿better in equipment and in appearance﴾: He said: al-riyy is the appearance, and al-athath is the goods.

* Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adiyy narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Sulayman, from Abu Zabyan, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: al-riyy is the appearance.

* 'Ali narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿better in equipment and in appearance﴾: he says: appearance.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿better in equipment and in appearance﴾: al-athath is wealth, and al-riyy is appearance.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Hawdhah narrated to us, saying: 'Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿equipment and appearance﴾: He said: al-athath is the best goods, and al-riyy: he said: wealth.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding the words of God, blessed and exalted, ﴿And how many generations We destroyed before them, who were better in equipment and in appearance﴾: i.e., more goods and better standing and station; so God destroyed their wealth and corrupted their forms upon them, blessed and exalted is He.

* al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿better in equipment and in appearance﴾: He said: better in forms and more in wealth.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿athathan﴾: he said: goods; ﴿wa-riyyan﴾: he said: in what people see.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similar to it.

* Ibn Humayd and Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, both saying: Jarir ibn Qabus narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: al-athath is wealth, and al-riyy is the fine appearance.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn 'Abbas, ﴿wa-riyyan﴾: appearance in color and beauty.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn 'Abbas, ﴿wa-riyyan﴾: appearance in color and beauty.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿better in equipment and in appearance﴾: He said: al-riyy is the appearance, and al-athath is the goods; better in goods and better in appearance.

* I was told from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say regarding His words ﴿better in equipment﴾: meaning wealth; ﴿and in appearance﴾: meaning fine appearance.

The readers differed in reading this. The majority of the readers of Medina recited "wa-riyyan" without hamza, and when read so it may be taken in two ways. First: the reciter intended the hamza, changed it into a yā', so the yā' that replaced the hamza and the yā' that is the third radical of the verb came together and were assimilated, becoming one doubled yā', in order to make it rhyme, since it is the end of a verse, with its counterparts among the other verse-endings before and after it. Second: that it derives from "rawiytu" (I quenched my thirst), "ruwiyatan wa-riyyan." When it is meant in this sense, the meaning of the speech is: how many generations We destroyed before them, who were better in goods and better in sight of their wealth and knowledge of its management, for the Arabs say: "How good is so-and-so's sight (ru'yah) in this matter," when he has good judgment in it and knowledge of it. The majority of the readers of Iraq, Kufa and Basra recited "wa-riʾyan" with hamza, meaning the sight of the eye, as if he intended: better in goods and appearance (mar'a). It is related from some of them that he read "athathan wa-zayyan" with a zay, as if he intended: better in goods, condition and appearance, for zayy is the condition and appearance, from their saying: "zayyaytu al-jariyah," meaning I adorned her and prepared her.

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the readings in this matter is the reading of the one who recites "athathan wa-riʾyan" with the rāʾ and the hamza, because the consensus of the authorities among the scholars of interpretation is that its meaning is appearance, and that this is from the sight of the eye, not from the thought (ru'yah), so the hamzated form is more fitting for it. If a reciter recites it without the hamza, intending this meaning, he is not mistaken in his recitation. As for the reading with the zay, it is an outlying reading, contrary to the readings of the readers, so I do not permit recitation with it because it contradicts their reading, although for it there is a sound interpretation.

The grammarians differed over whether al-athath is a collective or a singular noun. Al-Ahmar, as was related to me from him, used to say: it is a collective, whose singular is athathah, just as al-hamam is a collective whose singular is hamamah, and al-sahab is a collective whose singular is sahabah. As for al-Farra', he used to say: it has no singular, just as al-mata' has no singular. He said: the Arabs pluralize al-mata' as amti'ah, amatih, and mata'. He said: if you pluralized al-athath you would say: thalathat athhh and athath. As for al-riyy, its plural is ara'.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 75:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Whoever is in error, let the Most Merciful extend for him an extension, until, when they see what they are promised, either the punishment or the Hour, then they will know who is worse in position and weaker in soldiers.﴾ (19:75)

His saying, exalted is He, is addressed to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who deny their Lord, who say, when Our verses are recited to them, "Which of the two groups, ours or yours, is better in station and finer in assembly?": whoever among us and you is in error, deviating from the path of truth and following other than the way of guidance, then let the Most Merciful extend for him an extension. That is: let Allah prolong for him in his misguidance, and let him be given respite in it.

The scholars of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿whoever is in error, let the Most Merciful extend for him an extension﴾: Allah leaves him in his transgression.

And al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

And His saying: ﴿until, when they see what they are promised, either the punishment or the Hour﴾

His saying, exalted is He: Say to them, "Whoever among us and you is in error, then let the Most Merciful extend for him in his error until the command of Allah comes to them, either a punishment that hastens, or they meet their Lord at the rising of the Hour, which Allah has promised His creation to gather them for. So when the promise of Allah comes to them with one of these two matters, ﴿then they will know who is worse in position﴾, and in dwelling, among us and them, ﴿and weaker in soldiers﴾: whether they or you?" And at that time they will realize which of the two groups is better in station and finer in assembly.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 76:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah increases in guidance those who are guided. And the enduring good deeds are better in the sight of your Lord for reward and better for return.﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: Allah increases those who take the straight path (qasd al-mahajjah) and are guided to the way of rectitude (rushd), who believe in their Lord, affirm His signs, act upon what He has commanded them, and refrain from what He has forbidden them—increasing their guidance through the new faith that is renewed in them regarding the obligations He imposes upon them, acknowledging the necessity of their obligation upon them, and acting upon them. That is an increase from Allah in their being guided by His signs, a guidance upon their previous guidance. This is similar to His words: ﴿And whenever a surah is revealed, among them are those who say, "Which of you has this increased in faith?" As for those who believe, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice.﴾

Some of them interpreted it thus: "And Allah increases those who are guided in guidance" by means of the abrogating (nasikh) and abrogated (mansukh) parts of the Qur'an: they believe in the abrogating part just as they believed earlier in the abrogated part, and that is an increase of guidance from Allah upon their previous guidance.

﴿And the enduring good deeds are better in the sight of your Lord for reward﴾: He, exalted is His mention, says: The deeds that Allah commanded His servants and was pleased with from them—the enduring things for them, not the perishing ones—are better in the sight of your Lord as reward for their doers, ﴿and better for return﴾ to them than the stations of these polytheists who associate others with Allah, and their gatherings in which they boast over the people of faith in this world.

We have already explained the meaning of "the enduring good deeds," mentioned the disagreement of those who differ concerning it, and indicated the correct view on it earlier, in a manner sufficient to avoid repeating it in this place.

⁕ Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn Rashid informed us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) sat one day, took a dry stick, and shook off its leaves, then said: 'Indeed, the saying "There is no god but Allah," "Allah is greatest," "All praise is for Allah," and "Glory be to Allah" cause sins to fall away, just as the wind shakes off the leaves of this tree. Take them, O Abu al-Darda', before you are prevented from them. They are the enduring good deeds, and they are among the treasures of Paradise.'" Abu Salamah said: Whenever Abu al-Darda' mentioned this hadith, he would say: "I shall surely declare the oneness of Allah (la ilaha illa Allah), I shall surely magnify Allah (Allahu akbar), and I shall surely glorify Allah (subhan Allah)," until the ignorant person who saw me thought I was insane.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 19, verses 77–78:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our verses and said, "I will surely be given wealth and children"? (77) Has he looked into the unseen, or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful?﴾ (78)

His saying, exalted is His remembrance, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Have you seen﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿the one who disbelieved in Our verses﴾, meaning: Our proofs, so he did not affirm them, and he denied Our threat, from among the people of disbelief. ﴿And said﴾, while he was a disbeliever in God and in His Messenger: ﴿"I will surely be given"﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿wealth and children."﴾

It is mentioned that these verses were revealed concerning al-‘As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi, the father of ‘Amr ibn al-‘As.

Mention of the narration to that effect: Abu al-Sa'ib and Sa'id ibn Yahya narrated to us, both saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Muslim, from Masruq, from Khabbab, who said: "I was a blacksmith, and al-‘As ibn Wa'il owed me a debt. I came to him demanding it, and he said: 'By God, I will not pay you until you disbelieve in Muhammad.' I said: 'By God, I will not disbelieve in Muhammad until you die and are then resurrected.' He said: 'When I die and am resurrected as you say, I will come to you with wealth and children.'" He said: So God, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our verses and said, "I will surely be given wealth and children"? Has he looked into the unseen, or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful?﴾ ... up to His saying: ﴿and he will come to Us alone﴾.

⁕ Abu al-Sa'ib narrated it to me, and he recited in the hadith: "wa-waladan" (and children).

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ‘Abbas, that some men from the companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to seek payment of a debt from al-‘As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi. They came to him demanding it, and he said: "Do you not claim that in Paradise there is silver and gold, silk, and fruits of every kind?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then your promise is the Hereafter. By God, I will surely be given wealth and children, and I will surely be given the like of your book which you have brought." So God struck this example in the Qur'an, and said: ﴿Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our verses and said, "I will surely be given wealth"?﴾ ... up to His saying ﴿and he will come to Us alone﴾.

⁕ Muhammad ibn ‘Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu ‘Asim narrated to us, saying: ‘Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding God's saying ﴿I will surely be given wealth and children﴾, that he said: "Al-‘As ibn Wa'il says it."

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

⁕ Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our verses and said, "I will surely be given wealth and children"?﴾ He said: It was mentioned to us that some men from the companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) came to a man of the polytheists seeking payment of a debt. He said: "Does not your companion claim that in Paradise there is silk and gold?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then your appointment is Paradise. By God, I will not believe in your book which you have brought," mocking the Book of God, "and I will surely be given wealth and children." God says: ﴿Has he looked into the unseen, or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful?﴾

⁕ al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ‘Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, who said: Khabbab ibn al-Aratt said: "I was a blacksmith in Mecca, and I used to work for al-‘As ibn Wa'il, and dirhams had accumulated for me upon him. I came to demand them, and he said to me: 'I will not pay you until you disbelieve in Muhammad.' I said: 'I will not disbelieve in Muhammad until you die and are resurrected.' He said: 'When I am resurrected, I will have wealth and children.'" He said: "I mentioned that to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and God, blessed and exalted is He, revealed: ﴿Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our verses and said, "I will surely be given wealth and children"?﴾ up to ﴿and he will come to Us alone﴾."

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His saying ﴿wa-waladan﴾. The readers of Medina, Basra, and some of the people of Kufa recited ﴿waladan﴾ with a fatha on the waw, from walad (child), throughout the Qur'an, except that Abu ‘Amr ibn al-‘Ala' singled out the one in Surah Nuh with a damma, reciting it ﴿māluhu wa-wulduhu﴾. As for the majority of the readers of Kufa other than ‘Asim, they recited from this surah, from His saying ﴿mālan wa-waladan﴾ to the end of the surah, and the two in al-Zukhruf, and the one in Nuh, with a damma on the waw and sukun on the lam.

The people of Arabic grammar differed regarding the meaning of this when its waw is vowelled with a damma. Some of them said: the damma and the fatha have one meaning; they are simply two dialects, like their saying al-‘udm and al-‘adam, and al-huzn and al-hazan. In support of their view they cited the verse of the poet:

"So would that so-and-so had been in his mother's womb, and would that so-and-so had been the offspring (wuld) of a donkey."

[[The verse is cited in (Lisan al-‘Arab: w-l-d) without attribution. He said: "walad" and "wuld" are one, like "al-‘arab" and "al-‘urab," and "al-‘ajam" and "al-‘ujam," and the like. Al-Farra' recited: "fa-layta fulanan..." the verse. This is one. He said: Qays makes "wuld" a plural and "walad" (with vowel change) singular. Ibn al-Sikkit said: it is said of "walad" "al-walad" (with kasra on the first letter) and "la wald" (with damma on the first letter). He said: "wuld" (with damma on the first letter) may be singular and plural. He said: "wuld" may be the plural of "walad," like "asad" and "usd." (This is close to what the author transmitted from al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an.)]]

And al-Harith ibn Hilliza says:

"Indeed I have seen people who have multiplied wealth and wuld (children)..."

[[The verse is by al-Harith ibn Hilliza al-Yashkuri, and is among the witnesses in (Lisan al-‘Arab: w-l-d), like the preceding witness. Al-Farra' also cited it in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (Jami'a manuscript no. 24059, p. 195), then said: "walad" and "wuld" are two dialects, like what they said: "al-‘udm" and "al-‘adam."]]

And the verse of Ru'ba:

"Praise be to God, the Mighty, the Unique in His singularity, who has not taken from wuld of anything a wuld."

[[The two verses are by Ru'ba ibn al-‘Ajjaj, and they are from the rajaz meter. "Al-fard" means the one singular in lordship and in command apart from His creation, the one, the unique, who has no equal and no second. The author cited this verse with the two preceding witnesses, as evidence that "wuld" with damma on the waw and sukun on the lam means "walad" with fatha, and that it is singular, though it may come in the sense of a plural.]]

The Arabs say in a similar matter: "wulduki min dammā 'aqibayki" (your child from the blood of your two heels). He said: All of this is one, in the sense of "walad."

It has been mentioned to me that Qays makes "wuld" a plural and "walad" a singular.

Perhaps those who recited with a damma, in what they chose the damma for, recited it so in order to distinguish between the plural and the singular.

Abu Ja'far said: The view most correct in this matter, in my opinion, is that the fatha on the waw of "walad" and the damma on it have one meaning, and they are two dialects. Whichever of them the reciter reads, he is correct; however, the fatha is the more common of the two dialects, so reciting with it is more pleasing to me for that reason.

* *

He, mighty is His remembrance, says: Has this speaker of this statement known the knowledge of the unseen, so that he knows that he will have wealth and children in the Hereafter, through his looking into knowledge of what is hidden from him? ﴿Or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful?﴾ He says: Or has he believed in God and acted upon what He commanded, and refrained from what He forbade, so that he has thereby a covenant with God that He will give him what he says of wealth and children?

As:
