And His saying ﴿Has he looked into the unseen﴾

He, mighty is His remembrance, says: Has this speaker of this statement known the knowledge of the unseen, so that he knows that he will have wealth and children in the Hereafter, through his looking into knowledge of what is hidden from him? ﴿Or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful?﴾ He says: Or has he believed in God and acted upon what He commanded, and refrained from what He forbade, so that he has thereby a covenant with God that He will give him what he says of wealth and children?

As:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿Has he looked into the unseen, or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful?﴾ — "by a righteous deed he sent forward."

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿Nay, We shall record what he says, and We shall extend for him the extension of punishment﴾ [19:79] and ﴿We shall inherit from him what he says, and he will come to Us alone﴾ [19:80].

He, may His remembrance be exalted, means by His saying ﴿Nay﴾: the matter is not as he claims. He did not look into the unseen so as to know the truth of what he says and the reality of what he mentions, nor did he take a covenant with the Most Merciful by believing in God and His Messenger and acting in obedience to Him. Rather, he lied and disbelieved. Then He, may His remembrance be exalted, said ﴿We shall record what he says﴾, meaning: We shall record what this disbeliever in his Lord says, the one who said ﴿I will surely be given wealth and children﴾ [19:77] in the Hereafter. ﴿And We shall extend for him the extension of punishment﴾ means: We shall increase him in punishment in Hell for his speaking falsehood and vanity in the world, in addition to his punishment for his disbelief in God.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and We shall inherit from him what he says﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We shall strip this speaker, who said "I will surely be given wealth and children" in the Hereafter, of his wealth and children, and what he has of wealth and children will become Ours to the exclusion of him. ﴿And he will come to Us alone﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, alone, with no wealth and no children with him.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation, tafsir) have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿and We shall inherit from him what he says﴾: his wealth and children. And that is what al-'As ibn Wa'il said.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿and We shall inherit from him what he says and he will come to Us alone﴾: he will have no wealth and no children.

* al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿and We shall inherit from him what he says﴾, he said: what he has, and that is His saying ﴿I will surely be given wealth and children﴾. And in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "and We shall inherit from him what he has."

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and We shall inherit from him what he says﴾, he said: what he gathered of the world and what he did in it. ﴿And he will come to Us alone﴾, he said: alone of that, with nothing of it following him, neither little nor much.

* 'Ali narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿and We shall inherit from him what he says﴾: "We shall inherit him [[Thus also in Ibn Kathir. What is in al-Durr from Ibn 'Abbas is: "and We shall inherit from him what there will be": his wealth and children.]]

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿Nay, We shall record what he says, and We shall extend for him the extension of punishment﴾ [19:79] and ﴿We shall inherit from him what he says, and he will come to Us alone﴾ [19:80].

He, may His remembrance be exalted, means by His saying ﴿Nay﴾: the matter is not as he claims. He did not look into the unseen so as to know the truth of what he says and the reality of what he mentions, nor did he take a covenant with the Most Merciful by believing in God and His Messenger and acting in obedience to Him. Rather, he lied and disbelieved. Then He, may His remembrance be exalted, said ﴿We shall record what he says﴾, meaning: We shall record what this disbeliever in his Lord says, the one who said ﴿I will surely be given wealth and children﴾ [19:77] in the Hereafter. ﴿And We shall extend for him the extension of punishment﴾ means: We shall increase him in punishment in Hell for his speaking falsehood and vanity in the world, in addition to his punishment for his disbelief in God.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and We shall inherit from him what he says﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We shall strip this speaker, who said "I will surely be given wealth and children" in the Hereafter, of his wealth and children, and what he has of wealth and children will become Ours to the exclusion of him. ﴿And he will come to Us alone﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, alone, with no wealth and no children with him.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation, tafsir) have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

And that is what al-'As ibn Wa'il said.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿and We shall inherit from him what he says and he will come to Us alone﴾: he will have no wealth and no children.

* al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿and We shall inherit from him what he says﴾, he said: what he has, and that is His saying ﴿I will surely be given wealth and children﴾. And in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "and We shall inherit from him what he has."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 81–82:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And they have taken gods besides Allah, that they may be for them a source of might﴾ [81] ﴿No! They will reject their worship of them, and they will be opposed to them﴾ [82]

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: And the polytheists among your people, O Muhammad, have taken gods besides Allah to worship, so that these gods may be for them a source of might, protecting them from the punishment of Allah and securing for them a nearness to Allah through their worship of them. As for His saying ﴿No!﴾, He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: The matter is not as they supposed and hoped regarding these gods they worship besides Allah, namely that they would rescue them from the punishment of Allah and deliver them from it, and from any evil which their Lord might intend for them.

* *

His saying: ﴿They will reject their worship of them﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Rather, on the Day of Resurrection the gods will reject the worship of these polytheists of them, and their rejection of it will be their saying to their Lord: "We disown You; they did not worship us" (cf. Qur'an 28:63). They will deny that they had worshipped them or commanded them to do so, and will disassociate themselves from them. That is their rejection of their worship.

As for His saying ﴿and they will be opposed to them﴾, the People of Interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed in its interpretation. Some of them said: its meaning is: "and their gods will be helpers against them." They said: al-didd (opposed) means al-'awn (helper).

Mention of those who said this:

* Ali related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿and they will be opposed to them﴾: he said: "Helpers."

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us [transmission marker "ḥ"]; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and they will be opposed to them﴾: he said: "Helpers against them, disputing with them and denying them."

* al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and they will be opposed to them﴾: he said: "Their idols on the Day of Resurrection, in the Fire."

Others said: rather, by al-didd in this place is meant "companions (qurana')."

Mention of those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿and they will be opposed to them﴾: he said: "They will be companions to them."

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿opposed﴾: "Companions in the Fire, cursing one another and disowning one another."

* al-Hasan related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿opposed﴾: he said: "Companions in the Fire."

Others said: the meaning of al-didd here is "enemies (al-'aduww)."

Mention of those who said this:

* It was narrated to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿and they will be opposed to them﴾: he said: "Enemies."

Others said: the meaning of al-didd in this place is "affliction (bala')."

Mention of those who said this:

* Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿and they will be opposed to them﴾: he said: "They will be an affliction upon them."

Al-didd means affliction, and in the speech of the Arabs al-didd means opposition. It is said: "So-and-so opposes (yadadd) so-and-so in such-and-such a matter," when he contradicts him in his conduct, undoing what he has done right and correcting what he has spoiled. Since that is its meaning, and since the gods of these polytheists, whom Allah mentions in this place, will disown them and disclaim them on that day, they become opponents to them, and so they are described accordingly.

Some grammarians of Basra said: it is used in the singular because it can refer to a group or to an individual, like al-rasad and al-arsad (the watchers / watchers in the plural); he said: al-rasad may also be used for a group. Some grammarians of Kufa said: it is singular because its meaning is "helper (al-'awn)." He mentioned that Abu Nuhayk used to recite it that way.

**On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿On the Day We shall gather the God-fearing to the Most Merciful as a delegation (wafdan)﴾ (19:85) and ﴿We shall drive the criminals to Hell as thirsty herds (wirdan)﴾ (19:86)**

He, the Exalted, says: On the Day We gather those who were mindful of God in this world, who feared His punishment and therefore avoided His disobedience and performed His obligations, to their Lord, ﴿as a delegation (wafdan)﴾. By *wafd* is meant riders. It is said: "I went to so-and-so (wafadtu 'ala fulan)" when I came to him, and "the people sent a delegation (awfada al-qawm wafdan) to their commander" when they dispatched a group ahead of them. The word *wafd* in this context is used in the sense of a collective, but it is singular, because it is the verbal noun (masdar) of their singular *wafid* (one who comes as a delegate). The plural of *wafd* may also be *wufud*, as one of the Banu Hanifa said:

*Indeed I am one who praises him, but what will he do?*
*The chief of the delegations is Muzahim ibn Jassas.*

[The verse is by one of the Banu Hanifa, as the author says. In Taj al-Arus (under j-th-th: Jassas, on the pattern of Kitab, is the son of Nashba ibn Rabi' al-Taymi, the son of 'Amr ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Lu'ayy ibn 'Amr ibn al-Harith ibn Taym ibn 'Abd Manat ibn Ud: he is the ancestor of a tribe; from his descendants is Muzahim ibn Zafar ibn 'Ilaj ibn al-Harith ibn 'Amr ibn Jassas, who narrated from Shu'ba, from whom Abu al-Rabi' al-Zahrani transmitted, and his brother 'Uthman ibn Zafar, who narrated from Yusuf ibn Musa al-Qattan and others. In Khulasat Tadhhib Tahdhib al-Kamal by al-Khazraji: Muzahim ibn Zafar ibn al-Harith al-Kufi, from 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz; and from him Shu'ba and Sufyan transmitted; Ibn Ma'in deemed him trustworthy. In Lisan al-'Arab (under w-f-d): God the Exalted said: "On the Day We gather the God-fearing to the Most Merciful as a delegation." It has been said: *al-wafd* are the honoured riders... and they are the *wafd* and the *wufud*. As for *wafd*, it is a noun of collective meaning, and it has been said it is a plural. As for *wufud*, it is the plural of *wafid*... and the plural of *wafd* is *awfad* and *wufud*.]

The *wufud* in this place may also be the plural of *wafid*, just as *julus* is the plural of *jalis* (sitter).

The commentators (ahl al-ta'wil) have said things similar to what we have said.

**Those who said that:**

- Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'ida narrated to me, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from al-Nu'man ibn Sa'd, from 'Ali, regarding His words ﴿On the Day We gather the God-fearing to the Most Merciful as a delegation﴾, he said: By God, the delegation is not gathered on foot, nor are they driven. Rather, they will be brought camels the like of which creation has never seen, with saddles of gold, and their reins of chrysolite (zabarjad), and they will ride them until they knock on the gates of Paradise.

- Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Shu'ba, from Isma'il, from a man, from Abu Hurayra, regarding ﴿On the Day We gather the God-fearing to the Most Merciful as a delegation﴾, he said: upon camels.

- 'Ali narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to us, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿On the Day We gather the God-fearing to the Most Merciful as a delegation﴾, he said: riders.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Bashir narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Qays al-Mala'i narrated to us, saying: When the believer comes out of his grave, a person of the most beautiful form and the sweetest scent will meet him, and he will say: "Do you know me?" He will say: "No, except that God has made your scent sweet and your form beautiful." He will say: "Thus you were in the world: I am your righteous deed, which you used to ride much in the world; so ride me today." And he recited ﴿On the Day We gather the God-fearing to the Most Merciful as a delegation﴾.

- al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿to the Most Merciful as a delegation﴾, he said: a delegation to Paradise.

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His words ﴿On the Day We gather the God-fearing to the Most Merciful as a delegation﴾, he said: upon noble she-camels.

**On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿On the Day We shall gather the God-fearing to the Most Merciful as a delegation (wafdan)﴾ (19:85) and ﴿We shall drive the criminals to Hell as thirsty herds (wirdan)﴾ (19:86)**

He, the Exalted, says: On the Day We gather those who were mindful of God in this world, who feared His punishment and therefore avoided His disobedience and performed His obligations, to their Lord, ﴿as a delegation (wafdan)﴾. By *wafd* is meant riders. It is said: "I went to so-and-so (wafadtu 'ala fulan)" when I came to him, and "the people sent a delegation (awfada al-qawm wafdan) to their commander" when they dispatched a group ahead of them. The word *wafd* in this context is used in the sense of a collective, but it is singular, because it is the verbal noun (masdar) of their singular *wafid* (one who comes as a delegate). The plural of *wafd* may also be *wufud*, as one of the Banu Hanifa said:

*Indeed I am one who praises him, but what will he do?*
*The chief of the delegations is Muzahim ibn Jassas.*

[The verse is by one of the Banu Hanifa, as the author says. In Taj al-Arus (under j-th-th: Jassas, on the pattern of Kitab, is the son of Nashba ibn Rabi' al-Taymi, the son of 'Amr ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Lu'ayy ibn 'Amr ibn al-Harith ibn Taym ibn 'Abd Manat ibn Ud: he is the ancestor of a tribe; from his descendants is Muzahim ibn Zafar ibn 'Ilaj ibn al-Harith ibn 'Amr ibn Jassas, who narrated from Shu'ba, from whom Abu al-Rabi' al-Zahrani transmitted, and his brother 'Uthman ibn Zafar, who narrated from Yusuf ibn Musa al-Qattan and others. In Khulasat Tadhhib Tahdhib al-Kamal by al-Khazraji: Muzahim ibn Zafar ibn al-Harith al-Kufi, from 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz; and from him Shu'ba and Sufyan transmitted; Ibn Ma'in deemed him trustworthy. The interpretation of His saying, ﴿They will not have power of intercession, except for one who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful﴾ [19:87]

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: those who disbelieve in their Lord, O Muhammad, will not possess intercession on the Day when Allah gathers the God-fearing to Him as a delegation. This is when the people of faith intercede for one another with Allah, so that some of them intercede for others. ﴿Except for one among them who has taken with the Most Merciful﴾ in this world ﴿a covenant﴾ through faith in Him, affirming His Messenger, acknowledging what he brought, and acting on what he was commanded.

As follows:

⁕ Ali narrated to me, he said: Abdullah narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying, ﴿except for one who has taken with the Most Merciful a covenant﴾: He said: "The covenant is the testimony that there is no god but Allah, and disowning to Allah any power or strength, and hoping in none but Allah."

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying, ﴿They will not have power of intercession, except for one who has taken with the Most Merciful a covenant﴾: He said: "On that day the believers will be intercessors for one another. ﴿Except for one who has taken with the Most Merciful a covenant﴾" He said: "Righteous deeds."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying, ﴿They will not have power of intercession, except for one who has taken with the Most Merciful a covenant﴾: That is, through obedience to Him. And in another verse He said, ﴿No intercession will benefit except for one whom the Most Merciful has permitted and whose word He approves﴾ [20:109], so that they may know that on the Day of Resurrection Allah intercedes for believers on behalf of one another. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "Indeed, among my nation is a man through whose intercession Allah will admit more people into Paradise than the tribe of Banu Tamim." And we used to narrate that a martyr intercedes for seventy of his family members.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, from Abu al-Malih, from Awf ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed my intercession is for whoever dies among my nation without associating anything with Allah."

As for "man" (مَن) in His saying, ﴿except for one (إلا مَنْ)﴾, it is in the accusative position as an exception (istithna', grammatical exception). It cannot be in the genitive by the preposition of the lam (lam, the particle), but it may be accusative in speech in other contexts. This is like the saying of a speaker: "I intended to pass by today, except the enemy, for I do not pass by him," where the enemy is excepted from the meaning. But this is not so in His saying, ﴿They will not have power of intercession, except for one who has taken with the Most Merciful a covenant﴾, because the meaning of the speech is: these disbelievers will not possess intercession except for one who believed in Allah. The believers are not among the number of the disbelievers. As for the one who reads it in the accusative with the meaning, "except for the one who has taken with the Most Merciful a covenant," then it should be made that His saying, "they will not have power of intercession," refers to the God-fearing, so the meaning of the speech becomes: on the day We gather the God-fearing to the Most Merciful as a delegation, they will not possess intercession, except for the one who has taken with the Most Merciful a covenant. Its meaning at that point is: except for the one who has taken with the Most Merciful a covenant. But if "they will not have power of intercession" is taken as a report about the criminals, then "man" would be in the accusative as a disconnected exception (istithna' munqati', an exception not of the same category as what precedes it), so the meaning of the speech is: they will not possess intercession, but the one who has taken with the Most Merciful a covenant possesses it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 88–90:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Certainly you have produced something monstrous. The heavens are almost rent apart from it, and the earth is split open, and the mountains collapse in ruin﴾

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: "And these disbelievers in Allah said, ﴿The Most Merciful has taken a son. Certainly you have produced something monstrous﴾," He, exalted is His remembrance, says to those among His creatures who say this: "Certainly you have produced, O people, a great thing, an abominable utterance."

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the like of what we have said.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Certainly you have produced a monstrous thing﴾, he said: "Certainly you have produced a great thing, and it is the abominable utterance."

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿shay'an idda﴾, he said: "Great."

- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

- al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿shay'an idda﴾, he said: "Great."

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Certainly you have produced a monstrous thing﴾, he said: "You have produced a great matter when they ascribed a son to the Most Merciful."

As for *idd* (إدّ), there are three dialectal readings. It is said: *laqad ji'ta shay'an iddan* with a kasra on the alif, *iddan* with a fatha on the alif, and *adan* with a fatha on the alif and a long vowel, in the pattern of *madd*, form *fa'il*. The readers of the major cities recited it thus, and by it we recite. It is related from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami that he recited it with a fatha on the alif, but I do not consider his reading so, since it contradicts the reading of the readers of the cities. The Arabs say of every great matter: *idd*, *imr*, and *nukr*. From this is the saying of the rajiz (rajaz poet):

*Qad laqiya al-a'da'u minni nukra... dahiyatun dahya'a idda imra*

[These are two verses of rajaz (mashtur al-rajaz), the poet's citation of which was previously mentioned at His saying in Surah al-Kahf (18:74), "You have certainly produced a monstrous thing." We explained them there.]

From this is the saying of another:

*Fi lahathin minhu wa hathlin iddan*

[This is a verse of rajaz whose speaker I do not know. *Al-lahath* and *al-lahath* is the heat of thirst in the belly. In *al-Lisan* (lahatha), Ibn Sida said: the dog lahatha, with fatha, and lahatha yalhathu in both, lahthan: he extended his tongue from the intensity of thirst and heat, and likewise a bird when it extends its tongue from heat or thirst. *Lahatha al-rajul* and *lahatha* (with fatha on the first and kasra on the second) yalhathu (with fatha) in both dialects, lahthan, fa-huwa lahthan: he was exhausted. As for *al-hathl*, I did not find in the lexicons under the root h-th-l a meaning suited to the verse, and perhaps it is a corruption of *al-khabl*, which is the corruption of the limbs, or of *al-khatl*, which is deceiving someone while they are heedless, and perhaps the rajiz describes a hunting dog or a horse. As for *al-idd*, it is wonder and a dreadful matter; and it is the point of evidence in the author's speech, like the two verses before it.]

And His saying ﴿The heavens are almost rent apart from it﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says:

The heavens almost split apart into pieces from their utterance ﴿The Most Merciful has taken a son﴾. From this it is said: "We were split by it," when it is torn asunder.

The people of interpretation have said the like of what we have said.

Those who said this:

- Ali related to me, saying: Abdullah related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿The heavens are almost rent apart from it, and the earth is split open, and the mountains collapse in ruin, that they ascribed to the Most Merciful a son﴾, he said: "Because of shirk, the heavens, the earth, the mountains, and all creation were terrified, except the two weighty ones (jinn and humans), and they were almost about to cease to exist from the greatness of Allah. Just as with shirk the goodness of the mushrik does not benefit him, so too we hope that Allah forgives the sins of the monotheists." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Instruct your dying with the testimony that there is no god but Allah; whoever says it at his death, Paradise is due to him." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what of one who says it in his health?" He said: "That is more binding and more binding." Then he said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, if the heavens and the earths, and whatever is in them, between them, and beneath them, were brought and placed in one pan of a scale, and the testimony that there is no god but Allah were placed in the other pan, it would outweigh them."

- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿The heavens are almost rent apart from it, and the earth is split open, and the mountains collapse in ruin﴾: it was mentioned to us that Ka'b used to say: "The angels became angry, and Hell blazed, when they said what they said."

And His saying: ﴿And the earth is split open﴾

He says: The earth almost split open and was cleft from that ﴿and the mountains collapse in ruin﴾. He says: the mountains almost fell, some upon others, in collapse. *Al-hadd* is the falling, and it is a verbal noun of *hadadtu*, so I *ahuddu hadda*.

The people of interpretation have said the like of what we have said.

Those who said this:

- Ali related to me, saying: Abdullah related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿and the mountains collapse in ruin﴾, he said: "Demolishing."

- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said, regarding ﴿and the mountains collapse in ruin﴾: "The hadd is the swooping down."

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and the mountains collapse in ruin﴾, he said: "In anger for Allah." He said: "Indeed these people who ascribed this to Allah, the heavens, the earth, and the mountains became angry because of their saying. He had asked them to repent and called them to repentance, saying: ﴿Certainly those who said, 'Allah is the third of three,' have disbelieved﴾ — they said: He, his consort, and his son; they made them two gods alongside Him — ﴿and there is no god but One God﴾ ... to His saying: ﴿and they seek His forgiveness, and Allah is Forgiving, Merciful﴾."

- Ali related to me, saying: Abdullah related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿and the mountains collapse in ruin﴾, he said: "Demolishing."

- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said, regarding ﴿and the mountains collapse in ruin﴾: "The hadd is the swooping down."

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and the mountains collapse in ruin﴾, he said: "In anger for Allah." He said: "Indeed these people who ascribed this to Allah, the heavens, the earth, and the mountains became angry because of their saying. He had asked them to repent and called them to repentance, saying: ﴿Certainly those who said, 'Allah is the third of three,' have disbelieved﴾ — they said: He, his consort, and his son; they made them two gods alongside Him — ﴿and there is no god but One God﴾ ... to His saying: ﴿and they seek His forgiveness, and Allah is Forgiving, Merciful﴾."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 88–90:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Certainly you have produced something monstrous. The heavens are almost rent apart from it, and the earth is split open, and the mountains collapse in ruin﴾

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: "And these disbelievers in Allah said, ﴿The Most Merciful has taken a son. Certainly you have produced something monstrous﴾," He, exalted is His remembrance, says to those among His creatures who say this: "Certainly you have produced, O people, a great thing, an abominable utterance."

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the like of what we have said.

Those who said this:

- Ali related to me, saying: Abdullah related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿shay'an idda﴾, he said: "A grave utterance."

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Certainly you have produced a monstrous thing﴾, he said: "Certainly you have produced a great thing, and it is the abominable utterance."

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿shay'an idda﴾, he said: "Great."

- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

- al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿shay'an idda﴾, he said: "Great."

As for *idd* (إدّ), there are three dialectal readings. It is said: *laqad ji'ta shay'an iddan* with a kasra on the alif, *iddan* with a fatha on the alif, and *adan* with a fatha on the alif and a long vowel, in the pattern of *madd*, form *fa'il*. The readers of the major cities recited it thus, and by it we recite. It is related from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami that he recited it with a fatha on the alif, but I do not consider his reading so, since it contradicts the reading of the readers of the cities. The Arabs say of every great matter: *idd*, *imr*, and *nukr*. From this is the saying of the rajiz (rajaz poet):

*Qad laqiya al-a'da'u minni nukra... dahiyatun dahya'a idda imra*

[These are two verses of rajaz (mashtur al-rajaz), the poet's citation of which was previously mentioned at His saying in Surah al-Kahf (18:74), "You have certainly produced a monstrous thing." We explained them there.]

From this is the saying of another:

*Fi lahathin minhu wa hathlin iddan*

[This is a verse of rajaz whose speaker I do not know. *Al-lahath* and *al-lahath* is the heat of thirst in the belly. In *al-Lisan* (lahatha), Ibn Sida said: the dog lahatha, with fatha, and lahatha yalhathu in both, lahthan: he extended his tongue from the intensity of thirst and heat, and likewise a bird when it extends its tongue from heat or thirst. *Lahatha al-rajul* and *lahatha* (with fatha on the first and kasra on the second) yalhathu (with fatha) in both dialects, lahthan, fa-huwa lahthan: he was exhausted. As for *al-hathl*, I did not find in the lexicons under the root h-th-l a meaning suited to the verse, and perhaps it is a corruption of *al-khabl*, which is the corruption of the limbs, or of *al-khatl*, which is deceiving someone while they are heedless, and perhaps the rajiz describes a hunting dog or a horse. As for *al-idd*, it is wonder and a dreadful matter; and it is the point of evidence in the author's speech, like the two verses before it.]

* *

And His saying ﴿The heavens are almost rent apart from it﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says:

The heavens almost split apart into pieces from their utterance ﴿The Most Merciful has taken a son﴾. From this it is said: "We were split by it," when it is torn asunder.

The people of interpretation have said the like of what we have said.

Those who said this:

- Ali related to me, saying: Abdullah related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿The heavens are almost rent apart from it, and the earth is split open, and the mountains collapse in ruin, that they ascribed to the Most Merciful a son﴾, he said: "Because of shirk, the heavens, the earth, the mountains, and all creation were terrified, except the two weighty ones (jinn and humans), and they were almost about to cease to exist from the greatness of Allah. Just as with shirk the goodness of the mushrik does not benefit him, so too we hope that Allah forgives the sins of the monotheists." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Instruct your dying with the testimony that there is no god but Allah; whoever says it at his death, Paradise is due to him." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what of one who says it in his health?" He said: "That is more binding and more binding." Then he said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, if the heavens and the earths, and whatever is in them, between them, and beneath them, were brought and placed in one pan of a scale, and the testimony that there is no god but Allah were placed in the other pan, it would outweigh them."

- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿The heavens are almost rent apart from it, and the earth is split open, and the mountains collapse in ruin﴾: it was mentioned to us that Ka'b used to say: "The angels became angry, and Hell blazed, when they said what they said."

He says: The earth almost split open and was cleft from that ﴿and the mountains collapse in ruin﴾. He says: the mountains almost fell, some upon others, in collapse. *Al-hadd* is the falling, and it is a verbal noun of *hadadtu*, so I *ahuddu hadda*.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 91–93:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿That they attribute to the Most Merciful a son﴾ (91) ﴿And it is not befitting for the Most Merciful to take a son﴾ (92) ﴿There is none in the heavens and the earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant﴾ (93)

His saying, may He be remembered: "The mountains are about to collapse in pieces because they attribute to the Most Merciful a son." The particle "an" (that) is in the accusative position according to some grammarians, since it is joined to the verb, and according to others it is in the genitive position through the omitted preposition. We have already explained the correct view on this in more than one place in this book, in a way that makes repeating it here unnecessary.

As for His saying ﴿an da'aw lil-Rahmani waladan﴾ (that they attribute to the Most Merciful a son), the meaning of "da'aw" (attribute) is: that they made for Him a son, as the poet said:

"Ala rubba man tad'u nasihan wa in taghib ... tajiduhu bi-ghaybin ghayra muntasihi al-sadr" [[See the explanation of this witness together with the explanation of the one following it.]]

And Ibn Ahmar said:

"Ahwa laha mishqasan hashran fa-shabraqaha ... wa kuntu ad'u qadhaha al-ithmida al-qarada" [[(1) The verse is in (Lisan: da'a). It is attributed to Ibn Ahmar al-Bahili. He said: "da'awtuhu bi-Zayd" means "I named him with it (dau'tuhu iyyahu: I named him)," the verb being transitive after dropping the preposition; Ibn Ahmar al-Bahili said: "Ahwa laha..." the verse, meaning: I name it, and he intended: "Ahwa laha bi-mishqas," so he dropped the preposition and the verb reached its object. The saying of the Mighty and Majestic, "that they attribute to the Most Merciful a son," means: that they made. He also recited Ibn Ahmar's verse and said: meaning, I used to make and name; and similar to it is the saying of the poet: "Ala rubba man tad'u tasihan... the verse." The mishqas (arrow-head) among arrows is what is long and not broad; if it is broad, it is al-mi'bala. A hashr arrow is one whose feathers are even and smooth, and every fine, delicate thing is hashr. "Shabraqaha": he tore it apart; it is said: a "mushabraq" garment is one cut and torn. In the book "al-Ma'ani al-Kabir" by Ibn Qutaybah (printed in Hyderabad, p. 988) it says: he says: I, in my solicitude over her, used to name what would harm her a speck of dust, so how about what would injure her. His saying "ad'u" means "usammi" (I name); you say: "What do you call this among you?" meaning: what do you name it? The hashr is a light-feathered arrow whose shaft and feathers are tightly bound. Al-ithmid is black kohl, and al-qarad is that which gets lodged in the eye; it is also said: al-qarad is that whose parts stick together. The meaning: you used to name black kohl a speck, out of your caution regarding her.]]

* *

As for His saying ﴿wa ma yanbaghi lil-Rahmani an yattakhidha waladan﴾ (and it is not befitting for the Most Merciful to take a son):

It means: it is not fitting for God to take a son, because He is not like the creatures who are overcome by desires, and whose delights compel them to intercourse with females; and no child comes into being except from a female, while God is exalted above being like His creation. This is like the verse of Ibn Ahmar:

"Fi ra'si khalqa'a min hanqa'a mushrifatin ... ma yanbaghi dunaha sahlun wa la jabal" [[This verse was cited earlier in this volume, p. 84, and we explained it there.]]

The meaning: it is not suitable and cannot be.

﴿in kullu man fi al-samawati wal-ardi illa atil-Rahmani abdan﴾ means: there is none among all who are in the heavens, of the angels, and in the earth, of mankind, humans and jinn, ﴿but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant﴾, meaning: but that he comes to his Lord on the Day of Resurrection as His servant, humbled, submissive, acknowledging his servitude to Him, with no kinship between him and Him.

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Certainly He has enumerated them and counted them with an exact counting (94). And each of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone (95).﴾

He, the Exalted, says: Certainly the Most Merciful has enumerated all His creation and counted them with an exact counting, so the extent of all of them is not hidden from Him, and He knows their number, so not one of them escapes Him. ﴿And each of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone⦈ means: all of His creation will come before Him on the day the Hour is established, alone and solitary, with no helper from Allah and no one to defend him, and Allah will decree concerning him what He decrees and do with him what He does.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 96–97:

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection﴾ [Q. 19:96] ﴿So We have only made it easy in your tongue that you may give good tidings thereby to the righteous and warn thereby a people hostile [in opposition]﴾ [Q. 19:97].

His saying, Exalted is His remembrance: Indeed, those who believed in Allah and His messengers, and affirmed what came to them from their Lord, and acted upon it, so they made lawful what He made lawful and made unlawful what He made unlawful, ﴿the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection﴾ in this world, in the hearts of His believing servants.

And in accordance with what we have said on this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said that:

• Yahya ibn Talha narrated to me, he said: Shurayk narrated to us, from Muslim al-Mala'i, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection﴾ he said: love among the people in this world.

• Ali narrated to me, he said: Abd Allah narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection﴾ he said: love (hubban).

• Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection﴾ he said: affection from the Muslims in this world, good provision, and truthful tongue.

• Yahya ibn Talha narrated to me, he said: Shurayk narrated to us, from Ubayd al-Muktib, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection﴾ he said: love among the Muslims in this world.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Hakkam narrated to us, from Anbasa, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection﴾ he said: He loves them and makes them beloved to His creation.

• Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection﴾ he said: He loves them and makes them beloved to the believers.

• al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

• al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Hashim narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Hakam, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, he said: He loves them and makes them beloved.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: al-Hakam ibn Bashir narrated to us, he said: Amr narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection﴾ he said: No servant draws near to Allah except that Allah draws the hearts of the servants towards him, and increases him from His own.

• Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, His saying ﴿Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection﴾: Yes, by Allah, in the hearts of the people of faith. It was mentioned to us that Hurm ibn Hayyan used to say: No servant draws near to Allah with his heart except that Allah draws the hearts of the believers towards him, until He grants him their affection and mercy.

• Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, that Uthman ibn Affan used to say: There is no servant among the people who does good and does no evil, except that Allah clothes him in the cloak of his deed.

• al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from al-Thawri, from Muslim, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection﴾ he said: love. And it is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf.

• Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Sa'id al-Wasiti narrated to me, he said: Ya'qub ibn Muhammad informed us, he said: Abd al-Aziz ibn Imran narrated to us, from Abd Allah ibn Uthman ibn Abi Sulayman ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from his father, from his mother Umm Ibrahim, daughter of Abu Ubayda ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, from her father, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, that when he migrated to Medina, he felt grief at parting from his companions in Mecca, among them Shayba ibn Rabi'a, Utba ibn Rabi'a, and Umayya ibn Khalaf, so Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection﴾.

* *

And His saying ﴿So We have only made it easy in your tongue that you may give good tidings thereby to the righteous﴾

His saying, Exalted is His remembrance: So We have only made this Qur'an easy in your tongue, O Muhammad, that you recite it to give good tidings thereby to the righteous, who guard against the punishment of Allah by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions, with Paradise ﴿and warn thereby a people hostile [in opposition]﴾. He says: and to warn by this Qur'an of the punishment of Allah your people from Quraysh, for they are people of contention (luddun) and vain disputation, who do not accept the truth. And al-Lidd (luddun) is intense enmity.

And in accordance with what we have said on this, the people of interpretation have said.

Mention of those who said that:

• Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿luddan﴾ he said: they do not go straight.

• al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

• Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿and warn thereby a people hostile﴾ he said: that you warn by it people who are wrongdoers.

• Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, ﴿and warn thereby a people hostile﴾: i.e., contentious disputation in falsehood, possessors of enmity and dispute.

• al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿and warn thereby a people hostile﴾ he said: sinful transgressors.

• al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿a people hostile﴾ he said: contentious disputation in falsehood.

• Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and warn thereby a people hostile﴾: al-alladd is the wrongdoer, and he recited the saying of Allah ﴿and he is the most contentious of opponents﴾.

In the original: with an undotted dad, a misprint.]] narrated to us, he said: al-Ala' ibn Abd al-Jabbar narrated to us, he said: Mahdi Maymun narrated to us, from al-Hasan regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿and warn thereby a people hostile﴾ he said: deaf to the truth.

We have already explained the meaning of al-alladd with its evidences earlier, which suffices so that it need not be repeated in this place.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 96–97:

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection﴾ [Q. 19:96] ﴿So We have only made it easy in your tongue that you may give good tidings thereby to the righteous and warn thereby a people hostile [in opposition]﴾ [Q. 19:97].

His saying, Exalted is His remembrance: Indeed, those who believed in Allah and His messengers, and affirmed what came to them from their Lord, and acted upon it, so they made lawful what He made lawful and made unlawful what He made unlawful, ﴿the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection﴾ in this world, in the hearts of His believing servants.

And in accordance with what we have said on this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said that:

• Yahya ibn Talha narrated to me, he said: Shurayk narrated to us, from Muslim al-Mala'i, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection﴾ he said: love among the people in this world.

• Ali narrated to me, he said: Abd Allah narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection﴾ he said: love (hubban).

• Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection﴾ he said: affection from the Muslims in this world, good provision, and truthful tongue.

• Yahya ibn Talha narrated to me, he said: Shurayk narrated to us, from Ubayd al-Muktib, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection﴾ he said: love among the Muslims in this world.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Hakkam narrated to us, from Anbasa, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection﴾ he said: He loves them and makes them beloved to His creation.

• Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection﴾ he said: He loves them and makes them beloved to the believers.

• al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

• al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Hashim narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Hakam, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, he said: He loves them and makes them beloved.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: al-Hakam ibn Bashir narrated to us, he said: Amr narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection﴾ he said: No servant draws near to Allah except that Allah draws the hearts of the servants towards him, and increases him from His own.

• Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, His saying ﴿Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection﴾: Yes, by Allah, in the hearts of the people of faith. It was mentioned to us that Hurm ibn Hayyan used to say: No servant draws near to Allah with his heart except that Allah draws the hearts of the believers towards him, until He grants him their affection and mercy.

• Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, that Uthman ibn Affan used to say: There is no servant among the people who does good and does no evil, except that Allah clothes him in the cloak of his deed.

• al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from al-Thawri, from Muslim, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection﴾ he said: love. And it is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf.

• Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Sa'id al-Wasiti narrated to me, he said: Ya'qub ibn Muhammad informed us, he said: Abd al-Aziz ibn Imran narrated to us, from Abd Allah ibn Uthman ibn Abi Sulayman ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from his father, from his mother Umm Ibrahim, daughter of Abu Ubayda ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, from her father, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, that when he migrated to Medina, he felt grief at parting from his companions in Mecca, among them Shayba ibn Rabi'a, Utba ibn Rabi'a, and Umayya ibn Khalaf, so Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 98:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And how many generations have We destroyed before them? Do you perceive from them anyone, or hear from them a faint sound?﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And many were the people We destroyed, O Muhammad, before your people, of the polytheists of Quraysh, from a generation (qarn), meaning a group of people, when they followed the same path as them in opposing Me and committing acts of disobedience. Do you perceive from them anyone: that is, "Do you perceive any of them, O Muhammad, so that you see him and observe him?" ﴿Or hear from them a faint sound﴾, meaning:

Or hear from them any voice. Rather, they have perished and been destroyed, their homes have been emptied of them, their dwellings have become desolate, and they have gone to an abode in which nothing benefits them except a righteous deed they sent ahead. Likewise, these people of yours are headed toward what those others have come to, unless they seek to repent before destruction.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of interpretation) said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said this:

• ʿAlī narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiya narrated to us, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿or hear from them a faint sound﴾, he said: a sound.

• al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatāda, regarding His words ﴿Do you perceive from them anyone, or hear from them a faint sound﴾, he said: Do you see an eye, or hear a sound.

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatāda, regarding His words ﴿Do you perceive from them anyone, or hear from them a faint sound﴾, he says: Do you hear any sound from them, or see any eye.

• It was related to me from al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say, regarding His words ﴿or hear from them a faint sound﴾, meaning: a sound.

• Abū Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn ʿUyayna narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The rikz of people is their voices. Abū Kurayb said: Sufyān said regarding ﴿Do you perceive from them anyone, or hear from them a faint sound﴾: or hear from them a faint sound (ḥass). He said: al-rikz is al-ḥass.

Abū Jaʿfar (al-Ṭabarī) said: In the speech of the Arabs, al-rikz is a faint sound, as the poet said:

"So she sensed the mention of a companion, and it startled her, from a hidden place, while the companion was her sickness."

[The verse is from the Muʿallaqa of Labīd ibn Rabīʿa al-ʿĀmirī (Jamharat Ashʿār al-ʿArab, pp. 63–74; Sharḥ al-Zawzanī of the Seven Muʿallaqāt; Sharḥ al-Tibrīzī of the Ten Odes). The version in the Jamhara reads: "and she heard the rajz of the companion." He said: al-rikz is a faint sound. Allah the Exalted said: "or hear from them a faint sound." It is also narrated as rizz with doubling. Al-anīs means humankind. ʿAn ẓahr ghayb: meaning a hidden place. Al-ghayb is what is concealed from you, whether of land or knowledge. In al-Tibrīzī: "and she heard the rizz of the companion." He said: it is also narrated: "she sensed the rikz of the companion," meaning the cow heard the sound of people and was startled by it, and did not see the people. Al-razz and al-rikz are a faint sound. His words "ʿan ẓahr ghayb" mean: from behind a veil, i.e., she hears from where she does not see. "Al-anīs saqāmuhā": meaning the companion is her destruction, i.e., he hunts her; "rāʿahā" means frightened her; the subject of "tasammaʿat" is the pronoun of the cow, and the subject of "rāʾahā" is a pronoun referring to the rizz. In al-Zawzanī: "wa-tawajjasat rizz al-anīs," then he explained the verse in the same way as al-Tibrīzī's explanation.]

End of the commentary on Surah Maryam, and praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
